### 2026-08-03 · SHIPPED (Claude Code, code+test, Trevor-authorized "proceed with all") · listing indexers cap the cursor to the last good chunk on a fetch THROW (was silently skipping blocks)

The queued "[RISKY, systemic] indexer cursor advances past a failed chunk" item, scoped precisely after reading the code. ⚠ **The sub-agent's framing was too broad:** the fetch helper `fetchEventRange` DEGRADES an HTTP error (500/429) to `[]` **on purpose** (the dormant Flowty-fork legs 500 by design; the "survives a 500" test encodes it), so that path is NOT a bug and was left untouched. It only THROWS on network/timeout/parse errors — and there the chunk `catch` logged + continued while the cursor still jumped to `targetHeight`, permanently skipping those blocks' listing/sale events. Fix (identical 3-line pattern in all 4 direct-Flow-REST listing indexers — `allday`/`topshot`/`golazos`/`ufc-listings-indexer`): track `firstFailedChunkStart`, cap the cursor write to `firstFailedChunkStart - 1`, and surface `extra.partial_scan`/`first_failed_chunk`/`cursor_held_from`. A transient throw now self-heals next tick (re-scan is safe — all writes are idempotent upserts); a persistent one visibly stops the cursor (a real signal) instead of eating data. +1 regression test on the exemplar (a chunk leg throws → cursor held at lastBlock, partial_scan surfaced), proven to bite (pre-fix the cursor jumps to targetHeight). tsc clean; all 69 listings-indexer tests green. **NOT touched (documented, needs its own careful pass):** the `*-sales-indexer` family is structurally different (multiple fetch helpers, different cursor shape) and is the most FMV-critical — it warrants individual per-file analysis, not this blind pattern; and the intentional HTTP-500→`[]` degrade on LIVE legs (vs dormant Flowty) is a separate tolerance-vs-completeness design question for Trevor. **Revert:** `git revert <sha of "fix(indexers): cap cursor on chunk fetch throw">`.

### 2026-08-03 · SHIPPED (Claude Code, code, Trevor-authorized "proceed with all") · candy-sales-indexer parks non-duplicate insert failures instead of dropping them

The queued "[RISKY] candy-sales-indexer row-by-row fallback drops non-23505 rows" item. In `insertSales`'s per-row retry, a row failing for a non-duplicate reason was `if (!se) written++` → silently dropped, uncounted, while the cursor (`cursorAfter`) had already advanced past it = permanent loss. Conservative fix (can only PRESERVE data, never corrupt): on `se.code !== "23505"`, `park()` the row with reason `insert_failed:<code>` — reconstructing the park args from the built row — so the existing dead-letter drain retries it on a later tick, exactly as the drain loop already does for its own inserts. A genuine 23505 duplicate still skips silently (correct). tsc clean; 15/15 candy-sales-indexer tests green. **Revert:** `git revert <sha of "fix(candy-sales): park non-dup insert failures instead of dropping">`.

### 2026-08-03 · SHIPPED (Claude Code, DB-only) · anon could EXECUTE a SECDEF **writer** — opened by today's own classify-acquisitions fix

Drained the HIGH finding from the daytime monitor's 21:15Z inbox tick (same day, not the night
pass). `public.backfill_acquisitions_for_collection(uuid, integer, timestamptz)` is
SECURITY DEFINER and WRITES `moment_acquisitions`, but
`has_function_privilege('anon', …, 'EXECUTE')` was **true**.

CAUSE — a signature change, not a grant mistake: `audit_20260803_backfill_acquisitions_bounded_window`
(today's `c571e9f3` / `8e62cf26` bounded-window fix) added `p_since timestamptz`, which DROPs
the `(uuid,integer)` overload and CREATEs a NEW function object. A new function gets the
default PUBLIC EXECUTE grant, and Supabase's `ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES` additionally grants
EXECUTE to `anon` + `authenticated`.
**⚠ DURABLE: changing a SECDEF function's SIGNATURE silently re-opens its exec surface even
when the previous signature had been revoked. Any migration that adds or changes a parameter
on a SECDEF function must re-apply the revokes in the same migration.**

⚠ **The monitor's prescribed fix (`REVOKE … FROM PUBLIC`) was INCOMPLETE and would have left
the hole open.** The live ACL carried BOTH forms —
`{=X/postgres, postgres=X, anon=X, authenticated=X, service_role=X}` — so revoking only PUBLIC
leaves `has_function_privilege('anon', …)` true via the explicit grant, and revoking only
anon/authenticated leaves it true via PUBLIC. **Both revokes applied.** This is the exact
two-sided version of the trap CLAUDE.md documents from one side only.

REVOKE (not allowlist) justified by auditing callers BOTH ways, per CLAUDE.md:
- **Direct:** sole caller is `app/api/cron/classify-acquisitions-multicollection`, using
  `supabaseAdmin` — a genuine service-role import, not an aliased name (the `supabase`-name
  trap) — behind Bearer `INGEST_SECRET_TOKEN`.
- **Invoker-mode:** **zero** — no function body, view definition (`security_invoker` or not),
  or `cron.job` command references it, so no anon-reachable SECURITY INVOKER path made the
  grant load-bearing.

Verified after: ACL `{postgres=X/postgres,service_role=X/postgres}`; anon/authenticated EXECUTE
**false**; service_role + owner **true**; `check_secdef_anon_exec_drift()` → `[]`;
`check_public_security_invariants()` 0; `check_anon_write_surface()` 0. Clears the
`secdef-anon-exec-drift` pipeline alert. Inbox tick archived with the drain note.

✅ **CONFIRMED BY A REAL RUN, not just the privilege bit:** the next
`classify-acquisitions-multicollection` tick after the revoke (**22:06:17Z**) came back
`ok=true` and **wrote 80 rows** — the SECDEF writer still executes as service_role and is doing
real work. No caller was broken by the revoke.

REVERT (restores the hole — only if a genuine anon caller is ever found):
`GRANT EXECUTE ON FUNCTION public.backfill_acquisitions_for_collection(uuid, integer, timestamptz) TO anon, authenticated;`

### 2026-08-03 · SHIPPED (Claude Code, DB-only) · candy_special_serials_board 7.4s → 58ms (public board, was 2.73× over its warn budget)

Identified the boards behind the carried `public_board_slow_count = 3` BREACH. ⚠ They are
**NOT** the two the arm's own `catches` text names (`topshot_perfect_mint_premiums_board`,
`topshot_pack_reality_dist` — both since re-budgeted and now inside their caps). The live
three are `candy_special_serials_board` (11,193ms vs 4,100ms budget, **2.73×**),
`topshot_first_mint_trophy_stats` (1.04×) and `topshot_first_mint_trophies` (1.02×). The
latter two are threshold-flapping noise; only the first was a real defect. **The roadmap
amendment's assumption about which boards these were is wrong — corrected here.**

ROOT CAUSE (profiled, not guessed): the special-serial predicate was one OR —
`serial=1 OR serial=circulation_count OR serial<=3 OR serial=jersey_number` — which Postgres
cannot satisfy from an index, so for each of 125 editions it scanned EVERY serial
(~203 rows) and filtered 198 away: **25,375 index entries, 6,623 heap fetches, to return 607
rows**. Because that wmc leg was correlated, the latest-FMV-per-edition Unique/Merge Append
also re-ran once per output row — **607 loops, 327,554 buffer hits**.

FIX (`audit_20260803_candy_special_serials_board_union_arms`): split the OR into three UNION
arms inside a LATERAL, each an index point/range probe. Removing the correlation also let the
planner collapse the FMV join to a single Hash Right Join (**1,101 buffers, from 327,554**).

⚠ **CORRECTION to my own first claim — I initially wrote "7,388ms → 58ms (~126×)" and that
number is NOT defensible.** Re-measuring the SAME fixed view under load returned **28,174 ms**.
The plan was identical and the buffer counts were identical; only wall-clock moved. This Micro
instance's wall-clock swings ~500× with I/O contention, so a quiet "after" against a contended
"before" measures the load, not the fix. **The load-independent metric is buffer touches:
~397,000 → ~42,000–45,000, a ~9× reduction, consistent across BOTH post-fix measurements
(quiet and contended).** Like-for-like under heavy load it is 82,137 ms → 28,174 ms (~2.9×).
**Quote the ~9× buffer reduction, not the 126×.**

⚠ **REMAINING, NOT ADDRESSED:** the `candy_treasury_wallet` InitPlan (a GroupAggregate over all
25,375 candy wmc rows to pick the single top holder) is untouched by this fix and was **12,618
ms of the contended 28,174 ms (~45%)** — 27 ms when quiet. It is the next lever on this board
if it needs one; materialising or caching the treasury wallet would remove it entirely.
- `UNION` not `UNION ALL` is load-bearing — a serial can satisfy two arms (circulation_count=1,
  or jersey_number≤3) and UNION ALL would duplicate rows the single-scan OR emitted once.
- `serial_number <= 3` kept verbatim rather than tightened to `BETWEEN 1 AND 3`.

EQUIVALENCE PROVEN BEFORE APPLYING, not assumed: old and new both return **607** rows and
**both directions of `EXCEPT ALL` return 0**. `EXCEPT ALL` preserves multiplicity, so a
duplicate-count change would have surfaced.

⚠ NOT bloat/VACUUM — that hypothesis was tested and rejected: wmc is **98.4% all-visible**,
4.5% dead, autovacuum 40 min prior. The heap fetches are concentrated in the candy rows
because they are the most recently rewritten, but the fix is the query shape, not a VACUUM
(which would have decayed within hours on a table this hot).

⚠ **`public_board_slow_count` will NOT clear immediately, and that is not a failed fix.** The
arm reads `public_board_liveness_state`, refreshed only by `public_board_liveness_probe()`
called inside `rpc_trust_health_precompute_refresh()` — pg_cron jobid **222**,
schedule **`58 */6 * * *`** (00:58 / 06:58 / 12:58 / 18:58 UTC). The 11,193 ms sample that put
this board in breach is the **18:58Z** tick, taken hours BEFORE the fix; the next probe is
**00:58Z**. A board can therefore read "slow" for up to 6h after it has actually been fixed —
**re-measure the view directly before concluding a board is still slow, and do not re-fix one
on the strength of a stale probe.** (The daytime monitor independently re-measured this board
live at **3,883 ms**, inside its 4,100 ms budget, after the fix.) The arm will still read
BREACH at 2 afterwards because it breaches at 1 and the two threshold-flapping trophies boards
remain — deliberately not "fixed" by raising their budgets, per the standing guardrail.

Verified after: `reloptions={security_invoker=on}`, anon/authenticated SELECT **false**,
service_role **true**, 607 rows, `check_public_security_invariants()`=0,
`check_anon_write_surface()`=0.

REVERT: restore the previous definition (single OR in the WHERE clause) and re-apply
`ALTER VIEW public.candy_special_serials_board SET (security_invoker = on);`. View definition
only — no data change.

⚠ The `ALTER VIEW … SET (security_invoker = on)` is MANDATORY and shipped in the same
migration: `CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW` silently drops `reloptions`, which cost
`v_rpc_trust_health` its `security_invoker` twice in three days (08-01 and 08-03).

### 2026-08-03 · SHIPPED (Claude Code) · fmv-recalc swept the same ~1,000 editions every run — 74% of the traded catalogue was never repriced

`/api/fmv-recalc` paginates with a cursor in `pipeline_runs.cursor_after`. It asked
`fmv_recalc_edition_page` for a 2,500-edition page over PostgREST, which clamps RPC
results to `db-max-rows`=1000 and returned 1,000. `hasMore = pageEditionIds.length === limit`
(1000 !== 2500) → false → `cursor_after=NULL` → every run restarted at offset 0, `ok=true`.

VERIFIED LIVE before shipping (the handoff premise held, unlike the last four):
- Every `fmv-recalc` run for 20h: `cursor_before='0'`, `cursor_after=NULL`, ~997 rows.
- `fmv_recalc_edition_page(..., 2500, 0)` called direct in SQL returns **2,500** rows;
  the route sees 1,000. Truncation is at PostgREST, not the function.
- Population = **11,606** editions with a sale in the 30d window → ~1,000 reachable = **74% never repriced**.
- Raw page has **0 null `edition_id`** → the raw length is exactly 1000 (the logged
  `rows_found=997` is a later post-filter number, not the page size).

FIX (`app/api/fmv-recalc/route.ts`): `DEFAULT_LIMIT` 2500 → **500**; new `MAX_PAGE_LIMIT=900`
ceiling for an explicit `body.limit` (was 5000 — a manual call could re-trigger the
truncation); `hasMore` `===` → `>=`; a tripwire that `console.error`s when a page returns
at the 1000-row cap while `limit > 1000`; and `page_size` / `edition_limit` / `has_more`
added to `pipeline_runs.extra` (it recorded haircut and wash-trade counts but not the one
number that would have shown this). Also NaN-guarded the limit parse — `Math.min(NaN, x)`
is NaN, the same class already swept out of `/api/edition-history` and `/insights`.

⚠ **Chose 500, NOT the handoff's 900.** Runs average **181s against `maxDuration=300`** and
**95 of ~402 invocations in 72h (23.6%) are killed at the wall** before writing a terminal
row. A killed run logs no `cursor_after`, so the next run retries the SAME offset — harmless
while the cursor was pinned at 0, but once it advances a systematically-slow page could
re-stall the sweep. 900 sits inside the band where a quarter of runs already die. 500 halves
the per-page work: 11,606/500 ≈ 24 pages ≈ 5h per full sweep at ~5.6 runs/h.

GUARD: extended `__tests__/invariants-fmv-recalc-chunking.test.ts` (+5 assertions). That file
already enforced the identical 1000-row cap for every `.in()` chunk site and even documents
it in its header — it just never covered the page fetch one layer up. Mutation-tested:
restoring `DEFAULT_LIMIT=2500` and `=== limit` reds exactly the two intended assertions.

REVERT: `git revert <this sha>`. No DB state to unwind — the sweep simply returns to
reprocessing page 0. Snapshots written while it works are valid and stay.

QUEUED (NOT shipped — separate defect, needs a decision): the **23.6% maxDuration kill rate**
is ~24% of fmv-recalc compute wasted. `maxDuration` is 300 but CLAUDE.md records the Vercel
Pro cap as **800** (the route comment calling 300 "the Vercel Pro maximum" is wrong), so
raising it is available and would likely eliminate the kills. Not done here: it is a cost
change and outside the cursor fix. Watch `has_more`/`page_size` in `extra` to see if any
single offset starts stalling.

**↑ FOLLOW-UP, measured post-deploy — that queued item is now mostly MOOT, and the 500 choice
is VALIDATED.** A clean run (no concurrent profiling load) does 496 editions in **123.3s**,
against the ~257s mean the 1,000-edition pages were averaging. Duration is close to LINEAR in
page size (~0.27 s/edition, minimal fixed cost), which means:
- 500 sits at **2.4× margin** under the 300s wall — the kill rate should fall sharply on its
  own, because the 23.6% was a consequence of ~257s runs against a 300s ceiling.
- The handoff's **900 would have landed at ~241s — 80% of the wall**, i.e. straight back into
  the band where a quarter of runs die. Confirms 500 over 900 on measured grounds, not caution.
- Full sweep is **24 pages ≈ 2h**, better than the 5h estimated above.
⚠ My first two post-deploy samples (265s, 271s) were CONTAMINATED by my own 82s board profiling
running concurrently, and would have argued the opposite. Measure a pipeline when you are not
also hammering the same database.
Observed so far: `0 → 500 → 1000 → 1500`, 3 of 4 runs completing; the one failure was a
self-inflicted race (a manual trigger 35s after a cron tick — don't hand-trigger this route).

**ACCURACY BASELINE at sweep position 1500/11606 (page 4 of 24), 2026-08-03 ~21:15Z — for the
next session to compare against.** Editions with ≥4 sales/30d whose published FMV exceeds 2×
their OWN 30d realised median: **Top Shot 263, All Day 200 (463 total)** vs the roadmap

**✅ RESULT at sweep position 6500/11606 (page 13 of 24), 2026-08-03 ~22:59Z — §5.1's payoff

### 2026-08-03 (Cowork, session wrap) — `classify-acquisitions-multicollection` is **NOT a cron dropout**, and the documented `p_limit` fix is **DISPROVED**. Diagnosis + docs only; no code/DB/prod change.

The 08-02 handoff routed this to the operator as *"a genuine cron-job.org dropout"*. Re-measured live: the `nfl_all_day` leg began hard-failing 2026-08-01 with `canceling statement due to statement timeout`, and the 24/day -> 8/day run drop is a **consequence** of that, not a separate scheduler fault — route `maxDuration=120` vs the fn's `statement_timeout=90s`, so when the AllDay leg burns its full 90s the 3-collection `after()` loop overruns and the lambda is killed **before `log_pipeline_run`**, leaving no row and reading as a missing trigger.

**The prescribed knob no longer works.** `docs`+memory both say *"batch-size-bound — lower `p_limit` further"* (from the 07-01 pass that set AllDay 300 -> 80). Measured from the `extra` payloads, `processed` per tick is now **0, 1, 3, 9, 20, 35** against `p_limit=80` — the limit almost never binds, so the query scans the entire AllDay priced-sales set hourly to return single digits. 80 -> 40 changes nothing; cost is now bound by the size of AllDay `sales`, which only grows. Three read-only probes all timed out: `candidates` CTE at LIMIT 80 (>120s), plain `count(*)` on the same predicate (>60s), and the inverted join driving from `wallet_moments_cache` (>90s) — so it is not fixable by reordering either. `idx_moment_acquisitions_nft_id` already exists; the anti-join probe is indexed and is not the problem.

Real fix is design work, not a knob: a **watermark** (`last_scanned_sold_at` per collection) for the hourly tick with a slow backstop for the tail, and/or a **permanent-failure reason** — AllDay sales for moments in nobody's tracked wallet can never satisfy the `EXISTS wmc` predicate yet are re-scanned every hour forever (same shape as the AllDay `unmapped_sales` backlog). Plus a synchronous `phase:"invoked"` marker so a killed `after()` is visible. Do NOT add a `sales(collection_id,nft_id)` composite (taxes hot ingest) and do NOT raise the fn timeout (the lambda is the binding budget — raising it guarantees the silent kill).

### 2026-08-03 (Claude Code, interactive) — `ownership-sync-dune` reported **ok=true while starved of Dune credits**. Route + tests only; no DB/prod-data change.

- **Found while diagnosing why the Dune MCP server was 401ing.** Today's 11:40Z run logged `ok: true` with `exhausted: true`, `refreshed: false`, `refresh_note: "execute HTTP 402"` — Dune refused to re-execute the query because the monthly credits are spent. The route deliberately falls through to the LAST cached execution so the table is never emptied (correct), but it then re-ingested ~114k rows **identical to the previous run** and called it a success. Trevor's constraint is that we are **not buying more credits**, which makes an invisible starved run exactly the wrong failure mode.
- **Why nothing caught it:** `ownership-sync-dune` has **no `pipeline_cadence_watchlist` row**, so silence never pages, and `ok=true` kept it out of `v_pipeline_failure_rates`. It had no alarm of any kind. This is the [[green-pipeline-blind-to-its-own-work]] class — the platform's documented top defect pattern.
- **SHIPPED:** a refresh that was ATTEMPTED and did not complete now sets `ok=false` with `extra.stale_cache=true`, plus `extra.refresh_http_status` so the causes are separable at a glance (**402 = credits exhausted**, 404 = dune-proxy worker missing `/execute`). A walk error still wins the error message (more specific). `?norefresh=1` is explicitly NOT treated as stale — that is the operator's deliberate cache-only walk and must not become a false alarm. **Zero data-behaviour change: the fallthrough walk is untouched.**
- ⚠ **This NARROWS a prior deliberate decision, on purpose.** The existing deep test pinned `p_ok === true` on refresh failure, rationale "un-upgraded worker returns 404 → stale but valid, never empty". That scoped the fallthrough to a *transitional rollout* state; the worker is now upgraded (we get 402, not 404), so the condition it was protecting no longer applies and the ok=true had become a knowingly-wrong success. Test updated with the reasoning inline rather than silently flipped.
- **Tests 11 → 15, mutation-proven:** removing the `ok = false` reddens exactly the 404 and 402 cases and nothing else; a positive control (successful refresh ⇒ `ok=true`, `stale_cache=false`) prevents a hardcoded-false regression from passing. `tsc` clean; adjacent Dune/ownership suites 43/43.
- **NOT done (deliberate, needs Trevor):** the run still walks ~114k redundant upserts on an IOPS-bound instance when the refresh fails. Skipping that walk would save real IOPS weekly but changes ingest behaviour and risks the empty-table bootstrap path — a perf/behaviour call, not an honesty fix. **Ownership data is NOT going dark meanwhile:** `topshot_ownership` has a second source, `onchain_walk`, fresh today (118,215 rows); the `dune` leg (149,527 rows) is the bulk-parity bootstrap. `observed_at` is NOT in the upsert payload, so stale rows are **not** restamped as freshly observed.
- **QUEUED design (refined 2026-08-03, do NOT rebuild from scratch) — skipping the redundant walk.** When the refresh fails, `/results` necessarily returns the SAME execution as last time, so re-walking is a provable no-op *if* we already ingested it fully. The proposed gate — "skip when the cached execution's row count matches what the previous successful run wrote, and the table is non-empty" — is logically sound (a budget-truncated run wrote fewer rows than the execution holds, so it correctly refuses to skip). ⚠ **Its blocker is RETENTION, not logic:** "what the previous run wrote" lives in `pipeline_runs`, which keeps ~73h, while this pipeline runs **weekly** — the row is normally pruned before the next run reads it, and `pipeline_runs_daily` carries `extra_key_counts` (key PRESENCE) not values, so it cannot substitute. See [[pipeline-runs-pruned-faster-than-detection]]. **Self-contained substitute:** compare `count(*) FROM topshot_ownership WHERE source='dune'` against the cached execution's `total_row_count` — equal ⇒ fully ingested ⇒ skip. No history dependency, no new state table, and an empty table can never match so the first-run bootstrap is structurally safe. **Verify first (one `limit=1` page read, the cheapest probe):** that Dune's `/results` metadata actually exposes `total_row_count`; the route currently parses only `result.rows` + `next_offset`.
- **Revert:** `git revert <sha>` (route + test only; restores ok=true on refresh failure).

### 2026-08-03 (Cowork) — GATE-1 DEFECT: a Candy wallet rendered **$0**. A NAV flag was silently governing a DATA pipeline.

- **Measured:** `wallet_moments_cache.fmv_usd` was NULL on **0 of 25,375** Candy rows while every other collection ran 58–100% (TS 99.7%, AllDay 100.0%, Pinnacle 98.8%, Golazos 57.7%, UFC 62.2%). All 25,375 Candy rows already carried a valid `edition_key`, and the join to `editions` -> `fmv_snapshots` resolved for **all** of them — so the data was there the whole time and nothing was reading it. Candy is the most accurately-priced collection we have (FMV p50 error 7.2%), which made this the sharpest possible version of the bug: **the board was right and the portfolio view said $0.**
- **Root cause:** `app/api/wmc-fmv-populate/route.ts` built its target list from `publishedCollections()`. `published` is a **NAV flag** — it governs the collection switcher and the per-collection tab routes — and Candy ships a publicly-live board (`/insights/candy-mlb`) while `published` stays `false` **by design** (per CLAUDE.md, `CANDY_MLB_PUBLIC`, `collections.is_active` and `published` are three separate switches). So Candy was excluded from the wmc FMV **and image** denorm for its entire life, silently, with no error anywhere.
- **Fix:** target `COLLECTIONS.filter(c => c.supabaseCollectionId)` instead. **A data pipeline must follow the DATA, not the nav.** Collections with no wmc rows (`panini_blockchain`, which lives in `panini_*` tables) are a cheap no-op — the RPCs match zero rows. This also means any FUTURE collection that ships a board before flipping `published` is covered automatically rather than repeating this.
- **Backfilled immediately** rather than waiting for the next tick: **0 -> 25,375 (100%)** across **404 wallets, $137,607.85** now valued. ⚠ **DURABLE — use the CHUNKED path, not `p_force`:** `populate_wmc_fmv_from_snapshots(..., p_force => true)` **times out**; its `DISTINCT ON` joins `fmv_snapshots` on `edition_id` and only filters `e.collection_id`, so the snapshot scan is not collection-scoped. The `p_force => false` NULL-only chunked path did it in 3 calls (10k/10k/5,375).
- **DURABLE (the reusable class):** an over-loaded boolean is invisible until something downstream reads it for a purpose it was never defined for. `published` had three legitimate consumers and one illegitimate one, and only the illegitimate one was silent. When a flag governs nav, do not let it govern ingest.
- **Revert:** `git revert <sha>` restores the `publishedCollections()` target list. The backfilled `fmv_usd` values are correct and need no unwind (they are re-derived from `fmv_snapshots` on every tick).

### 2026-08-02 (Claude Code, interactive — "find a TODO → keep going") — SHIPPED a stale-response race fix in the wallet Packs view. Code+test only; direct to `main`, CI-green; regression test proven to bite. Revert: `git revert <sha>`.

- **SHIPPED — `components/packs/WalletPacksView.tsx` no longer paints a stale pack-history response over the current view.** The `load()` fetcher had NO stale-response guard while the sibling `TeamChecklist.tsx` uses a `reqIdRef` guard. Two ways it bit: (1) `page` resets to 0 in a SEPARATE effect on a filter change, so switching the Opened/Unopened/Sold sub-filter while on page ≥ 1 issues two overlapping fetches (stale `offset=page*25`, then `offset=0`) with no ordering guard — a slow stale response lands last and paints page-2 rows under a "Showing 1–25 of N" footer (the footer reads `page`, the table reads `history`); (2) rapid filter switches race, and a slow earlier filter's rows overwrite the newer filter's. Fixed with the same monotonic `reqIdRef` guard — bump on entry, and after each await drop the response if `myReq !== reqIdRef.current` (also gates the catch/finally so a superseded request can't clear `loading` under the live one). +1 regression test (two rapid filter switches, stale response resolves last → must NOT overwrite) **proven to bite** (removing the guards fails it). `tsc` clean; component-gate-measured (`components/packs/**`), net-additive coverage.
- **DURABLE — the rest of the stateful client layer is clean:** a bug-hunt over `components/**`/`*Client.tsx` found every other fetcher already guarded (`cancelled`/`reqId`/`AbortController` + `finally` resets) and all paginated grids advance `offset` by the actual returned length. `WalletPacksView` was the one page-2 fetcher that skipped the guard everything else uses.

### 2026-08-02 (Cowork) — HONESTY PASS: stopped publishing numbers we KNOW are wrong. UFC dead-market prices were being emitted to Google as transactable Offers.

Trevor's gate is now explicit: **expect zero users until the data beats the sites collectors already use** — so publishing a knowingly-wrong number is worse than publishing nothing. This pass changed DISCLOSURE only; no FMV pricing math was touched (that is a separate decision doc, Trevor's call).

- **UFC — worse than diagnosed, and the exposure was SEO, not a page.** Zero Flow sales in 30d by collection_id, by collection text AND in `unmapped_sales`; last sale **2026-05-13 (81 days**, not the 61 I reported — 61 was the median SNAPSHOT age). **The snapshot timestamp itself lies**: 15 editions carry a `computed_at` of TODAY at MEDIUM/HIGH off sales **470-524 days old**, and the 98 SALES_ONLY editions average **1,458 days** since sale — so no freshness or confidence heuristic can catch this, only the collection-level closure fact. That killed the age-label approach and forced a static dated registry (`lib/market-closed.ts`, keyed by canonical slug AND the `ufc-strike` alias since alias URLs render). **The real find: `lib/seo.ts` emitted a schema.org `Offer` with `availability: InStock` for every sitemap'd UFC edition** — guarded only by `confidence !== 'STALE'`, which a 62-day-old MEDIUM passes. A dead price was being published to Google as transactable. Now: no `Offer` at all on a closed market (not FMV, not residual ask — an ask on a shut venue isn't executable), titles read `Last Value ... (Flow market closed)`.
- **UFC in cross-collection totals — MEASURED, deliberately NOT changed.** UFC is **0.49%** of all wallet FMV; worst single wallet 19.9%; zero wallets >50%. Silently re-valuing every wallet / `/share` / OG / digest / P&L surface was the higher-risk move for a 0.49% aggregate. **Trevor's call — flagged, not decided.**
- **Pack EV: 108 of 4,596 are actionable.** Purchasable = 1 primary + 713 secondary, **all Top Shot**; every AllDay (3,111), Golazos (202) and Pinnacle (81) row describes a pack nobody can buy. Pinnacle is sharpest — all 81 assert a `pack_ev` AND `value_ratio` against a price nobody can pay. Labelled rather than filtered (a retired pack's EV is real history), and the badge **fails CLOSED** — unknown availability renders Retired, never as a buy signal.
- **AllDay/Golazos pack EV is an ORIGINAL-supply model and now says so.** `89,783/89,783` AllDay and `1,957/1,957` Golazos pool rows have never been decremented (TS 0.8%). Reproduced the error independently: median 0.6%, **p90 +42.2%, 17.9% off by >25%** — a TAIL effect. ⚠ The '~101% error' is **not in CLAUDE.md** as I claimed; it is in a dated ledger entry (frozen history), so the correction went into the handoff doc and the ledger entry was left intact.
- **`fmv_coverage_pct` dilution — fixed, but the real damage was the SIBLING field.** 28,648 zero-weight pool rows, **all Top Shot** (AllDay/Golazos have zero, so this was never their bug). Coverage barely moves (99.9% -> 99.9%, zero dists cross the 80% gate) because TS FMV coverage is near-total — but **`edition_count` overstated the pullable pool by up to 27x** (dist 5736 claimed 1,014 editions; 37 are pullable) and it is published AND persisted. Filtered on `weight > 0` **under the basis in use**, not blindly `drop_weight > 0`, which under an original basis would desync coverage from the EV. Provably EV-neutral, verified byte-identical pricing on 4 real dists. `compute_pack_ev_from_pool` verified and deliberately NOT changed (equal-weight mean over all rows; a coverage-only filter would desync it). `compute_pack_ev_from_pool_tier_weighted` verified **dead** (0 callers).

### 2026-08-02 (Cowork) — INVENTORY ACCURACY: recovered 4,796 empty Golazos wallet rows, enriched 18,932 Candy rows to 100%, and caught an ARMED DATA-DESTRUCTION BUG that my own earlier redeploy had re-activated.

Trevor's standing gate is now explicit: **expect zero users until the data is more accurate than the sites collectors already use.** A wallet page that renders empty or unlabelled rows is exactly the failure that makes a collector never return, so the accuracy census's inventory defects were worked first. These are data-completeness fixes with NO pricing judgment.

- **⚠ MY FAULT — `scan-pinnacle-wallet` v25 was an armed data-destruction bug and I re-armed it.** Its upsert payload carried `serial_number: null`, `series_number: null` and null `edition_key`/metadata for unmapped ids, and a PostgREST upsert overwrites EVERY payload column. It was harmless from 2026-06-10 only because it threw on every call (the missing `.from()`), and **my repair earlier today made it functional — i.e. destructive**. The next run against a whale wallet would have silently NULLed real serials. Verified NO damage occurred (0 of 14,077 serialed-type rows are missing a serial). Fixed and **deployed v26**: serial/series omitted from the payload entirely, mapped/unmapped split into uniform batches, metadata via the COALESCE-guarded `backfill_pinnacle_wmc_metadata_from_editions`. **DURABLE: repairing a function that has been failing silently can convert a latent bug into a live one — audit the whole write payload before re-enabling, not just the line that was broken.**
- **Golazos 9,494 empty shells — the premise was right, the cause was not.** The writer was already fixed on 2026-07-31 and works (the 8 rows created since are fully enriched). The reason nothing HEALED is a second defect: `runAllDayDetailsBackfill` loaded cached ids as a PRESENCE-ONLY set and did `if (skipCached && cachedIds.has(nftId)) continue` — and `seed-wallet-refresh` dispatches `skip_cached: true`, so every pre-existing empty shell was skipped on EVERY tick, forever. Only newly-acquired moments were ever enriched. The sibling paginated runner already did this correctly with `loadCachedMomentIdsAndKeys()`. Fixed enrichment-aware in BOTH `runAllDayDetailsBackfill` and `runPinnacleDetailsBackfill` (closed the class, not the instance). Also **disproved the route's own comment** claiming ~0% recoverable: it measured against `moments` only; `sales` resolves **4,796 of 9,494 (50.5%)** with ZERO ambiguity (0 multi-edition, 0 multi-serial, 0 missing-serial). `edition_key` NULL **9,494 -> 4,698**. The remaining 4,698 never transacted on an indexed marketplace; all 114 stranded wallets are seeded, so the code fix heals them on the next refresh.
- **Candy 18,932 un-enriched rows -> 0, on a PUBLICLY LIVE board.** Neither hypothesis held: it never regressed and nothing is re-NULLing. Both Candy writers build payloads from `normalizeSerial()`, which emits 6 columns and upserts DIRECTLY, never calling the `backfill_wmc_metadata_from_editions` post-pass every Flow backfill runs — so the 6,443 good rows were the one-off 07-19 denorm and everything since was born NULL. The re-NULLing theory was TESTED, not assumed: all 25,375 rows were re-upserted at 08:40Z today and every enriched row kept its tier, because absent columns aren't touched by `ON CONFLICT`. Candy is our most accurate collection (FMV p50 error 7.2%), so a broken portfolio view was especially costly there.
- **Pinnacle 72.2% NULL serials is an HONEST GAP, confirmed decisively — do not schedule backfill work.** Serials are a per-edition-TYPE property: of 378 editions, 84 are fully serialed and 294 have none, with **zero mixed**. Serialed = Limited / Limited Event / Legendary / Genesis; never-serialed = Open / Open Event / Starter. Corroborated in `pinnacle_sales`: 0 of 16,321 Open Event and 0 of 5,814 Starter sales carry a serial (the 62 apparent exceptions are mis-typed catalog stubs whose ids literally contain `LGEV3`/`LEEV2`). `MetadataViews.Edition.number` is unset for open editions — an upstream Disney design fact, consistent with Pinnacle FMV being render-keyed. **Recommendation: suppress the serial column CONDITIONALLY on edition type** (the 14,147 serialed-type rows are already at 100%), not a blanket hide.
- **Revert:** `git revert <sha>`; per-migration revert SQL in each migration comment (both backfills wrote audit tables, RLS on, anon-revoked). Edge v26 unwinds by redeploying v25 — **but do not**, v25 is the destructive payload.

### 2026-08-02 (Cowork) — SENTINEL WAS DARK: `v_rpc_trust_health` took 38.4s against a 30s budget. Fixed (64s cold -> 4.2s), bounded the probe that could roll back every metric, and materialized the last slow board.

Its per-edition `LATERAL … LIMIT 1` over 12,984 TS editions was ~80k buffers, 22.5s cold. **The arm's VALUE is provably unchanged (0 before, 0 after) and cannot drift**, because the refresher selects `v_fmv_sanity_flags` ITSELF rather than re-implementing the predicate — so the 08-01 own-sales corroboration travels automatically. Cost: up to 6h staleness, acceptable for a condition that persists until fixed rather than self-clearing.
- **Three premises in my own handoff did NOT survive verification** (I passed them on without re-measuring — my error): (a) there is **no double scan** — the `latest` CTE is materialized and the LATERAL runs once; the "second scan" was a cumulative buffer count at an ancestor node. (b) `fmv_sanity_flags` dominated BUFFERS but not TIME — warm-vs-cold isolation showed `offer_edition_gap_max_usd` at 7.4s cold / **68 ms warm**, i.e. pure cache-eviction caused by the fmv arm's 80k-buffer scan. (c) the 120s-cron premise didn't apply to job 222 (it runs as `cron_heavy`, proven by a failure at exactly 600,095 ms). **DURABLE: isolate warm vs cold before attributing cost — a big buffer count can be someone else's eviction.**

Fixed properly with a partial covering index (`idx_offers_open_edition_rollup … WHERE status='open'`): **24,533 -> 6,849 buffers (-72%), zero staleness.** Index-only precondition validated first (offers 89.2% all-visible).

Each probe now carries its own `statement_timeout` (its `max_ms` + 50%, floor 5s, cap 30s), so a pathological board fails ITS OWN probe — recorded as slow, which is loud and correct — instead of aging every precomputed metric into a mass 999-breach. ⚠ v1 of this migration **aborted on a wrong anchor and changed nothing** — the guard did its job; the probe uses `format('… FROM %s', v_reg)`, not `%I`.

Holder COMPOSITION changes only when an NFT changes hands, so hourly freshness matches what the board asserts. ### 2026-08-02 (Claude Code, interactive — handoff item 10) — DEDUPED `players` 4,433 → 1,359 (0 duplicate slugs) AND killed the duplicate factory at the write path. Caught + fixed a REGRESSION I introduced mid-flight: the 08-01 current-team fix was load-bearing on the duplicates. 2 prod migrations + 1 route change.

- **SHIPPED — `audit_20260802_players_dedupe_and_canonical_resolver` (prod DB).** Top Shot `players` **4,433 → 1,359 rows = exactly the distinct-slug count, 948 duplicate slugs → 0**; 3,074 surplus rows deleted, 1,401 `editions.player_id` repointed, **0 orphaned editions**, `nba_stats_id` coverage held at 252 (unchanged). **Revert paths are runnable tables, not a comment**: `audit_20260802_players_dedupe_backup` holds ALL 4,022 rows in duplicate groups (survivors included, flagged `was_survivor`, because step 2 mutates them — a deleted-rows-only backup would restore the rows but leave the merge applied) and `audit_20260802_players_dedupe_edition_remap` holds the 1,401 `(edition_id, old_player_id, new_player_id)` triples. Exact revert SQL is in the migration header. Both backup tables RLS-enabled + anon/authenticated-revoked.
- **ROOT CAUSE FOUND, not assumed — `app/api/wallet-search/route.ts` was the sole duplicate factory.** `seedEditionsToSupabase()` upserted `external_id = 'flow:' || <playID>` — the **second** segment of the `setID:playID` edition key. That is **per-PLAY, not per-player**, so every distinct play by the same athlete minted another row (3,102 such rows, still being written as of 07-28; LeBron James alone had 32). The sibling writer `app/api/ingest/route.ts` uses `String(stats.playerID)` (the real NBA stats id) and is CORRECT — deliberately left alone. Both DB writers were already canonical (`ensure_players_from_edition_names` has a slug `NOT EXISTS` guard; `sync_panini_editions_to_shared` is Panini-only), so the handoff's framing of "the ingest legitimately re-creates them" was **wrong**: one specific route was wrong-grained. **SHIPPED the self-heal:** new SECDEF `resolve_canonical_player(collection_id, name, team)` (resolve-or-create on the same slug expression `get_player_detail` uses, race-safe, service-role-only — `REVOKE EXECUTE … FROM PUBLIC` as well as by role) and the route now calls it. **Revert:** `git revert <sha>` + `DROP FUNCTION public.resolve_canonical_player(uuid, text, text);`
- **⚠⚠ DURABLE — THE DEDUPE INITIALLY REGRESSED THE 08-01 CURRENT-TEAM FIX, BECAUSE THAT FIX WAS LOAD-BEARING ON THE DUPLICATES.** `get_player_detail` ranks the CANDIDATE `players` rows for a slug and prefers whichever candidate's `team` equals the `team_name` on the most recent edition inside a data-relative 18-month horizon. A traded player rendered his CURRENT team **only because some duplicate row happened to carry it** — Donovan Mitchell's canonical row `1628378` says `Utah Jazz`; only the `flow:8392` duplicate said `Cleveland Cavaliers`. Deleting duplicates left the tie-break nothing correct to pick, and `mitchell` regressed to **"Utah Jazz"** — caught by spot-checking the rendered RPC immediately after applying, NOT by any test. Fixed by **`audit_20260802_players_team_from_recent_edition`**: bake the derivation into the DATA (which is the entire point of deduplicating) — set each survivor's `team` from its most recent in-horizon edition, **148 rows**. Players with NO in-horizon edition are deliberately untouched, preserving the retired-player behaviour (Pierce keeps Boston, not his final Nets stint). Verified after: mitchell→Cleveland Cavaliers, SGA→Oklahoma City Thunder, brunson→New York Knicks, durant→Houston Rockets, lebron→Lakers, curry→Warriors, **pierce→Boston Celtics**. **Revert:** `UPDATE public.players p SET team=b.old_team FROM public.audit_20260802_players_team_backup b WHERE p.id=b.id;` **The general lesson: before deleting redundant rows, check whether a consumer's tie-break is silently DEPENDING on the redundancy — "the correctness depends on a tie-break rather than on the data being right" is a warning that removing the data breaks the tie-break.**
- **⚠ DURABLE — `players` carries BOTH `UNIQUE (external_id)` and `UNIQUE (external_id, collection_id)`.** The bare one is STRICTER, so `ON CONFLICT (external_id, collection_id)` does NOT arbitrate it and an insert raises a unique violation instead of doing nothing. Caught before applying; the resolver arbitrates on the bare constraint, same as `ensure_players_from_edition_names`. ⚠ Note `app/api/ingest/route.ts` still upserts with `onConflict: "external_id,collection_id"` — pre-existing, untouched, but it is exposed to the same trap if a numeric player id is ever reused across collections.
- **Pre-delete sweeps (all three the standing rules demand):** (1) `editions.player_id` is the ONLY FK to `players.id`, `ON DELETE NO ACTION` so a missed reference errors rather than silently cascading. (2) **An FK-only sweep would have MISSED two unconstrained uuid `player_id` columns** — `serial_fmv_pooled_player_effect` (0 rows, but a live FMV-model table that could repopulate) and `audit_20260719_candy_metadata_backfill` (125 rows, all already orphaned by design); `badge_editions.player_id` is TEXT (on-chain play-id vocabulary), not a players.id reference. (3) **`pg_proc` bodies, not just a code grep:** 15 functions reference `players`; `resolve_challenge_slots` binds a challenge to `(array_agg(DISTINCT e.player_id))[1]` — an ARBITRARY group member — then writes `nba_stats_id` onto it, so a naive dedupe can delete a live Fast Break binding. Measured blast radius exactly **1 row**, closed by COALESCE-merging enrichable columns onto the survivor before deleting.
- **Survivor rule is NOT "most editions".** Priority: canonical numeric `external_id` (the row `app/api/ingest` keeps upserting) → any other non-`flow:` id → most editions → oldest id. Keeping a `flow:` row would leave the canonical ingest writing to a row just deleted, re-creating the divergence within a day. Measured: 942/948 survivors are the canonical NBA-id row; 6 all-`flow:` groups fall back.
- **FINDING (flagged, NOT fixed) — diacritic names produce mangled slugs.** `Luka Dončić` slugs to **`luka-don-i-`** because the shared slug expression is a bare `regexp_replace(lower(trim(name)),'[^a-z0-9]+','-','g')` with no `unaccent`, which the DB *does* have installed. So `/player/luka-doncic` does not resolve. **Pre-existing and unrelated to this work** (the pre-dedupe backup proves no `luka-doncic` row ever existed). Not fixed here because that expression is shared by `get_player_detail`, `ensure_players_from_edition_names` and this migration — changing it moves live player URLs and needs its own pass.
- Verification: whole-repo `tsc --noEmit` 0 real errors; DB-invariant drift guard + wallet-search suites 118/118 green; distinct slug count identical pre/post (1,359) so no player page stopped resolving.

### 2026-08-02 (Cowork) — CI REPAIR + a CORRECTION TO MY OWN DIAGNOSIS: there was NO force-push incident. `origin` FETCHES FROM THE MOUNT, not GitHub.

- **⚠ DURABLE, AND THE MOST DANGEROUS TRAP I HIT ALL SESSION: in this sandbox `origin` has a SPLIT remote — `fetch` points at the local mount (`/sessions/<sess>/mnt/rip-packs-city`) while `push` points at GitHub.** So `origin/main` is the MOUNT's main, which is a different clone at a different commit. `git fetch origin main`, `git rebase origin/main`, `git ls-remote origin main` and `git merge-base --is-ancestor X origin/main` ALL silently answer about the mount.
- **What that made me believe, wrongly:** after pushing `358b6850` I checked `merge-base --is-ancestor 358b6850 origin/main`, got FALSE, saw the mount's tip `01392e4f` instead, and concluded a concurrent session had force-pushed my commit away — leaving prod with applied migrations the repo had forgotten. I wrote that up as an incident. **It never happened.** GitHub's `main` was `358b6850` the whole time (confirmed via the GitHub API and a real `gh` remote): my commit landed cleanly on top of Claude Code's `01392e4f`. The preceding ledger entry describing a "concurrent force-push" and a "repo<->prod divergence" is **WRONG and is retracted here**; nothing was lost and nothing diverged.
- **The correct check:** add a genuine GitHub remote (`git remote add gh https://github.com/jamesdillonbond/rip-packs-city.git; git fetch gh main`) and compare against `gh/main`, or query the API. Do NOT trust `origin/main` in this sandbox. The push rejections I saw were real, but they meant "you based this on the mount's older tip", not "someone rewrote history".
- **DURABLE (the meta-lesson): I diagnosed an incident from an instrument I had not verified — the exact failure this session has caught in four other places.** Distrust the instrument before the system, including when the instrument is git.
- **Removed `__tests__/component-SerialPremiumsBoardClient-headline-param.test.tsx`** (the genuine CI red). It asserted the `<h1>` contains `'#1'`/`'perfect'`; it renders **`'Serial Premiums'`**. **`.tsx` tests CANNOT execute in this sandbox** — `node_modules` lives only on the Windows mount, a symlinked jsdom+React mount exceeds the 45s command cap (user time ~1s; pure mount I/O), and background jobs do not survive a call boundary (`--unshare-pid`). The authoring agent flagged this and said "run it in CI"; I pushed anyway. Removed rather than re-guessed — a second assertion I equally cannot execute repeats the error with more confidence and less evidence. **The `?headline=perfect` PRODUCT fix stays; it was verified in a real browser.**
- **DURABLE: a `.ts` test is verifiable here, a `.tsx` test is not. Do not push a `.tsx` test you have not run.**
- **Revert:** `git revert <sha>` restores the test file (still red until its assertions match the real DOM).

Bisected: **not** the `editionsExtFieldsOk` ternary (removing it changes nothing) and **not** `--unstable-sloppy-imports`. Fixed with the compiler's own prescribed remedy — a named `GqlResult<T>` alias annotating `r`, and an explicit indexed-access type on `conn`. **Type-only ⇒ fully erased at runtime ⇒ these functions do NOT need a redeploy**, and annotating strictly increases type safety (a wrong property chain would now surface as a real error rather than being swallowed by `any`).

Those errors are an artifact, not a regression. Repair: `rm -rf node_modules/.deno node_modules/@onflow/fcl && npm install && git checkout package-lock.json`. Harmless in CI (fresh runner, and `edge-deno` is a different job from `typecheck`). Also note `deno check --config …` writes `supabase/functions/deno.lock`; it is now **gitignored on purpose** — CI has never validated against a lockfile and adding one introduces a lock-mismatch failure mode on remote-dep drift for a gate that is now blocking, while `supabase functions deploy` resolves deps independently of it.
- **Method note:** this box had no Deno; installed 2.9.4 from the **GitHub release** (`github.com/denoland/deno/releases/latest/download/deno-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.zip`) — the `deno.land/install.ps1` path fails here, matching the handoff's proxy note. Having a real toolchain is what made this adjudicable at all; the cloud sandbox could only guess, and guessed wrong twice.

### 2026-08-01 (Claude Code, interactive — "work through any issues" → wind-down) — VACUUMed the 7 `sales` partitions to fix a degrading MV-refresh; `mv_topshot_misattrib_candidates` refresh 43.5s → 30.4s (heap fetches → 0 on all static partitions). Prod maintenance op (no revert) + queued the structural residual.

- **Context:** `check_pgcron_recent_failures()` surfaced one `rpc-refresh-misattrib-candidates` failure (`REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW public.mv_topshot_misattrib_candidates` → statement timeout, 08-01 15:35Z). My first read was "one-off transient (6/7 daily success)" — WRONG. Profiling the MV's defining query showed it is genuinely **43.5s**, dominated (26.6s) by the `collide_groups` `count(DISTINCT nft_id) > 1` over ~3M TS `sales` rows, whose `idx_sales_YYYY_ts_edserial_collide` **index-only scans were degraded to massive heap fetches** (sales_2024 alone: 10.9s / 655k heap fetches) because the visibility map wasn't set. It grows with `sales`, so the timeout risk worsens over time — a real issue, not saturation.
- **SHIPPED (prod maintenance) — `VACUUM (ANALYZE)` on `sales_2020..sales_2026`.** Heap fetches now **0** on every static partition (2020–2025 receive no new writes, so they stay all-visible → durable); query 43.5s → 30.4s. Also benefits any other index-only scan on `sales`. The refresh function already carries `statement_timeout=600s` (generous — the 08-01 kill was an extreme-contention balloon past even that, during the busy CC wave), so raising the timeout is NOT the fix and a non-concurrent REFRESH locks the MV while it runs. **No revert** (VACUUM is maintenance: no schema/data change).
- **QUEUED (do NOT autonomously ship — ingest/FMV-adjacent MV):** the refresh is still ~30s+ and can exceed timeouts on a cold/contended Micro. Durable structural options for a focused session: (a) autovacuum tuning to keep the current-year partition all-visible, (b) incremental collision detection instead of a full 3M-row recompute daily, or (c) `REFRESH … CONCURRENTLY` (needs a unique index on the MV; the MV is a single `nft_id` column — a unique index is feasible). Consumer is `topshot-misattrib-drain`; a stale-by-a-day MV is low impact, so this is not urgent.
- **Also this session (already ledgered above):** fixed the UFC-slug→wrong-collection class in `/api/acquisition-stats` + `wallet-search` + `wallet-cache` (2 commits, CI-green, deploys READY). Full health sweep otherwise green: trust 0/25 breaching, advisors known-posture, Sentry 4 unresolved = the documented entity-page saturation class (pack-detail confirmed 52ms warm / 560ms cold, no indexable amplification) + a one-off smoke transient; pipeline fails/stalls all by-design or external cron-job.org tick dropout (`ufc-studio` — healthy, no data loss).

### 2026-08-01 (Claude Code, interactive — "work through any issues you can") — fixed a real anon-reachable 500 on the PUBLIC `/api/edition-history` route (`?days=<non-numeric>` → RangeError). Route-logic + regression test; direct to `main`.

- **SHIPPED — `?days=abc` (or empty / `NaN`) no longer 500s `/api/edition-history`.** The route is in `proxy.ts` `PUBLIC_READ_APIS` (anon-reachable) and has NO try/catch. It did `parseInt(?days) → const days = Math.min(Math.max(daysParam, 1), 90)`; `Math.min`/`Math.max` do NOT sanitize NaN (`Math.min(90, NaN) === NaN`), so a present-but-non-numeric `?days` gave `days = NaN` → `since.setUTCDate(getUTCDate() - NaN)` = Invalid Date → `since.toISOString()` threw `RangeError: Invalid time value` → 500. Exactly the NaN-clamp class the 08-01 `/insights` + `/api/recent-sales` sweeps fixed, missed because it sits OUTSIDE `/insights` and uses a bare `parseInt`+`Math` clamp rather than the `Number(x) || default` idiom. Guarded with `Number.isFinite(daysParam) ? Math.min(Math.max(daysParam,1),90) : 21` (21 = the pre-existing default). Added a 6-case `it.each` regression to `__tests__/api-edition-history.test.ts` — PROVEN TO BITE: reverting the guard reddens exactly the 3 NaN inputs (`abc`/``/`NaN`) with the RangeError while finite extremes still clamp. `tsc` clean; full edition-history suite green (10/10). **Revert:** `git revert <sha>`.
- **DURABLE — audited the WHOLE anon-reachable numeric-param surface, not just this route.** Swept every public path (`proxy.ts` `PUBLIC_READ_APIS` + the `/api/analytics/*`, `/api/public/*`, `/api/entity/*` public prefixes) for the NaN-clamp class: **all others are already guarded** — either via `Number(x) || default` (the `/insights` idiom; NaN is falsy → default, and covered by the directory-driven `invariants-public-insights-limit-nan-guard.test.ts`) or an explicit `Number.isFinite` helper (the analytics limit/days parsers, e.g. `parseInt1`/`parseInt32`/`parseLimit`). `edition-history` was the sole outlier. This class is now closed for anon routes — do NOT re-chase it broadly.

The gate is a **data-relative** horizon (`collection max(game_date) − 18 months`), deliberately not a hardcoded date, so it can never go stale AND stays correct for a collection whose data has stopped advancing (a frozen collection still resolves "team as of end of data" rather than marking everyone inactive). ### 2026-08-01 (Cowork, interactive — full platform audit: health · pipelines · data-integrity · CISO · CMO/SEO · Candy/Panini · codebase) — shipped 8 prod DB migrations + 1 code batch closing a **P0 credential leak**, a **live anon cost-basis exposure**, **5 IDOR routes**, and **2,781 pack pages** that were hiding an EV we already held. Each item below has its own revert path; direct to `main`.

Nine parallel audits (pipelines/schedulers, data-integrity at population scale, CISO, CMO+SEO+onboarding, Candy/Panini go-live, codebase+backlog, FMV/pack-EV coverage, plus implementation agents). Findings that were healthy-by-design are recorded as such and NOT actioned.

**SECURITY (all verified with functional `has_table_privilege` / `SET ROLE anon` probes, never `information_schema`):**
- **P0 — live Dapper session + PII committed to a PUBLIC repo.** `scripts/fetch-allday-collection.mjs` hardcoded `cf_clearance` + `nfl_session.0/1/2` cookies and an RS256 `ID_TOKEN` whose payload carries a real email, legal name and Flow account id. `git check-ignore` → NOT ignored; tracked since `1c3e01a8f`. Converted to the env-var pattern its sibling scripts already use (`ALLDAY_COOKIES` / `ALLDAY_ID_TOKEN`) + a fail-fast guard. ⚠ **HEAD-only — the secrets remain in git HISTORY. Trevor must (a) invalidate that Dapper session and (b) run `git filter-repo --path scripts/fetch-allday-collection.mjs --invert-paths` + force-push.** Repo-wide sweep found no sibling file with the same pattern.
- **P1 — cost-basis / P&L was anon-readable** (`audit_20260801_revoke_anon_cost_basis_surface`). `moment_acquisitions`: **790,801 rows readable as `anon`**, 89,117 with a real `buy_price`, across 7,627 wallets (`buy_price`, `fmv_at_acquisition`, `seller_address`, `loan_principal`). This silently defeated the deliberate `proxy.ts` decision that "spend/P&L is private, owner-only". Revoked from `anon` **and** `authenticated` (front door is open since 07-20, and no RLS scopes rows to their owner) + dropped `public_read_moment_acquisitions`. Three invoker-chains were run down first (`v_topshot_edition_pull_provenance`, `pipeline_health`, `get_wallet_summary`/`get_wallet_moments_with_fmv`) — all reach the table via `supabaseAdmin`, so none was load-bearing. **Revert:** `GRANT SELECT ON public.moment_acquisitions TO anon, authenticated;` + recreate the policy.
- **P1 — 5 IDOR routes.** `profile/watchlist` (GET/POST/DELETE), `watchlist` (GET/POST/DELETE), `wallet/save` (POST), `wallet/profile` (GET), `profile/portfolio-history` (POST) all handed a request-supplied `ownerKey` to the SERVICE-ROLE client as the row selector — the request param WAS the authorization decision. New `lib/auth/owner-key-guard.ts`. **DURABLE: `owner_key` is POLYMORPHIC** — measured live, the same column holds an auth user UUID (all 1,217 `portfolio_snapshots` rows), a `profile_bio.username`, AND a 0x Flow address (what `localStorage.rpc_owner_key` actually holds after `collection/page.tsx` + `SignInWithDapper` overwrite it, i.e. what `WalletHydrator` sends). A guard resolving only usernames would have 403'd live traffic; this one bridges all three (user-id fast path → `saved_wallets` membership for address-shaped keys → `profile_bio` exact claim → 403), fails closed on every error, and re-checks the `ilike` result exactly so a `%` wildcard can't grant ownership. `wallet/profile`'s in-process cache is now keyed `${user.id}::${ownerKey}`. **`portfolio-history` GET stays PUBLIC by design** (it backs the public profile card). 32 guard tests + 26 repaired route tests + new 401/403 assertions on every guarded verb.
- **P3 — `watchlist_items` was anon-readable** (the CISO sweep had it as "latent, not breached" — it was breached; empty today, so nothing leaked). Revoked + policy dropped, along with 6 dead `qual=true` policies on `panini_*`/`candy_offers` (`audit_20260801_drop_dead_anon_read_policies_staged_data`) so a single future GRANT can't replay the 2026-07-19 incident.
- **P3 — 6 anon-EXECUTE volatile writers revoked** (`audit_20260801_revoke_anon_exec_volatile_writers`). `compute_price_snapshots()` had ZERO callers repo-wide and was an unauthenticated, argument-free aggregate over `sales` = a free DB-CPU exhaustion lever on an IOPS-bound instance. Revoked `FROM PUBLIC` as well as the roles (a role-only revoke leaves `has_function_privilege` true — trap #3).
- Post-state: `check_public_security_invariants()` 0 · `check_anon_write_surface()` 0 · `check_secdef_anon_exec_drift()` `[]`.

**DATA CORRECTNESS:**
- **2,781 pack pages un-hidden** (`audit_20260801_pack_ev_latest_admit_unknown_price_packs_v2`). `pack_ev_latest` filtered `pack_price > 0`, but the AllDay/Golazos writers do `node.price?.value ? Number(...) : 0` — **"price unknown" was written as "price zero"** and the view dropped the row, discarding a correctly-computed EV over a fully-populated drop pool (~40,600 pool rows; AllDay avg gross_ev **$678.72**, i.e. the most valuable AllDay packs in the index). Measured split of the 2,773 `pack_price=0` rows: AllDay 2,589 + Golazos 175 have `retail_price_usd IS NULL` (unknown) · Pinnacle 6 + TS 3 have `= 0` (genuine REWARD packs) · TS 32 have `> 0` (a writer defect). Now admits ONLY the unknown class and forces every price-RELATIVE field (`pack_ev`, `value_ratio`, `is_positive_ev`) to NULL, so no margin is ever asserted against a price we don't have; reward packs and the writer-bug class stay excluded. **AllDay 504→3,110 rows, Golazos 27→202; platform total 1,814→4,595.** Also relaxes the `>= 9999` DROP to the same treatment. **Revert:** restore the prior viewdef (in the migration comment).
- **489 Top Shot packs regained Typical Pull** (`..._backfill_topshot_historical_pack_ev_persist_typical_ev_v2`). `compute_pack_ev_per_edition_weighted` returns `typical_pull_ev` for every collection and both live writers persist it — this historical backfill omitted `typical_ev` from its INSERT column list. AllDay/Pinnacle were at 100%; **Top Shot was the only collection with the hole**, in the figure the public pack-EV block is required to LEAD with. Corrects CLAUDE.md's inverted framing.
- **Candy MLB Holders tab was rendering EMPTY on the LIVE public board** (`audit_20260801_candy_holder_board_scope_fmv_join`). `candy_holder_board` joined `fmv_current`, whose DISTINCT ON materializes over all ~944k `fmv_snapshots` rows before filtering to the 125 Candy editions → **82.3s**, blowing the request budget; the page's fail-soft `fetchView` returned `[]` so a headline tab read "Holders 0" while the view holds **373 collectors**, with nothing in Sentry. Scoped the FMV lookup to the Candy partition slice: **82.3s → 2.9s cold**, 373 rows. Same anti-pattern as the 2026-08-01 `get_set_detail` lesson.
- **91 Golazos moment pages had 404 team links** (`audit_20260801_get_team_detail_accept_unaccented_team_slug`). `slugifyTeam` strips diacritics (`atletico-de-madrid`) but the SQL slug expression does not (`atl-tico-de-madrid`), so `get_team_detail` returned NULL → 404 for Atlético de Madrid (51 editions), UD Almería, Cádiz, Málaga, Deportivo, Leganés, Hércules. Trevor's ruling: accept EITHER. The exact-match fast path is untouched (a bare `OR` would defeat `idx_editions_collection_team_slug` and reintroduce the cold-scan → pool-timeout class); the `extensions.unaccent` lane runs ONLY on a would-be 404. Guarded splice that ABORTS on anchor drift. Verified: both slugs resolve, genuine 404s still 404, TS control unaffected.

**MONITORING — closed the structural "running ≠ working" gap** (`audit_20260801_pipeline_failure_rate_alert_arm`). All 98 `pipeline_cadence_watchlist` rows key on `max_silent_minutes` ONLY, so the entire alerting model asks "did it RUN?" and never "did it WORK?". Measured today, three pipelines were failing hard while every sentinel read green: `topshot-active-listings-ingest` 51.6%, `topshot-pack-opens-history-backfill` 71.9%, `topshot-misattrib-drain` 100% (not even watchlisted). ### 2026-08-01 (Claude Code, interactive — picking up the handed-over "trust-health view takes 49s" item) — DISPROVED the handoff's diagnosis, then fixed the REAL hot spot. One DB-only index; `v_rpc_trust_health` 7,999ms → 1,006ms with the board byte-identical (25 arms, 0 breaching).

The handoff ([/tmp/handoff-2026-08-01f-trust-health-view-49s.md](../handoff-2026-08-01f-trust-health-view-49s.md), Cowork) proposed moving the `packev` CTE into `rpc_trust_health_precompute`, citing "packev is 92% of it" and estimating ~49s → ~4s. **That change was NOT made — its rationale does not survive measurement.**

- **THE CORRECTION (durable — this is the reusable lesson): `packev` is 92% of the planner COST ESTIMATE (522,256 of 567,668) but only ~8.5% of RUNTIME (676ms of 7,999ms). Cost is not time.** Measured per-arm with `EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, TIMING ON)`: the real hot spot was **`pinnacle_fmv_impossible_flags` at 3,911–4,639ms, ~50–58%** of the view; then `unmapped_resolution_backlog_max` 937ms, `offer_edition_gap_max_usd` 772ms, `packev` 676ms, `edition_integrity_flags` 415ms. Shipping the proposed change would have bought **~8% (8.0s → 7.3s), not 12×**, in exchange for making two arms up to 6h stale. Being fair to it: `packev` is the most VARIABLE leg (676ms quiet → 5,267ms contended, 8× swing, ~385k buffer *hits* from a SubPlan run 62,615×), so under contention it can dominate — the instinct wasn't baseless, only the evidence cited.
- **THE HANDOFF'S SAFETY ALARM WAS ALREADY CLOSED, and it flagged this as unverified.** "A monitoring system that times out looks healthy" does not apply: `v_rpc_trust_health`'s consumer is **`/api/sentinel`, NOT `/api/check-alerts`** — `get_pipeline_alerts()` does not read the view at all. [app/api/sentinel/route.ts:329-331](../../app/api/sentinel/route.ts) catches the error, classifies it via `isSaturationError()`, and pushes `status:"warn"` prefixed `INCONCLUSIVE (db saturated) — `, never `ok`. So a timeout makes the board **UNREAD, not falsely green** — a real visibility gap (service_role budget is 30s and the cold path exceeded it), but not the silent-healthy failure that justified urgency.
- **SHIPPED — `audit_20260801_pinnacle_sales_render_rollup_covering_index` (DB-only, no deploy, no behavioural change).** `v_pinnacle_fmv_sanity_flags`'s per-render 90d rollup planned as a Bitmap Heap Scan touching 3,831 blocks (3,661 heap) and returned `shared hit=6 read=3825` — **essentially zero cache hits, re-reading ~30MB from disk every call** on Micro. The existing `idx_pinnacle_sales_pulse_window` covers `(sold_at DESC) INCLUDE (sale_price_usd, …)` but **omits `render_id`**, so it could not go index-only. New `idx_pinnacle_sales_render_rollup` = `(sold_at DESC) INCLUDE (render_id, sale_price_usd)`, ~9MB, 13th index on the table. **Arm 3,911ms → 30.6–35ms; disk reads on that leg 3,742 → 240** (the cache-independent metric, so the COLD path improves by ~3,500 block reads); **whole view 7,999ms → 1,006ms**. Verified board identical: 25 arms, 0 breaching, `pinnacle_fmv_impossible_flags` still `0`.
- **VALIDATED THE PRECONDITION BEFORE BUILDING, rather than assuming** (the exact error I'd just caught in the handoff): a covering INCLUDE index only helps if index-only actually engages, and the documented counter-case is hot not-all-visible pages ([[large-index-build-on-hot-table]] / the FMV `fmv_current` note in CLAUDE.md). Checked `relallvisible = relpages = 6474` → **100% all-visible** → index-only will engage. It did (`Index Only Scan`, residual `Heap Fetches: 9095` are post-autovacuum rows and are cache hits, not disk reads).
- **NOT done, deliberately:** `packev` is now the largest remaining leg (611ms of ~1,006ms) — but at ~0.6s of a 1s query it is **no longer worth 6h of staleness on two arms**, so the handoff's change stays declined on its merits, not just its rationale. Also left alone: consolidating the now-overlapping `idx_pinnacle_sales_pulse_window` into the new index (would serve both consumers with one index, but touches a live surface for no measured win).
- **Revert:** `DROP INDEX IF EXISTS public.idx_pinnacle_sales_render_rollup;` (pure performance object — no arm value or behaviour depends on it) + `git revert <sha>` for the migration file.

### 2026-08-01 (Claude Code, interactive — handoff drain, cont.) — SHIPPED the fix for the queued TS-PACK-OPENS-HISTORY-BACKFILL-SPORK-FLOOR-500. The diagnosis in that queued item was wrong on three counts; the real defect is an all-or-nothing 25k-block window against a FLAKY (not dead) spork. Edge fn `ingest-topshot-pack-opens-history` now checkpoints partial scan progress. Repo + DEPLOYED v4 via Supabase MCP.

- **Three corrections to the queued item, each evidence-backed.** (1) **"rows_written=0 for four days incl. the green days" is NOT silent loss — it is correct dedup.** Positive control: the 03:56Z run logged `rows_found=81` over blocks 95,090,659–95,115,658, and `pack_rips` holds **exactly 81** TS rips in that window. It found 81 opens, all 81 already stored, wrote 0. The signal was missing because **`rows_skipped` was never instrumented** on this route (logged 0 despite 81 dedups) — `rows_written` alone is a null instrument for a *re-walking* backfill. (2) **The "cursor-skip" was a fast-forward, not a skip.** 95,090,659 → 61,930,346 = exactly `MIN(pack_rips.block_height)` for TS; coverage from there to head is dense and gapless (20/20 width_buckets populated, 21k–120k rips each). Nothing was stepped over. (3) **`c4c4d3c9` cannot be the cause — it is a docs-only ledger commit** (`git show --stat`: 1 file, `docs/overnight/ledger.md`). The correlation was spurious. Also: AllDay is not out-finding TopShot — both find 80–330/run; AllDay *writes* them because it is on uncovered ground.
- **Where the low-range data actually came from:** all **272,559** TS rips below block 96M were written on **one day, 2026-07-11**, spanning 61,930,346–95,999,995 — the Dapper `searchPackNft` registry bulk load ([[dapper-searchpacknft-opens-registry]]), not this event scanner. So the fn has been re-verifying the registry's work, which is why it found plenty and wrote nothing.
- **THE ACTUAL DEFECT.** The fn scans a 25,000-block window as ~100 sequential 250-block `/events` queries and abandons the **entire** window on the first failure (`after = anyTransient ? cur : start`). The deep-history spork is **flaky, not down** — the 41 failing runs died at query **1,2,3,4,5 in rotation**, i.e. different sub-windows each time, several getting 4 chunks deep. With any per-query failure rate, a 100-query all-or-nothing window essentially never completes, so the cursor never moved and 96 runs/day burned. This is NOT the spork-floor problem the queued item assumed (`floor` was already correctly set to 27,341,470 and `spork_available:true`).
- **SHIPPED — descending scan + checkpoint (edge fn, repo + deployed v4).** `scanOpens` now walks **DESCENDING** (end→start, matching the cursor's direction) and returns `scannedFloor` = the lowest block CONFIRMED scanned; an ascending scan cannot checkpoint because a mid-window failure leaves a hole *above* the scanned prefix. `resolveOpens` returns `resolvedFloor` + `exhausted` so the cursor never advances past opens the tx budget left unwritten (scanning a block ≠ having written its rips). Cursor advances to `min(scannedFloor-or-resolvedFloor, cur)`, clamped at `floor`. Progress is now **monotonic under any upstream failure rate**. Also: `rows_skipped` is now populated (= dedup count) via `writeRips` returning `{written, candidates}`, and `ok` = *progressed OR no error* — a checkpointed run that advanced did its job (failure preserved in `extra.scan_err` + new `extra.partial`); only a run that moved NOTHING stays `ok=false` and pages.
- **The "how far back" question the queued item deferred is already answered IN THE FN's own header** — `SPORK_FLOOR = 27,341,470` (mainnet17 root, 2022-04-06). Public sporks bottom out there; TS genesis (~block 7M, Oct 2020) is permanently unreachable and documented as an explicit gap. So there is **~34.6M blocks of real, reachable, un-indexed TS pack-open history** (2022-04-06 → 2023-09-29) below the registry floor. No decision was needed and none was invented — the fn should keep walking to 27,341,470.
- ⚠ **Deployed as a MINIMAL DIFF: the deployed body keeps its inline `https://esm.sh/@supabase/supabase-js@2` import** while the repo file uses the bare specifier via `supabase/functions/deno.json`. That is the documented pre-existing repo↔deployed divergence, deliberately not changed in the same deploy as a logic fix.
- ⚠ **Unexplained-by-code:** nothing in the repo sets the cursor to 61,930,346 — the fn only ever writes `start`. Consistent with a deliberate manual fast-forward to the registry floor; noted, not treated as a defect.
- **POST-DEPLOY VERIFICATION — fix CONFIRMED working, and the flaky-not-dead diagnosis is now PROVEN.** 14:57:19Z tick: `ok=false`, `progress_blocks=0`, failed chunk `61,930,096–61,930,345` (the top chunk — descending scan starting nearest the cursor, as designed). 15:11:01Z tick: **that same chunk SUCCEEDED**, `ok=true`, `partial=true`, `q=2`, cursor 61,930,346 → **61,930,096**, `scanned_floor=61,930,096`. A chunk that 500s and then serves 14 min later is conclusive — the sub-61.93M region is flaky, not dead, so the queued spork-floor guard would have been wrong. Under the old code that 15:11 run would have been `ok=false` with zero progress; the 250 blocks are now kept.
- ⚠ **NEW RISK INTRODUCED BY THIS FIX — do not read the above as a clean win. THROUGHPUT, and the loss of every alarm.** At ~1–3 chunks/tick (~250–750 blocks) against **34.6M blocks remaining**, this region would take on the order of YEARS. Worse, because the cursor now moves and runs report `ok=true`, **neither `cursor_stalled` NOR the fail-rate alarm can ever fire for it again** — the job is now invisible while making ~1% of design throughput. That is precisely the [[green-pipeline-blind-to-its-own-work]] class. The fix is still strictly better than a hard wedge (it was making ZERO progress and paging), but the pipeline now needs a *rate* signal, not a liveness one. ⚠ **The ETA is a 2-SAMPLE estimate** — the ascending history (failures at query 1–5, i.e. 0–4 chunks succeeding) is the same order but this must be measured over a full day before anyone acts on it.
- **QUEUED (next lever, deliberately NOT taken unilaterally — it is a cost/throughput tradeoff against the spork proxy): raise the per-chunk retry budget on the spork events path.** `j()` gives up after 3 tries at 400ms×n backoff; since the identical chunk demonstrably succeeds minutes later, a larger in-run retry budget (or a longer backoff) should raise chunks-per-run substantially and is a one-constant change. Second queued item: a **backfill-rate metric** (e.g. blocks/day per history cursor, or an ETA-to-floor arm on `v_rpc_trust_health`) so a crawling-but-green backfill is visible — without it this fix trades a loud wedge for a silent one.
- **SAME-CLASS DEFECT FOUND + FIXED IN THE ALLDAY TWIN — and it is ACTIVELY LOSING DATA TODAY (repo only, NOT deployed).** `ingest-allday-pack-opens` carries the identical ascending-scan + `after = anyTransient ? cur : start`. It is not wedged (its region isn't flaky yet, 53,165 rows/24h) but it has the **second** failure mode live: on a `MAX_TX=180` tx-budget stop it still advances the FULL 25,000-block window over opens it never resolved. **Measured: 16 of 143 runs in 24h hit `tx_fetched = 180` exactly, every one advancing the full 25,000 blocks** (e.g. 11:56Z `rows_found=939`, budget hit, cursor 111,465,659 → 111,440,659). Those opens are never revisited — the cursor only walks down.
- ⚠ **DURABLE — scan direction MUST match the caller's cursor direction, and this fn has TWO walkers going opposite ways.** A naive port of the Top Shot fix (unconditional descending) would have silently changed which rows the FORWARD walker's budget drops: forward walks UP, so a descending scan leaves its *lowest* opens unresolved while it advances to `end`. Fixed properly instead — `scanOpens(start, end, dir)` with `"desc"` for backfill and the default `"asc"` for forward/probe, so **forward-mode behaviour is byte-identical to today** and only backfill gains the checkpoint. Getting the direction backwards is silent loss, not an error: the unscanned hole ends up on the side the cursor is about to claim.
- **Why AllDay is NOT deployed this session (deliberate, not a deferral of work — the artifact is committed and reviewable):** it is a healthy, high-volume live pipeline, and the MCP deploy channel inlines the whole ~460-line body by hand, which CLAUDE.md flags as a transcription risk for byte-exact constants. It deserves its own deploy + post-deploy tick verification rather than riding at the tail of another change. Both fns type-clean under `tsc --strict` (only the pre-existing `Deno.serve` `req: any`, identical in both). **To deploy:** same MCP call as the Top Shot one, `verify_jwt:false`, then confirm a backfill tick shows `cursor_after < cursor_before` with `extra.resolve_exhausted` honoured. **Forward-mode tx-budget loss is left OPEN** (pre-existing; needs the asc-side checkpoint) — queued, not silently fixed.
- **Revert:** `git revert <sha>` restores the repo file; to unwind PROD, redeploy the previous body — `mcp__supabase__deploy_edge_function` with `ingest-topshot-pack-opens-history`, `verify_jwt:false`, using the **v3** source (recoverable via `get_edge_function` history, or `git show <sha>^:supabase/functions/ingest-topshot-pack-opens-history/index.ts` with the import line swapped back to the esm.sh form). No DB or cursor change to unwind — the cursor moves only forward-down and re-walking is idempotent on `tx_hash`.

### 2026-07-31 (Claude Code, interactive — "find a TODO → also fix any bugs you encounter") — SHIPPED a DB fix for the one open live Sentry bug: `get_set_detail` now DEGRADES instead of throwing on a statement timeout (the "Base Set" set page). Prod DB migration (applied via MCP + committed) + re-pinned DB test.

- **Context:** the TODO sweep re-confirmed the standing finding (every live TODO is RESOLVED/GATED — nothing safe + straightforward to implement), so on the "also fix bugs" directive I took the sole open Sentry issue: `JAVASCRIPT-NEXTJS-22` "set detail unavailable: canceling statement due to statement timeout" on `GET /[collection]/set/[slug]` (1 user, last seen ~07-30).
- **Root cause (profiled, not guessed):** `get_set_detail`'s only expensive work is the per-edition latest-FMV rollup. For Top Shot "Base Set" (3,606 thumbnail-bearing editions) the `LEFT JOIN LATERAL … ORDER BY computed_at DESC LIMIT 1` fans out to 3,606 correlated probes across the yearly `fmv_snapshots` partitions — **~2.0s warm** (+3,883 cold reads) — and cold under contention it exceeded the request statement budget and THREW, erroring the whole public set page. `rpcWithRetry` (which the page's read already uses) deliberately does NOT retry 57014 (07-26 change — a slow query just re-times-out), so retry was never the fix.
- **Rejected alternatives (measured, not assumed):** the CLAUDE.md "use `fmv_current`" rule is for the JS-1000-row-cap correctness case, NOT this in-DB path — a `fmv_current` DISTINCT-ON join is **11× WORSE (22.5s)** (materializes the DISTINCT ON over all ~942k snapshot rows before filtering). A covering `INCLUDE(fmv_usd,floor_price_usd)` index doesn't help either: the wanted row is always the newest = a hot, not-all-visible page, so index-only still heap-fetches. Precompute into `sets_summary` is wrong-scoped (its `edition_count` deliberately excludes the thumbnail filter) + a sensitive daily-matview change. So the LATERAL stays and we bound its FAILURE instead.
- **SHIPPED — `audit_20260801_get_set_detail_graceful_fmv_timeout` (DB-only, no deploy).** Wrapped ONLY the rollup in `BEGIN … EXCEPTION WHEN query_canceled` so a request-level statement timeout DEGRADES the header stats to NULL (page renders "—" via `fmtCount(null)`) instead of throwing; the page — incl. the separately-fetched editions grid — still renders. Also dropped the RETURN's `COALESCE(edition_count,0)` so a degraded read shows "—" not a misleading "0" beside a populated grid. Happy path behaviourally byte-identical (COUNT(*) is never NULL; normal sets finish in a few ms). STABLE preserved; grants preserved + re-asserted (service_role-only; anon/auth EXECUTE false).
- **Durable finding (cost a live break, now fixed):** `statement_timeout` is armed at the TOP-LEVEL command boundary and CANNOT be re-armed mid-function — a `SET LOCAL statement_timeout` inside the body throws "SET is not allowed in a non-volatile function" on a STABLE fn (my first apply broke the fn on EVERY call for ~2 min until the fix), and even under VOLATILE the inner SET is a no-op (verified: `pg_sleep(1)` under `SET LOCAL '50ms'` completes).
