### 2026-07-31 (Claude Code, interactive — handoff verification, round 2) — ROOT-CAUSED the TopShot 5,426-row cluster to `/api/wallet/seed` and hardened it. **Falsifies the "fell out of walk rotation" diagnosis, and CORRECTS my own prior entry's "writer unidentified" claim, which was drawn from a pruned table.**

**⚠ CORRECTION to the entry below (and to the handoff that proposed it).** Both said *"`pipeline_runs` has no matching record for the 07-28 15:31 write window, so the writer is unidentified."* That inference is unsound: **`pipeline_runs` oldest retained row is 2026-07-29 00:41 — ZERO rows before that.** The daily prune had destroyed the 07-28 evidence days before either of us queried it. We were reading absence from a table that *cannot* contain the answer and calling it a finding. Same null-instrument error as `cadence_check` earlier in this thread — **third occurrence in two days. Before concluding anything from an empty result, establish the instrument's range.**

**The rotation theory is falsified on two independent checks.** (1) **No code anywhere deletes from `seeded_wallets`** — grep across `app/` + `lib/` for delete/remove against that table returns nothing, so there is no mechanism by which a wallet "falls out". (2) **`0x25ab9f12447a88f4` was never IN rotation** — it has **no `seeded_wallets` row at all**, and rotation is driven by `seeded_wallets.last_refreshed_per_collection[slug]`. It is an on-demand seed, not a dropped regular. **The control group settles it:** all 3 non-seeded TopShot wmc wallets — `0x25ab9f12` (5,477 rows, **99.1% broken**), `0x01be49cb` (1,687 rows, **0.0%**), `0x54f4a98f` (32 rows, **0.0%**). Never-re-walked does not cause breakage; two wallets in the identical situation are perfect. So "why does a failed walk drop a wallet from the queue" would have been chasing a mechanism that does not exist.

**Actual writer: `app/api/wallet/seed/route.ts`.** Signature match is exact — the bare rows have `edition_key` **NULL** (not `''`) and **0 serials**. That rules out the main TopShot walk: `app/api/wallet-backfill/route.ts:344` emits `""` on a partial-metadata miss, and `upsert_wmc_batch` writes `edition_key` **verbatim with no coercion** (confirmed from `pg_proc`) — and TopShot wmc holds **zero** empty-string edition_keys. The seed route instead maps **every** on-chain id unconditionally (L236), writes `edition_key: edition?.external_id ?? null` on an enrichment miss (L247), and hardcodes `serial_number: null` (L253) — so seed-written rows can *never* carry a serial. The 51 good rows (50 with serials) came from the real walk running concurrently; that is why the two groups **overlap in time** (good 15:31:37.362–38.486, bare 15:31:37.817–53.107).

**Why enrichment missed ~99%: three stacked, already-documented footguns in `enrichStandard`.** (a) the `error` was **not destructured** — a failed query left `editions` undefined, `?? []` degraded it to "no editions matched", and every moment was then written bare, silently; (b) **unchunked `.in()` over 5,477 ids** — past the PostgREST 1000-row cap and into URL-length territory, the exact non-throwing-error mechanism behind the fmv-recalc silent stall; (c) a **raw `fmv_snapshots` DESC + JS latest-wins dedup**, the pattern CLAUDE.md's DURABLE RULE forbids. Which one fired on 07-28 is **not recoverable** — the evidence was pruned.

**SHIPPED (code+test only; no migration, no prod-DB mutation):** `enrichStandard` editions lookup chunked at 500 and now **throws** on error instead of degrading to empty; FMV read moved to **`fmv_current`** + chunked. **Deliberately NOT done:** the write-bare-on-miss semantic at L247 is left as-is — turning it into a skip is a product judgment (a bare row still records ownership) and is not mine to make unilaterally. The hardening removes the *cause* of mass misses without changing what a genuine miss writes. **The 5,426 existing rows are NOT healed by this** — `0x25ab9f12` is not in rotation, so nothing will re-walk it; clearing them needs a deliberate one-off re-seed.

**The handoff cleared `wallet_moments_cache` as "enrichment lag, not loss." That conclusion was wrong**, and the age-cohort table that supported it omitted the column that mattered. It showed `player_name`/`fmv` converging monotonically to 100% by 30 days — true. But `edition_key` is **not** monotonic: 100% (<1d) → 100% (1–3d) → **49.7% (3–7d)** → 100% (7–14d) → 100% (>30d). **Root cause — a known bug, already found and fixed twice, never generalized.** `runIdOnlyBackfill` writes `edition_key: null` deliberately (helpers L546-559), on the stated premise that *"out-of-band edition resolvers populate player/set/tier on the editions table and reads JOIN at query time."* **Nothing can JOIN to `editions` without an `edition_key`**, and only **0.0%** of these rows are recoverable via `moments` (TopShot 2.3%). Separately `0x25ab9f12447a88f4` TopShot is **5,426/5,477 (99.1%) broken, 51 FMV** (different path, NOT fixed here — see QUEUED).

**Shipped:** new `GET_GOLAZOS_MOMENT_DETAILS` script + `detailsCadence`/`detailsMode` optional config fields; `runAllDayDetailsBackfill` now reads them (**defaults preserve AllDay behavior byte-for-byte**); `wallet-backfill-golazos` route switched from `runIdOnlyBackfill`. Verified against **mainnet contract source** via Cadence MCP: `A.87ca73a41bb50ad5.Golazos` is literally *"Adapted from: AllDay.cdc"* and exposes `editionID: UInt64` + `serialNumber: UInt64` on `Golazos.NFT`, with `Collection` conforming to `NonFungibleToken.Collection`. Script tries **both** public paths — the contract declares `/public/GolazosNFTCollection` but the working ID-only script uses legacy `/public/GolazoNFTCollection` (no trailing `s`), and that one demonstrably resolves for live wallets.

### 2026-07-31 (Claude Code, interactive — AllDay sales serial-supply regression) — FIXED THE WRITER + backfilled 8,575 rows. The inbound handoff scoped this to `onchain_dapper_v2` (1,325 rows) and called v1 "unaffected"; measured, it is **all three AllDay onchain sources, 8,626 rows, and v1 is the largest and fastest-growing arm**.

**SHIPPED — writer fix (`app/api/allday-sales-indexer/route.ts`) + backfill migration `audit_20260731_allday_sales_serial_backfill_from_nft_edition_map`.**

**Root cause (measured, not inferred).** The indexer's ONLY serial sources were `wallet_moments_cache` and a Cadence borrow fallback capped at `CADENCE_FALLBACK_MAX = 12` per run that fires only when the **edition** is unresolved. wmc holds only moments in a wallet we have walked, so for these NFTs there was **no wmc row at all** (`wmc_row_exists = 0`, not merely a null serial). The borrow then resolved the edition while returning no usable `serialNumber` (`Number(undefined)` → NaN → 0 → the `if (resolvedSerial > 0)` guard skips the set), so the row was inserted with `serial_number: null`. `nft_edition_map` — the durable nftID→serial record — was never consulted on the direct-insert path, **even though `promote_unmapped_sales` already uses exactly that fallback**. The precedent existed in the DB path and was missing in the route.

**The load-bearing measurement: 1,321 of 1,325 v2 rows (99.7%) had a positive serial in `nft_edition_map` BEFORE the sale row was written** (median lag 0). The data was there at write time; the writer didn't read it. That is what makes this a writer defect rather than a recovery-timing problem — and it is why the writer fix had to land, not just a backfill.

**Scope correction — the handoff's "v1 is unaffected (0–3.4%)" is wrong.** All three sources are written by the SAME insert path (`source` is derived from `s.saleSource` inside one loop), so one fix covers all three. Weekly, by ingestion:

| source | 06-15→07-06 | 07-13 | 07-20 | 07-27 | bad rows | recoverable |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `onchain_dapper_v1` | **0.0%** | 37.6% | 23.8% | **41.6%** (2,506) | 5,078 | 98.9% |
| `onchain` | **0.0%** | 15.4% | 6.0% | 3.3% | 2,223 | 100% |
| `onchain_dapper_v2` | **0.0%** | 11.6% | 9.6% | 20.5% | 1,325 | 100% |

Identical 07-13 onset on all three after 4+ weeks at a hard zero. v1 alone in the latest week (2,506 rows) exceeds the entire v2 finding the handoff reported.

**NOT caused by `5c1b0db9`** (the 07-04 "write NULL not phantom 0" commit), the obvious suspect: it landed a full week before the onset and the week of 07-06 is still 0.0% on all three arms. That commit changed the *sentinel* (0 → NULL); it did not create the gap.

**Impact.** `serial_number` drives `serial_fmv_estimate`, the special-serials board and jersey-match. Nothing monitored it — `allday-sales-indexer` is green throughout because it writes rows successfully. Same shape as the Panini sale-field outage: a healthy pipeline silently dropping one field.

**Backfill result:** 8,575 rows recovered, **0 mismatches**, 59 left (genuinely no map row with a positive serial). Audit table records every mutated row. RLS enabled + anon/authenticated REVOKED; `check_public_security_invariants()` 0 rows, `rowsecurity=false` 0 tables after.

**Test:** `__tests__/api-allday-sales-indexer-deep.test.ts` — new case reproduces the exact prod mechanism (no wmc row + borrow returns no `serialNumber` + map holds the serial). **Verified it FAILS without the fix** (`serial_number: null` vs expected `42`) and passes with it, so the pin cannot silently rot into a test that asserts nothing.

**Revert path:**
```
git revert <code-sha>
```
```sql
UPDATE public.sales s SET serial_number = NULL
  FROM public.audit_20260731_allday_serial_backfill a
 WHERE s.id = a.sale_id AND s.serial_number = a.new_serial;
DROP TABLE public.audit_20260731_allday_serial_backfill;
```

**SECOND FINDING — the serial RECOVERY lane has the identical blind spot, and had been failing on these rows for 26 days while green.** `sales-serial-backfill` (edge fn, 37/37 ok runs, 4,314 rows written/30d) resolves serials **only on-chain**, by borrowing the moment from its *current holder* — `nft_edition_map` appears nowhere in it. That structurally cannot work for a sold NFT that has since moved or sits in escrow. **7,276 of the 8,575 rows I just backfilled were sitting in `sales_serial_backfill_failures`** with **46,376 accumulated retries** (`onchain_nil` 5,508 / `no_holder` 1,768), first failing **2026-07-06** and still retrying at **02:41Z today** — the durable local map held the answer the whole time. `get_serial_backfill_targets` was NOT the problem: it correctly includes AllDay and keys on `serial_number IS NULL OR = 0`, so these rows were eligible every run. The lane picked them up, went on-chain, failed, and logged `ok=true`.

**This class has recurred once already, which validates the writer-first ordering.** `audit_20260705_allday_serial_backfill` (**8,964 rows**) is a prior manual backfill of the same defect on 07-05. It drained the rows and did NOT fix the writer, so the gap re-accumulated to 8,626 within ~3 weeks. A backfill alone buys ~3 weeks.

**Side benefit, quantified:** the backfilled rows now carry a serial, so they drop out of `get_serial_backfill_targets` automatically — the lane's daily futile on-chain retry load fell from **~7,674 → 398 rows**.

**⚠ POST-DEPLOY CORRECTION — I FIRST DEFERRED THE RECOVERY-LANE FIX ON A BAD MEASUREMENT. IT IS THE ITEM THAT ACTUALLY CLOSES THIS. Read this before acting on anything above.**

I initially wrote that teaching `sales-serial-backfill` to read `nft_edition_map` "would recover exactly 1 row today" and deferred it. **That number was a point-in-time artifact: I measured the residual in the one minute after my own backfill had just drained it.** The correct denominator is the ONGOING arrival rate, and it is not small.

**Verified against the first post-deploy indexer runs (03:36Z / 03:41Z):**

| path | rows | no serial |
|---|---|---|
| `onchain_dapper_v2` | 4 | **0** ✅ |
| `onchain_dapper_v1` | 24 | 22 ❌ |
| `onchain` | 10 | 10 ❌ |

**32 rows arrived with a null serial in the ~22 min after deploy, and 31 of them (96.9%) are recoverable from `nft_edition_map` NOW** — i.e. the map is populated *shortly after* the sale is written, by a later pipeline. My writer fix reads the map at ingest, so it fixes the case where the NFT is ALREADY mapped (which was 99.7% of the 8,626-row backlog — hence the clean drain) but it **cannot** fix a first-sight NFT whose map row does not exist yet. For that, only a **re-sweep after the map fills** works — which is precisely what `sales-serial-backfill` is for, and precisely what it fails at by going on-chain instead of reading the map.

**So: the writer fix + backfill closed the accumulated backlog and the already-mapped case; the ONGOING case is still open and the recovery-lane fix is the thing that closes it.** Do not read the headline "31.3%/9.1%/7.1% → 0.4%/0.0%/0.0%" as the ongoing rate — that is the state of the *stock* after the backfill, not the *flow*.

Also corrected: `promote_unmapped_sales` is a second writer of these rows (matched by exact `ingested_at` ↔ its `pipeline_runs` timestamps, 03:36:17.459/03:41:37.394) — it DOES read `nft_edition_map`, but in those transactions the map row is written in the same txn and is not visible to its lookup, so it falls through its `COALESCE(..., 0)` → trigger → NULL. That is a distinct ordering defect from the route defect fixed above.

**Consequence to expect, and it is CORRECT behaviour:** the `sales_serial_supply_worst_pct` arm shipped tonight reads **0.75** right now only because its 24h window is still dominated by pre-fix rows that the backfill filled. As the window rolls forward onto the ongoing flow, it will climb and **may breach 5 and page**. That is the metric working, not a false alarm — the underlying gap is real and unfixed. Do not silence it; fix the recovery lane.

**✅ ROOT CAUSE OF THE ONGOING CASE FOUND AND FIXED — it was NOT the recovery lane, and it was a one-line route bug in 3 files.** Chasing the residual to its source: `promote_unmapped_sales` inserts `COALESCE(r.serial_number, r.map_serial, 0)`, where `r.serial_number` is `unmapped_sales.serial_number` and `map_serial` is the `nft_edition_map`→`wmc` fallback. **All three onchain sales indexers wrote `unmapped_sales` with a HARDCODED `serial_number: 0`** — and `COALESCE` returns the first **non-null** value, so a literal `0` always wins and **`map_serial` is unreachable DEAD CODE**. The row then lands in `sales` as 0 → `trg_sales_coerce_zero_serial_to_null` → NULL. A serial we already had on file was being discarded at the last step, and the DB-side fallback everyone (including the inbound handoff) assumed was working had never once executed for these rows.

`5c1b0db9` (2026-07-04) established NULL as the canonical unknown-serial sentinel and fixed the `sales` writer — **it missed the `unmapped_sales` writer**, which is where the COALESCE actually reads from. That is why the gap opened without any code change to the serial logic itself.

**SHIPPED:** `serial_number: 0` → `null` in the `unmappedRows` push of **`allday-sales-indexer`, `golazos-sales-indexer`, `ufc-sales-indexer`**. AllDay is the proven-affected one; Golazos/UFC carry the identical dead-fallback defect and are fixed preventively (same literal, same COALESCE, column is nullable with no default).

**Caller sweep done before shipping (the "enumerate EVERY consumer" rule):** `unmapped_sales.serial_number` has ZERO code readers; DB readers are `promote_unmapped_sales`, `backfill_nft_edition_map_from_sales`, `analytics_data_quality_overview` and 4 views. **Tests: three existing assertions PINNED THE BUG** (`serial_number: 0` on the unmapped row) and were rewritten. Note the two Golazos/UFC `serial_number: 0` assertions that REMAIN are correct and deliberately untouched — they assert the `sales` insert, where the trigger coerces 0→NULL harmlessly; only the `unmapped_sales` path poisons the COALESCE. 27 tests green, `tsc` clean.

**Revert:** `git revert <sha>` (restores `serial_number: 0` in all three; DB unchanged, no migration).

**AND THE PENDING STOCK, TOO — `audit_20260731_unmapped_sales_zero_serial_to_null` (DB-only, no deploy).** The writer fix only affects NEWLY written unmapped rows; the pending backlog still carried the poisoned literal. ### 2026-07-31 (Cowork, interactive) — MEASURED: the "AllDay `packEditionsV3` is Cloudflare/CF-1009 transport-blocked" diagnosis is **WRONG from the path that matters**. It is an upstream **HTTP 404**. Docs-only; no prod/DB state change, no deploy.

This matters because the recorded fix was "find a transport that isn't CF-blocked" — **building a proxy workaround would not have worked**, and it was sitting at the top of the priority list.

**Why the earlier finding didn't apply.** The CF-1009 result was measured from a **Cloudflare Worker** and from **residential**. But `app/api/allday-pack-ev/route.ts` calls `alldayGraphql()` ([lib/chains/flow/allday.ts](lib/chains/flow/allday.ts)), which hits **`https://nflallday.com/consumer/graphql` DIRECTLY — no worker proxy** — and CLAUDE.md already records that *"Vercel routes that hit consumer/graphql directly … work because Vercel egress isn't WAF-blocked there."* Nobody had tested the Vercel path.

**Test method:** POSTed the live production route from an authenticated browser session (Trevor's own site; a read-only compute endpoint, no mutation), and classified the upstream failure **without echoing the response body** — booleans for `403 / 1009 / 1015 / cloudflare / 429 / timeout` plus the first status code in the message. (The browser tool scrubs cookie/query-string-shaped data, so a raw error read is unavailable anyway.)

**Result — 4 packListingIds, consistent:** dist **15** and **2** (retired 2021 packs) and dists **7585 / 7580 / 7578** (the newest 2026 Rewind / Grail Seeker packs) all returned route **HTTP 502** wrapping upstream **HTTP 404**, failing at the `getPackListing` "pack supply" stage before `packEditionsV3` is ever reached. **Zero mentions of 403, 1009, 1015, Cloudflare, "attention required", 429 or timeout on any call.** A WAF block does not present as a uniform 404 across both retired and current listings.

**Reading:** the AllDay consumer `getPackListing` surface appears **retired**, which is consistent with the documented platform change (*"NFL All Day ended primary pack sales"*, May 2026). If so, AllDay per-edition remaining is **not obtainable at all**, not merely hard to reach — a more final answer than "blocked", and it removes transport work from the roadmap.

⚠ **LIMIT OF WHAT I PROVED — do not overstate this.** I did **not** establish that the whole consumer endpoint is dead. Probes at `/api/allday-sets` and `/api/allday-wallet-search` returned **400/405 parameter-validation errors and never reached upstream**, so they are uninformative; I stopped rather than keep guessing param names. **The open question is now narrow and cheap: does `nflallday.com/consumer/graphql` still serve OTHER queries from Vercel?** If yes → only `getPackListing` is gone and AllDay remaining is permanently unavailable. If no → `allday-wallet-search` and `allday-sets` are silently broken in production, which would be a live regression nobody has noticed. **That single check should be the next thing anyone does here.**

**Revert:** `git revert <sha>`.

**Then** `audit_20260801_normalize_retail_price_boundary_row` — moved both normalizers from `> 1000000` to `>= 1000000`. I first shipped `>` to match the existing `pack_distributions_v` convention, which left exactly one row (dist 8227 "NBA Top Shot x NBA ID", raw `1000000`) still rendering **$1,000,000** publicly. ⚠ **That was me protecting a decision I'd already made rather than the user:** every value in the set is `price × 1e8`, so `1000000` = **$0.01** — the consistent reading of its 107 siblings, and plausible for an NBA ID promo — while `$1,000,000 retail` for a 20,000-mint pack trading at $29 secondary is *certainly* wrong. ### 2026-07-31 (Claude Code, interactive — migration-record recovery) — RECOVERED 11 prod migrations that had NO repo file AND NO ledger entry, committed verbatim from `schema_migrations`. Repo/docs only; no prod/DB state change (these already ran days ago), no deploy.

**THE RULE (generalized, and it is not Cowork-specific).** `apply_migration` via MCP writes to `supabase_migrations.schema_migrations` ONLY — never a repo file, never the ledger. Any migration applied that way is live in prod with **no revert path on disk** unless someone files it separately. Recovery is mechanical: `SELECT array_to_string(statements, E'\n') FROM supabase_migrations.schema_migrations WHERE version = '<v>';`

**⚠ THE REPO WAS NEVER THE SYSTEM OF RECORD — do not read "no migration file" as "unauthorized change."** Prod holds **2,334** migrations; the repo holds **242** (~10%). Filing a `.sql` has always been the exception, so a missing file proves nothing on its own. **The binding record per CLAUDE.md is the LEDGER** (date · what shipped · revert path). So the real audit question is "does this have a ledger entry with a revert path?", and the correct check is a two-key one — repo file OR ledger entry — not a repo-file scan. Across the 43 migrations applied 07-28→07-31, **11 had neither**; the rest were covered by one or the other.

**CORRECTED THE INBOUND LIST IN BOTH DIRECTIONS** (the handoff asked for this to be verified rather than assumed, and both corrections matter):
- **`audit_20260801_panini_serial_sale_field_supply` was NOT missing** — it is already filed at `supabase/migrations/20260801010000_...`, reconstructed from live `pg_get_viewdef` by an earlier session. It was flagged only because the repo's version stamp (`20260801010000`) differs from the DB's (`20260801011610`). **Match migrations by NAME, not version stamp** — MCP assigns its own timestamp, so a hand-filed copy never shares it.
- **`..._allday_pull_edition_backfill_apply` and `..._v_pack_remaining_basis_rename_multi_tier_flag` were NOT missing either** — both are in the ledger, named in shorthand (`_stage` + `_apply`; `..._rename_multi_tier_flag`) with revert paths. ### 2026-07-31 (Cowork, interactive) — TESTED and KILLED the "publisher-independent remaining" idea. Docs-only; no prod/DB state change, no deploy.

**The attractive idea:** every collection except Top Shot lacks per-edition remaining, and the APIs that would supply it are transport-blocked (AllDay `packEditionsV3` is CF-1009 blocked; Pinnacle unknown). So infer depletion from data we already own — an edition's minted circulation vs its original pool count — giving `remaining ≈ orig_drop_weight − circulation_count`. That would bypass the transport problem for AllDay, Golazos **and** Pinnacle at once. It does not work.

**Tested against Top Shot ground truth** (26,143 pool rows / 756 dists where `pool_source='gql'` supplies true per-edition `remaining`), correlating each candidate's normalized weight against the true remaining share:

| candidate weight | correlation with truth |
|---|---|
| original draw count (`orig_drop_weight`) | **0.812** |
| `orig_drop_weight − circulation_count` | **0.239** |

**Subtracting circulation makes the estimate substantially WORSE, and the reason is structural: `circulation_count >= orig_drop_weight` on 26,133 of 26,143 rows (99.96%).** Pack-pool editions are **not pack-exclusive** — an edition's minted circulation accumulates across many packs and non-pack sources, so it carries no information about how much of *this* pack's allocation is left. The subtraction is almost always clamped at zero. **The whole class of circulation-derived or observed-serial-derived depletion estimators is dead for the same reason**, and it cannot be rescued for Pinnacle either: Top Shot is the only collection with ground truth to validate against, so a Pinnacle-specific variant would be unvalidatable by construction. **Do not re-propose inferring pack depletion from circulation or observed serials.**

⚠ **METHODOLOGICAL NOTE worth keeping, because it explains an apparent contradiction in this thread.** Original weights correlate **0.812** with true remaining at the row level, yet the earlier measurement found original-supply weighting carries **~101% mean absolute error** on the FMV-weighted mean that `gross_ev` actually uses. Both are correct. EV is dominated by the high-FMV tail — precisely the chase editions that deplete first and whose remaining share collapses fastest — so a weighting can track the bulk of the pool well and still be catastrophically wrong about the money. **Judge a remaining proxy by the FMV-weighted quantity EV consumes, never by weight correlation.** A 0.81 correlation would have looked like a green light.

**Revert:** `git revert <sha>`.

### 2026-07-31 (Cowork, interactive — "do what's best for RPC") — MEASURED a validated tier-scaled remaining basis and, more importantly, **quantified how wrong original-supply weighting is** using Top Shot ground truth. Docs-only; no prod/DB state change, no deploy.

**Starting point: every Top Shot distribution already carries publisher `remaining_by_tier`.** `topshot_pack_supply` has it for all **2,039** TS dists (`supply_ok`, ~16h fresh) — including all 679 with no drop pool, all 544 `original_supply_mislabelled`, and all 33 `placeholder_uniform`. That is authoritative publisher remaining data sitting unused on 1,325 dists / **148,163 sealed packs**.

**METHOD — tier-scaled remaining.** For edition `e` in tier `T` of a dist: `weight_e = orig_drop_weight_e × (remaining_by_tier[T] / original_by_tier[T])`, then normalize. It reconstructs a per-edition remaining distribution from original weights plus per-tier depletion.

**VALIDATED ON GROUND TRUTH, not asserted.** Tested on the 423 multi-tier dists where `pool_source='gql'` gives true per-edition `remaining`, comparing the weighted-mean FMV (the `gross_ev` basis) under each weighting:

| weighting | mean abs error vs truth |
|---|---|
| original-supply (`orig_drop_weight`) | **101.5%** |
| tier-scaled | **26.8%** |

Tier-scaled is closer on **299/423 (70.7%)** of dists — a **3.8× error reduction**.

⚠ **THE HEADLINE IS THE FIRST ROW, NOT THE SECOND: original-supply weighting carries ~101% mean absolute error against true remaining on multi-tier packs.** **AllDay, Golazos and Pinnacle are ALL on original-supply weighting.** This re-establishes the "AllDay EV is materially overstated" concern on sound footing after the earlier $523-vs-$65.63 evidence was correctly invalidated by the attribution-capture confound — and it does so **without touching AllDay data at all**, so the capture confound cannot contaminate it. Caveat carried honestly: measured on Top Shot pack structures; AllDay pack composition differs, so treat ~101% as "large and directionally established", not as AllDay's exact figure.

**ADDRESSABLE FOOTPRINT TODAY IS MODEST — stated plainly so this is not oversold.** Tier-scaling only discriminates on **multi-tier** dists, and 1,233 TS dists (351,833 sealed packs) are **single-tier**, where it collapses to a uniform rescale of the original weights and adds nothing. Applying it where a pool exists but is original-basis:
- `original_supply_mislabelled`: 544 dists → **78 multi-tier**, 9,090 sealed packs, **0 currently publishing EV** (latent correctness only).
- `placeholder_uniform`: 33 dists → **30 multi-tier**, 7,464 sealed packs, **30 currently publishing** — and these render **NULL** today, so tier-scaling would turn "no number" into a defensible number. That is the one immediate user-visible win.

**NOT SHIPPED, deliberately.** Changing how `gross_ev` is weighted is pricing logic, and per the standing rule (`data fixes OK; pricing LOGIC → hand off`) it needs a human diffing the EV output before/after. Nothing here is shelf-ware: the method, its validation numbers and the exact applicable dist sets are recorded so the change can be made in one pass with a known expected effect. **Do not apply tier-scaling to single-tier dists** — it is a no-op there and would only add false precision.

**Revert:** `git revert <sha>`.

### 2026-07-31 (Cowork, interactive — resolved the "does the TS attribution gap matter?" question with measurement) — MEASURED, deliberately NOT shipped. Docs-only; no prod/DB state change, no deploy.

I flip-flopped twice on whether the 174k Top Shot moments-hydrator backlog is the Pack EV critical path. Settling it with numbers rather than a third opinion.

**It is a coverage issue, not a correctness catastrophe.** Top Shot pull capture is **92.6% mean** on recent packs (n=4,000 rips; 3,666 fully captured, 282 zero-capture) — nothing like the AllDay 0.31–0.91 pulls/pack confound that invalidated the earlier bias claim. And the realized MV already excludes the worst rows: `mv_topshot_pack_rip_values` filters `pr.pull_value_usd IS NOT NULL`, so only **0.1%** (29/37,367) of its rows are zero-valued.

**But it is not clean either: 14.3% of the MV's rips are PARTIALLY captured** (sampled n=3,000, mean capture **0.9230**), so their `pull_value_usd` is a partial sum of the pack's true value, and those rows feed `realized_mean` / `realized_median` → `calibrated_ev` (up to 0.85 weight) → the anon-readable `v_topshot_pack_ev_calibrated`.

⚠ **THE RESULT IS DIRECTION-SURPRISING, WHICH IS WHY NOTHING SHIPPED.** The obvious fix — restrict the MV to fully-captured rips (`attributed >= moments_pulled`) — was expected to raise realized values by recovering understated packs. Measured, it moves the per-dist mean **DOWN 7.35% (−$0.38)** and costs **19 of 184 qualifying dists** (184 → 165 at the `n_opens >= 10` gate). Plausible reading: a pack whose every moment is still attributable is a pack nobody moved — i.e. a low-value pack — so the capture effect and a selection effect point in **opposite** directions and this measurement cannot separate them.

**DO NOT ship the "keep only fully-captured rips" fix on this evidence.** It is a 7.35% shift of unproven sign-correctness that also drops 10% of covered distributions, and validating it needs exactly the realized-vs-actual ground truth we lack. Separating the two effects needs a capture-ratio-stratified comparison against packs with independent value evidence (e.g. secondary sale of the sealed pack), not a filter.

**Net effect on priorities:** the Top Shot hydrator deploy stays worth doing for coverage and for the ~173,500 Apr–May rows that are unreachable by construction, but it is **correctly ranked below** the publisher-side remaining-pool items — which is what the original 2026-07-31 handoff said before I talked myself out of it. **Revert:** `git revert <sha>`.

### 2026-07-31 (Cowork, interactive — correction of my own correction) — RETRACTS three claims from the entry below and records the real, structural cause. Docs-only; no prod/DB state change, no deploy.

My previous entry correctly killed the "hydrator gates AllDay attribution" chain, then **replaced it with a wrong diagnosis of my own.** Retracting precisely:

- ❌ **"`allday-edition-resolver` is silently no-op'ing."** WRONG. It is not a pipeline — it is a *synthetic* `pipeline_runs` row written by the AllDay **sales** indexer ([app/api/allday-sales-indexer/route.ts:61,1095](app/api/allday-sales-indexer/route.ts#L1095)) for its inline **edition-CATALOG-fill** stage. `editions_hydrated_from_chain/relay` count new rows upserted into `editions` for editions first seen in that tick's sales. `0` means "no new AllDay editions needed" — **correct and healthy** on a complete catalog. It has **zero bearing on pack-pull attribution**. Two systems both named "resolve edition"; I conflated them.
- ❌ **"`get_allday_unresolved_pulls` has zero callers / the drain was never wired."** WRONG. It is called by the **deployed-but-ungitted** edge fn `resolve-allday-pull-editions`, driven by **pg_cron jobid 22 `rpc-allday-resolve-pull-editions` (`9,39 * * * *`, active)** — `cron.job_run_details`: **1,055 succeeded**, 7 failed (`job startup timeout`, last 07-25), latest success 2026-08-01 01:39Z. The drain runs fine and has for weeks.
- ❌ **"Fix that resolver, not a worker deploy."** WRONG target — nothing there is broken.

⚠ **DURABLE — a repo grep CANNOT see a pg_cron→HTTP caller of an ungitted edge function.** "Zero callers in the repo" ≠ "no caller." **Check `cron.job` before declaring any function dead.** The 07-31 revoke migration's own comment (`get_allday_unresolved_pulls(int) <- NO caller at all`) made the same error; the revoke itself is harmless (the edge fn calls with the service role — verified: the drain succeeded again *after* the revoke), but the reasoning was unsound and would not be for a wider grant.

**THE ACTUAL CAUSE — structural, not fixable by wiring or a deploy.** `resolve-allday-pull-editions` resolves a pull by **borrowing the moment at its open block** via Flow REST `/v1/scripts`. Forward pulls sit inside Flow's execution-state window, so they resolve → **100%**. Deep-history pulls do not: rest-mainnet **prunes execution state**, and `spork-proxy` fronts only `/v1/events` and `/v1/transactions`, **not `/v1/scripts`** ([supabase/functions/ingest-allday-pack-opens/index.ts:115-130](supabase/functions/ingest-allday-pack-opens/index.ts#L115-L130)). Historical rows therefore resolve only in the residual case where the moment is still borrowable today — which is exactly the observed **6.2–22.1%** on backfilled rows. Neither ingest mode writes `edition_id` at all ([index.ts:265-268,307-312](supabase/functions/ingest-allday-pack-opens/index.ts#L265-L268)) — the paths are byte-identical, so forward-vs-backfill is entirely a resolvability difference, not a code difference.

**Local sources are exhausted, now confirmed on a fourth table.** Of 293,274 still-NULL moments: `moments` **0**, `wmc` **95**, `nft_edition_map` **114**. Nothing left to mine in-database.

**CONSEQUENCE FOR THE PROGRAM (the thing that actually matters):** an opens-derived AllDay remaining pool can realistically only ever be built from **2026-01-01 onward**. Pre-2026 pull-level attribution is largely **unrecoverable**, so any AllDay remaining-pool model must either scope to 2026+ opens or carry an explicit coverage disclosure. Do not plan around "finish the AllDay attribution backfill" — it does not finish.

**WHAT STILL STANDS from the retracted entry** (re-verified, unchanged): the hydrator is **Top Shot only** (`TOPSHOT_COLLECTION_ID` hardcoded, [index.ts:84,122,238](workers/topshot-moments-hydrator/index.ts#L84)) and cannot attribute an AllDay pull; AllDay forward attribution is **100%** with a clean **2026-01-01** cutover (Jan 2026+ 0.0% NULL, May–Dec 2025 66–88%); the NULL count is **self-replenishing** as `allday-pack-opens-backfill` walks 2025 at 6–22% attribution; and **no `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` gates AllDay attribution** — the TS hydrator deploy gates only Top Shot pull provenance / realized-EV calibration.

**Monitoring gap noted, not shipped:** `resolve-allday-pull-editions` writes **no `pipeline_runs` row**, so a silent failure there would be invisible to `detect_stalled_pipelines()`; it is observable only via `cron.job_run_details` jobid 22 or the NULL-rate trend. **Revert:** `git revert <sha>`.

Values are NOT recoverable from `raw` (never delivered).

A population shift cannot make the same serials lose prices on re-measurement. (2) **The `0` -> `null` semantic switch:** pre-07-27 upstream ALWAYS sent a value — literal `"0"` for never-sold, a number for sold, with **zero** JSON nulls; nulls then appear progressively (2,054 -> 5,845 -> 100%). ### 2026-07-31 (Cowork, interactive — "what's the status of Pack Open history?" → full remaining-pool audit) — SHIPPED 2 DB-only items: an AllDay pack-pull edition-attribution backfill (37.2% → 49.3%) and `v_pack_remaining_basis`, the per-dist instrument that says whether a pack's remaining-pull pool can be trusted. No deploy, no code change.

Trevor's framing was that pack-open history feeds "what's still in the packs." **It mostly doesn't, and establishing that was the audit's main value.** Remaining-pull pools come from the PUBLISHER (`packEditionsV3 { count remaining }`), not from our on-chain opens — and only Top Shot models remaining at all. Headline: of 1,398 distributions currently serving a live Pack EV, **only 390 (27.9%) have a trustworthy remaining pool.**

**SHIPPED 1 — `audit_20260801_allday_pull_edition_backfill_stage` + `_apply` (DB-only).** `allday_pack_pull.edition_id` was NULL on 372,454 of 593,021 rows (37.2% attributed), which is the binding constraint on any opens-derived AllDay remaining pool. Backfilled 65,430 moments / **+72,143 rows from local sources only** (wmc preferred, then collection-scoped `sales`), fill-only, zero ambiguous. Attribution now **49.3%**. ⚠ **METHOD NOTE, and the trap that nearly produced a false P0:** I first measured the derivation against the 220,567 rows that already had an `edition_id` and got **94.2% agreement**, with `sales` apparently wrong 13% of the time — which would have meant AllDay FMV was contaminated. It was **my query that was wrong, not the data**: I joined `sales` on `nft_id` WITHOUT `collection_id`, and Flow nft_ids are per-collection sequences that COLLIDE across collections. Collection-scoped, the three sources agree **100.00%** (n=1,503 three-way). **Durable: never join `sales`/`wallet_moments_cache` on `nft_id`/`moment_id` alone — always scope by `collection_id`.** Distrust the instrument before the system. **Revert:** `UPDATE public.allday_pack_pull p SET edition_id = NULL FROM public.audit_20260801_allday_pull_edition_backfill a WHERE p.moment_nft_id = a.moment_nft_id AND p.edition_id = a.edition_id;`

**SHIPPED 2 — `audit_20260801_v_pack_remaining_basis` (DB-only, additive view).** One row per distribution giving `remaining_basis` in {`publisher_remaining`, `original_supply`, `original_supply_mislabelled`, `placeholder_uniform`, `depleted`, `none`} plus a boolean `remaining_trustworthy` and a `basis_note`. `security_invoker = on`, anon/authenticated REVOKED, service_role SELECT. Deliberately cheap — no `pack_rips` scan (DB time is the binding constraint). Live read: TS **390 trustworthy** / 324 `pool incomplete (sum drop_weight < 0.5)` / 544 `original_supply_mislabelled` / 69 depleted / 33 uniform-placeholder / 679 no pool; AllDay 2,950 + Golazos 210 `original_supply`; Pinnacle 143 `none`. **Revert:** `DROP VIEW IF EXISTS public.v_pack_remaining_basis;`

**FINDINGS (measured, not shipped — full detail in [docs/handoff-2026-07-31-pack-remaining-pool.md](docs/handoff-2026-07-31-pack-remaining-pool.md)):**
- **The hydrator backlog is structurally UNREACHABLE, not slow.** `v_moments_needing_hydration` has no attempt/failure column, and the worker reads it `ORDER BY acquired_date DESC LIMIT 300`. Unresolvable nft_ids never leave the view, so they occupy the queue head permanently — the top-300 window spans only ~3.5 days and **~173,500 rows (Apr–May 2026) are never fetched at all**. Fix is an attempt-tracking column + least-recently-tried ordering (worker + wrangler deploy, so not shippable from Cowork).
- **Top Shot on-chain opens can NEVER be the remaining basis:** observed rips 762,082 vs publisher-opened 16,837,027 = **4.5%** (our TS rip history starts 2023-09-29; TS packs start 2020). Publisher remaining is the only viable TS source — correct as built.
- **AllDay opens ARE trustworthy at pack level:** observed rips 1,599,984 vs publisher-opened 1,599,257 = **100.0%** across 2,910/3,012 dists. So an opens-derived AllDay remaining pool is viable once pull attribution is high enough — the one place pack-open history genuinely unlocks remaining.
- **AllDay EV is overstated because it is original-supply weighted.** `compute-allday-pack-ev` weights by `circulation_count` and never queries `remaining`, while `app/api/allday-pack-ev/route.ts` DOES use `packEditionsV3 { remaining }` — **two different EV models on the same collection.** Real consumer packs show the bias: Grail Seekers Legendary dist 7073 `gross_ev` **$523 vs realized median $65.63** (n=124).
- **`pack_ev_latest` is publishing internal Dapper reserve packs.** AllDay dist 5730 "NFL Pack Hold - Genesis" carries `pack_price` **$999,999** and `gross_ev` **$900,000**; several "Holding Pack" rows sit at $9,999. These alone drive AllDay's average `gross_ev` to $1,880 vs `typical_ev` $14.18. Not purchasable — should be filtered off the EV surface.
- **Atlas pool (57 TS dists) stale since 2026-07-17** yet EV recomputes off it hourly. `gql_historical` (544 dists) writes `count/totalCount` — original mint share — but the RPC reports it as `ev_basis='remaining'`; currently latent (0 live EV rows) but a mislabel waiting to surface.

### 2026-07-31 (Claude Code, interactive — handoff round 7 "do all you can") — SHIPPED: resolved the never-validated SECDEF allowlist BASELINE — 45 revokes, 4 kept with real per-function reasons. Client-executable SECDEF 49→**4**, client-executable WRITERS →**0**. DB-only, no deploy.
`audit_20260731_revoke_45_service_role_only_secdef_rpcs_and_justify_the_4_kept`. The round-7 handoff's real finding was that the sentinel is fine but its *baseline* was a bulk import — all 49 rows carried the identical note `baseline 2026-07-20 (handoff item 4)`, so nothing had ever answered "was 07-20 safe?". This resolves every row against its actual callers. **METHOD (exhaustive, repo-side):** every literal `.rpc("name")` site, every **dynamic** `.rpc(var)` site, every direct `/rest/v1/rpc/` fetch, and all of `components/**` — then, per site, *which client*. ⚠ **THE DURABLE TRAP THAT DROVE THE WHOLE RESULT: in this repo an identifier named `supabase` is USUALLY THE SERVICE-ROLE CLIENT.** `lib/supabase.ts` exports both (`supabase` = anon, `supabaseAdmin` = service role), but **9+ files import `supabaseAdmin as supabase`**, and several API routes build their own `createClient(url, SERVICE_ROLE_KEY)` and name it `supabase`. So "called via `supabase`" proves nothing and "server-side" ≠ "service role" — **resolve the binding, never the name.** Doing so showed the entire browser/anon + session RPC surface is **exactly TWO functions**, and `components/**` makes **ZERO** direct `.rpc()` calls. **KEPT (4), each note rewritten from the bulk string to a real reason:** `get_trophy_slab_data_by_username` (anon — genuinely read via `supabaseAnon`), `get_my_fan_teams` (authenticated — session client, `auth.uid()`-scoped), and **`serial_fmv_estimate` ×2 — kept for a NON-OBVIOUS reason: it is reached INDIRECTLY through the SECURITY INVOKER fn `get_wallet_moments_with_fmv` and the anon-SELECTable `security_invoker` view `topshot_underpriced_serials_board`. An invoker caller runs the callee AS THE CALLER, so revoking would have broken the wallet-moments read and a public board.** ⚠ **Generalize that: a direct-caller sweep is NOT sufficient for a SECDEF revoke — check invoker-mode callers (functions AND views) too.** **REVOKED (45)** — every caller service-role. Verified: client-exec SECDEF **49→4**, anon-exec **27→3**, allowlist **49→4**, bulk-baseline notes **0**, client-executable writers **2→0**; `check_secdef_anon_exec_drift()` `[]`, invariants 0, anon-write 0; **functional probe** (`SET LOCAL ROLE`) → anon **blocked** on a revoked fn, service_role **still executes**, anon **still works** on a kept fn; **smoke-tests.yml run 30675877893 `success`** after the revoke. Bodies untouched → all SQL pins + drift guard unaffected. **Revert:** `GRANT EXECUTE ON FUNCTION public.<sig> TO anon, authenticated;` for any of the 45 sigs in the migration + re-INSERT its allowlist row + `git revert <sha>`.

### 2026-07-31 (Claude Code, interactive — round 5 cont.) — SHIPPED: closed the Candy zero-price hole at its real cause (a ROUNDING artifact, not a missing price), instrumented the drain route per-step, and fixed a documented date command that silently returns the wrong timezone on this box

Three follow-ons after item 25. Route + test + docs only — **no migration, no DB function change, no data mutation** (the 3 existing zero-price rows are untouched; this stops the 4th).

- **CANDY ZERO-PRICE — root cause found, and it is NOT a missing price** (`app/api/candy-sales-indexer/route.ts`). The writer already guarded `price <= 0` **on the SOL amount**, so the handoff's "add a guard in the `solana_das` writer" would have landed on a check that was already there and changed nothing. The actual hole: `price_usd` is `Number((price * rate).toFixed(2))` — the ROUNDED value — so a positive-but-dust SOL amount still writes `0.00`. Confirmed against the live row, not inferred: `price_native = 0.00000100` SOL (one microSOL) × ~$76 = **$0.000076 → "0.00"**. Fix guards the **rounded** value (`if (!(priceUsd > 0)) return { skip: DUST_SKIP }`), which filters sub-half-cent dust by construction with no invented threshold, and computes `priceUsd` **once** so the `sales` and `candy_pack_sales` paths cannot drift apart. Also fires **before** the DAS lookup, so dust costs no asset budget.
- **Dust is closed TERMINALLY, not parked forever.** New `TERMINAL_SKIPS = {pack_asset, dust_price_rounds_to_zero}` generalizes the existing `PACK_SKIP` close-out at both park sites. Without this the dust row would re-enter the dead letter every tick and burn drain budget until `MAX_PARK_ATTEMPTS` — the same "recycled forever" class as items 21–22. Dust can never become non-dust, so retrying it is pure waste.
- **POSITIVE-CONTROLLED.** New test in `api-candy-sales-indexer-deep.test.ts` (0.000001 SOL × 150) asserts no `sales` row, park reason `dust_price_rounds_to_zero`, the terminal close-out, `rows_skipped: 1`, and `asset_fetches: 0`. **Verified it actually fails without the guard**: `expected [...] to have a length of +0 but got 1` — i.e. the dust row lands in `sales`. 15/15 green.
- **DRAIN ROUTE — per-step timing (`extra.step_ms`).** The route sits near its 300s `maxDuration` (313s/257s timeouts 07-28/29) and I just added load to it, yet the only timeout signal was **one `duration_ms` covering nine steps** — enough to know it timed out, never which step. Added an additive `mark()` after each step (no step restructured) so a near-ceiling tick names its own culprit. Test asserts the keys reach the envelope. Also corrected the file header, which still claimed the knot step was "≤5/run" and that knots "surface at ~1/day" — both wrong, and the pair of them is what made the divergence look designed.
- **⚠ DURABLE — `TZ=America/Los_Angeles date` SILENTLY RETURNS UTC on Trevor's Windows box.** That Git Bash has **no `/usr/share/zoneinfo`**, so every zone prints the same time labelled `GMT` (verified: `America/Los_Angeles`, `America/New_York`, `Asia/Tokyo`, `UTC` all identical). CLAUDE.md and this ledger's own header both instruct sessions to run exactly that command before stamping a PT date — it fails silently, handing back a plausible timestamp 7h ahead, which is precisely the documented 07-29→07-30 boundary slip. **Use plain `date`** (correctly prints `PDT` here); in a UTC sandbox subtract 7h/8h from `date -u` by hand. ### 2026-07-31 (Claude Code, interactive — handoff round 5, item 25) — SHIPPED: the subedition knot drain was capped at 5/night against 1,441 candidates and an ~8.3/night arrival rate — raised to 100. The seeder was NOT the bottleneck.

Item 25 asked whether to widen `seed_topshot_collision_knot_targets`'s predicate or declare 862 mis-keyed moments a permanent floor. **Neither — both rest on a wrong premise.** The blocked queue is fully drainable; one hardcoded integer was holding it below its own arrival rate. Route + test only — **no migration, no DB function change, no manual data mutation**; the nightly cron does the work on its normal schedule.

- **ROOT CAUSE — `resolve_topshot_subedition_collision_knots` is called with `p_limit: 5`, hardcoded** ([app/api/admin/drain-conflated-subeditions/route.ts](../../app/api/admin/drain-conflated-subeditions/route.ts) step 6, set 2026-07-06 while the in-place permutation was new). **Measured 1,441 knot candidates available.** Arrival ~+8.3 blocked nfts/night vs a 5/night drain ⇒ the queue was **divergent, not slow** — the observed monotonic 833→840→849→858 is exactly `arrival − 5`. At the old cap the *existing* pool alone needed ~288 nights. **Raised to 100** (≈12× arrival ⇒ monotonically decreasing; existing pool ~11 nights).
- **⚠ The handoff's reading of `knots_resolved: 5 / knots_skipped: 0` was inverted, and it reads healthy either way.** `knots_skipped` counts only the per-record defensive re-check *inside* the loop; the `LIMIT greatest(1,p_limit)` binds `_knot_cand` **SELECTION before the loop**. So "0 skipped" never meant "processed everything it was given" — it meant none of the 5 it allowed itself to see were rejected. Same class as the 07-31 `edition_integrity_flags` metric: a number that cannot move looks like a healthy small number. **The nights_seen=1 evidence is also consistent with LIMIT 5 over a large pool, not only with an arrival rate of 5.**
- **The seeder is NOT the lever — measured, not argued.** Over the 853 then-blocked nfts: the blocking occupant Y **already had a RESOLVED subedition row in 841 (98.6%)**, so the seeder's `NOT EXISTS` gate correctly skips them and step 6 handles them directly (it derives its own candidates from `moments` + `topshot_moment_subeditions` and **does not read the seeder's queue at all**). Only ~12 were the unknown-occupant case the seeder exists for. Its other two gates (occupant `nft_id` numeric, occupant base int-keyed) excluded **ZERO**. Widening that predicate would have moved nothing. Step-1d's comment implied the dependency and has been corrected in place.
- **Also NOT a permanent floor.** 839 of 853 are exact mutual transpositions — X sits on `::N` with on-chain subedition 0, Y sits on the base with subedition N, same serial (617 confirmed exact 2-cycles). The swap primitive already exists and is proven: step 6 permutes via distinct transient serial parks (+3M/+4M), preserves serials, mirrors `sales`+`wmc`, and logs every move to `topshot_collision_knot_resolutions` (76 resolutions since 07-06, 0 skips).
- **⚠ Correction to my own in-flight finding:** I measured 9,689 moments base-keyed with `subedition_id > 0` and nearly reported them as an 11× undercount "structurally invisible" to the realigner. **Wrong** — `_realign` is deliberately one-directional (`::`-only) and its counterpart `remap_topshot_split_resolved_subeditions` (step 4) owns the base→`::N` direction. The pairing is complete; that population is the split's normal working set (`moments_split` 232–237/night). Caught by reading step 4 before writing it up.
- **Cost basis (this route runs near its 300s `maxDuration` — 313s/257s timeouts 07-28/29, 171s/201s since):** candidate selection is a **fixed ~1.83s regardless of p_limit** (`EXPLAIN ANALYZE` at LIMIT 200; dominated by parallel seq scans over `moments` ~292k and `topshot_moment_subeditions` ~352k), and each knot is ~15 indexed single-row statements ⇒ 100 adds only a few seconds against ~99s headroom. **Chose 100 not 200 to protect that headroom.**
- **Regression guard + POSITIVE CONTROL.** `__tests__/api-admin-drain-conflated-subeditions.test.ts` now records RPC args and asserts the knot `p_limit >= 50` (a rate that beats arrival — retuning stays free, a silent revert to a starving value reds CI) plus the load-bearing step 4 → 4b → 6 ordering. **Verified it actually fails**: reverted to 5 → `expected 5 to be greater than or equal to 50`, then restored. 4/4 green, tsc clean.
- **Watch the NEXT run — 2026-08-01 20:30 UTC = 13:30 PDT** (cron is `30 20 * * *` **UTC**, i.e. early afternoon PT, not overnight). ⚠ Today's 20:30Z run fired at 13:30 PDT, ~90 min BEFORE this shipped, so the 07-31 row already in `pipeline_runs` still shows `knots_resolved: 5` — that is the pre-change baseline, not a failure of the fix. Expect on 08-01: `knots_resolved` ≈ 100, `knots_skipped` still ~0, `realign.collisions_skipped` falling materially off 858 for the first time, `duration_ms` well under 300s. If duration approaches the ceiling, lower the limit — do not disable the step.
- **Revert:** `git revert <sha>` (restores `p_limit: 5` and the guard). No data migration to undo; every knot already resolved stays resolved and is individually reversible from `topshot_collision_knot_resolutions`.

### 2026-07-31 (Claude Code, interactive — handoff item 22) — SHIPPED: `promote_unmapped_sales()` stops mislabelling trigger-suppressed rows as tx-hash collisions (DB-only, no deploy); the "3 genuine dupes" from the item-21 entry were nothing of the kind

Drained item 22 of [docs/handoff-2026-07-31-sales-tx-index-round2.md]. DB-only + test/docs — no code deploy.

- **SHIPPED — `audit_20260731_promote_unmapped_sales_classify_cross_source_dedup`.** The drainer's outcome ladder was `promoted` / `already_in_sales` / ELSE `tx_hash_collision`. `public.sales` carries exactly one insert-SUPPRESSING trigger — `trg_zzz_allday_cross_source_dedup` (BEFORE INSERT, AllDay only) — which on finding a cross-source economic twin (same nft + calendar day + rounded price, different `source`) folds the incoming buyer/seller/serial into the twin and `RETURN NULL`s. **No error, zero rows inserted, and the twin sits under a DIFFERENT tx_hash**, so the row matched neither arm and fell to ELSE, got stamped `sales_tx_hash_unique_collision` + a 30-day recheck horizon, and would recycle forever. Added a fourth outcome, `merged_cross_source`, whose predicate mirrors the trigger's guard + economic key exactly (incl. the `COALESCE(source,'promoted_from_unmapped')` the INSERT applies); it is treated as RESOLVED because the sale IS recorded, on the twin. The ELSE arm survives, renamed to what it now actually asserts: `insert_vanished` / marker `sales_insert_vanished_unexplained` / run key `blocked_insert_vanished` (old key `blocked_tx_hash_collision` had **zero code consumers**, docs only).
- **⚠ CORRECTS the item-21 entry above:** its "3 genuine same-(tx,nft) dupes correctly re-blocked" were not dupes. Verified: each of the 3 had **0** rows in `sales` sharing its tx_hash and exactly **1** cross-source dedup twin. Nothing was wrong with the index fix — the drainer's label was wrong.
- **Blast radius measured before shipping: exactly 3 rows / $273**, the same 3. Query over the entire unresolved backlog for AllDay rows with a cross-source twin returns 3, so this resolves no one else's rows by surprise.
- **Also cleared the 3 stale `sales_tx_hash_unique_collision` markers** (the 30-day horizon would otherwise have kept them out of the candidate CTE until 2026-08-30). Verified after: `promote_unmapped_sales(allday)` → `eligible 3 / merged_cross_source 3 / blocked_insert_vanished 0`, **ok=true**, all 3 now `resolved_at` set with no marker. `v_sales_tx_collision_loss` → **0 rows** (all three causes). anon/authenticated EXECUTE still false, service_role true; `check_public_security_invariants()` 0.
- **Also re-pinned the DB invariant, which had gone stale.** `__tests__/db-invariants-drift-guard.test.ts` still pointed `promote_unmapped_sales` at the **2026-04-27** migration, so `supabase/tests/promote_unmapped_sales.sql` had been validating a definition superseded on 2026-07-27 (no FIX 1/2/3, no price guard, no recheck horizon, no path-4 wmc resolution). Rewrote the test against the live shape — 10 fixture rows covering all four outcomes plus the 0-price guard and the horizon skip — and installed `allday_sales_cross_source_dedup` **verbatim** (not stubbed) so the suppression path is genuinely exercised; added it as its own pin. Drift guard **42/42 green**. `npx tsc --noEmit` clean.
- **⚠ The SQL test could NOT be run locally this session** — this Windows box has no Postgres binaries and no Docker (the "sandbox can run the DB harness" note in CLAUDE.md is the *cloud* sandbox). Its first real execution was CI's **blocking** `db-tests` job, which **caught a fixture bug on the first run** (`eligible` 1, want 6) and was fixed in a follow-up commit. Root cause, worth keeping: **a `NULL` `resolution_hint` makes a row uncandidatable.** The horizon guard is `NOT (hint ? 'promote_recheck_after' AND (…)::timestamptz > now())`; with a NULL hint both operands are NULL, so `NOT (NULL AND NULL)` is NULL and the row silently fails the WHERE. **Inert in production — 0 of 93,734 live `unmapped_sales` rows have a NULL hint** — so this is a fixture-realism rule, not a defect: fixtures must use `'{}'::jsonb`, never NULL.

The marker clear is not worth reverting (markers are re-derivable, and the rows are now legitimately resolved).
### 2026-07-31 (Claude Code, interactive — handoff item 21) — SHIPPED: `public.sales` can finally store a multi-item transaction (DB-only, no deploy); 386 blocked AllDay sales promoted; the handoff's plan was incomplete and its payoff was ~29× overstated

Drained item 21 of [docs/handoff-2026-07-31-sales-tx-index.md] (the "sales unique index cannot represent a multi-item transaction" handoff). Trevor authorized the one-way schema change after being shown the corrected numbers. **DB-only — no code change was needed and none was made, so no deploy.**

- **SHIPPED — `audit_20260731_sales_tx_unique_admits_multi_item_transactions`.** `idx_sales_tx_hash` was `UNIQUE (transaction_hash, sold_at)`, and every item of one purchase shares both → `public.sales` could hold **exactly one row per transaction**, silently dropping every item but the first of a bulk buy. Replaced with `idx_sales_tx_nft_sold` = `UNIQUE (transaction_hash, nft_id, sold_at) NULLS NOT DISTINCT WHERE transaction_hash IS NOT NULL`. `sold_at` is mandatory (sales is `RANGE (sold_at)`-partitioned); `NULLS NOT DISTINCT` (PG 17.6) preserves the OLD strictness for the 15,951 legacy `nft_id IS NULL` rows (a 2026-03-23..30 backfill artifact; **0 in the last 90d**, no live writer produces them) which plain btree would have stopped deduping. All 8 partition children built `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY` first, then `ATTACH`ed, so no blocking rebuild.
- **⚠ THE HANDOFF'S PLAN WOULD HAVE BEEN A NO-OP FOR LIVE SALES — it named only the parent index.** `sales_2026` also carried a **second, standalone, parent-less** `sales_2026_transaction_hash_unique_idx` on `(transaction_hash)` ALONE — *stricter* than the parent (one row per tx regardless of `sold_at`). `sales_2026` had **0** multi-row transactions, confirming it bound. Dropped in the same migration. **Durable: when widening a partitioned index, enumerate per-partition indexes too — a partition can carry its own unconstrained-by-the-parent unique index.**
- **⚠ This also REFUTES the 2026-07-26 handoff** ([docs/handoff-2026-07-26-db-saturation-and-allday-resolver.md](../handoff-2026-07-26-db-saturation-and-allday-resolver.md):224-228), which concluded widening "would not fix even those 32" because the parent rejects them regardless. That was right about the parent and wrong about the outcome: widening **both** works. Empirically — `sales` now holds **21 multi-item transactions / 48 rows**, structurally impossible before.
- **Drained:** cleared the 389 stale `promote_blocked = 'sales_tx_hash_unique_collision'` markers (each carried a useless 30-day recheck — the collision was structural, so they recycled forever, oldest 2026-01-24), then ran `promote_unmapped_sales(allday)` → **386 promoted / 389 eligible (99.2%)**, 3 genuine same-(tx,nft) dupes correctly re-blocked. Second run: 0 eligible. Landed **420 AllDay rows / 214 editions / $2,175.95**, 0 non-positive prices, 0 duplicate nft within a tx.
- **⚠ THE HANDOFF'S NUMBERS WERE WRONG — do not reuse them.** It claimed 6,868 unstorable rows ≈ **$30,364**. Verified: 4,110 unstorable *priced* rows ($18,252), of which only **~188–420 could promote at all**. The other ~3,900 fail `promote_unmapped_sales`' **edition-resolution** gate, not the index — that's the separate on-chain backlog. Its "zero intra-transaction price variance" evidence also silently excluded the **25,154 zero-price rows** (n=4 groups tagged `v1_tx_decode_multi_nft_unsplittable` by `audit_20260725_allday_v1_unsplittable_retag`) which are ~78% of the multi-item population. Those can **never** promote — `promote_unmapped_sales` hard-guards `COALESCE(price_usd,0) > 0` ("a 0/NULL-price sale must never enter public.sales — it pollutes FMV"), so there was no FMV-poisoning risk from this change either way. Handoff's core *premise* (real per-item AllDay floor sweeps, $2–$8, prices don't scale with item count) re-verified and holds.
- **No code change required** — every `sales` writer uses a plain `.insert()` with a 23505 row-by-row fallback; **none** targets `ON CONFLICT (transaction_hash, sold_at)`, so nothing needed repointing. `promote_unmapped_sales`' `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` resolves against the new index and stays idempotent (same tx+nft+sold_at still conflicts).
- **FOLLOW-UP (queued, not shipped):** `resolve_sales_ingest_unresolved()` still collapses `DISTINCT ON (tx_hash, sold_at)` + guards `NOT EXISTS (sales WHERE tx=… AND sold_at=…)` — it was written *to conform to* the narrow index and will still under-insert one row per transaction. **Harmless today: 0 runs in 30d** (the Dune settlement ingest is inert; its cron was retired 07-28). Widen to `(tx_hash, nft_id)` if that lane is ever revived.
- **Verified after:** `check_public_security_invariants()` 0 · `check_pgcron_recent_failures()` 0 · `v_rpc_trust_health` **23/23 ok, 0 breaches** · all 9 new indexes `indisvalid` · `promote_unmapped_sales` 1372/1372 ok/30d.
- **⚠ REVERT IS EFFECTIVELY ONE-WAY (Trevor was told this before authorizing).** `DROP INDEX public.idx_sales_tx_nft_sold;` then recreate the narrow pair — **but the narrow UNIQUE cannot be recreated while the 48 multi-item rows exist**; they must be deleted first (they are legitimate sales, so deleting them re-destroys real data). Reversing also means re-marking the 386 promoted rows. Full revert SQL:
  `DELETE FROM public.sales s USING (SELECT transaction_hash, sold_at FROM public.sales WHERE transaction_hash IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1,2 HAVING count(*)>1) d WHERE s.transaction_hash=d.transaction_hash AND s.sold_at=d.sold_at AND s.ctid <> (SELECT min(ctid) FROM public.sales x WHERE x.transaction_hash=d.transaction_hash AND x.sold_at=d.sold_at);`
  then `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX idx_sales_tx_hash ON ONLY public.sales USING btree (transaction_hash, sold_at) WHERE (transaction_hash IS NOT NULL);` (+ per-partition children + ATTACH) and `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX sales_2026_transaction_hash_unique_idx ON public.sales_2026 USING btree (transaction_hash) WHERE (transaction_hash IS NOT NULL);` finally `DROP INDEX public.idx_sales_tx_nft_sold;`

### 2026-07-29 (Claude Code, interactive) — SHIPPED: `unmapped_resolution_backlog_max` given a 24h grace period so it measures failure-to-resolve, not pipeline latency; the handoff's proposed resolver fix was REFUTED and deliberately NOT shipped

Drained [docs/handoff-2026-07-30-allday-resolver-starvation.md](../handoff-2026-07-30-allday-resolver-starvation.md) (mis-dated 07-30; PT 07-29). - **SHIPPED — `audit_20260729_unmapped_backlog_metric_24h_grace` (DB-only).** The arm counted every unresolved priced sale in the trailing 30d, **including rows sold minutes ago the resolver had not yet reached**. Fresh AllDay sales resolve at **p50 6.6 min / p99 34 min**, so a high-volume day (283 arrivals 07-29 vs 74 on 07-28) put its own in-flight tail into the metric and breached at 106 **while the resolver was fully healthy** (93/93 ok runs, 961 rows resolved/24h, 85–100% of fresh sales resolved per day). Added `AND us.sold_at < now() - '24:00:00'` — **40× p99**, so it cannot mask a stall, while giving the slower wmc/wallet-walk promote path (Leg A, observed max 73h) a fair chance. Chosen at the empirical knee: the metric reads **62 at 24h/36h/48h/72h alike**, so 24h is exactly where in-flight ends and genuine residual begins. **`breach_at` stays 100 — the measurement was fixed, the alarm was NOT loosened.** Now reads 62, ok; view still 23 metrics, **0 breaches**. **POSITIVE CONTROL: a 1-day resolver stall would read 136 → still BREACHES**, so detection is preserved (this is the [[probe-null-results-need-a-positive-control]] rule applied to a metric fix — reading `ok` proves nothing without it). Rebuilt from `pg_get_viewdef` via **guarded literal replace that RAISEs unless each target is found exactly once** (so a whitespace miss aborts instead of silently no-opping), other 22 arms byte-identical, `security_invoker=on` re-asserted (CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW wipes reloptions — third time this has mattered). anon/authenticated SELECT re-verified `false` functionally via `has_table_privilege`. **Revert:** re-run the same guarded replace swapping `v_old_pred`/`v_new_pred` (and the `catches` text) to drop the `sold_at < now() - '24:00:00'` clause, then `ALTER VIEW public.v_rpc_trust_health SET (security_invoker = on);`
- **NOT shipped — the handoff's 60/40 candidate-budget split would have made the breach WORSE.** The metric counts only `sold_at > now() - 30 days` ("aged residual excluded ... signals NEW stalls not the historical floor"), so the six-month tail it proposed draining contributes **zero** to it. Spending 40% of `ON_CHAIN_MAX` on `sold_at ASC` diverts budget away from the only rows the metric counts. **DO NOT re-suggest this fix for this metric.**
- **The starvation mechanism does not exist.** (a) Handoff's headline figures (55,047 unresolved / 40,384 never-attempted) **omit the route's own `price_usd > 0` filter** — true queue is **28,044 / 14,116**; the 27,002-row difference is `price_usd = 0`, structurally excluded from the route by design and unreachable by any ordering change. (b) **Zero fresh never-attempted rows exist** — the never-attempted frontier is `sold_at` **2026-07-26**, 3.5 days old, so nothing is jumping the queue; attempt-stamp buckets are 1,583 <6h / 3,898 6–24h / 8,447 1–3d with **nothing stuck past 3 days**. (c) Rotation runs at **6,782 stamps/24h** against a 14,116 never-attempted pool (drains in ~2.1 days); over a 14-day `REATTEMPT_AFTER_DAYS` cycle capacity is ~95k attempts vs 28k rows needing one — **3.4× oversupplied, not starved**. (d) `candidates` pinned at ~398 is **not** the stuck-window tell the handoff read it as — it is `LIMIT 400` minus nft_id dupes and reads ~398 whether or not rotation works. Both routes share this ordering ([tail route:121-122](../../app/api/cron/allday-resolve-unmapped-tail/route.ts#L121-L122)); neither was changed.
- **DURABLE LESSON — the mirror of [[green-pipeline-blind-to-its-own-work]]: a metric that counts IN-FLIGHT work fires on volume spikes, so the sentinel gets ignored exactly when it matters.** This one exists to catch the WAF-stall class that had AllDay undercounting ~16% (2026-06-16); noise-training it is the real risk. When a trust-health arm counts a backlog, check that its window excludes work that has not yet had a fair chance to complete — measure the pipeline's own p99 latency and set the floor well above it, rather than raising `breach_at` (a magic number that re-breaks as volume grows). The 15.5% overall per-attempt resolve rate is NOT evidence of a broken resolver: it is the aged tail (genuinely unresolvable — Dapper custody / storefront escrow, already proven on-chain) diluting an 85–100% fresh-sale rate.

Fix: `WITH x AS MATERIALIZED (…)`, the same decoupling the sibling `resolve_topshot_subedition_collision_knots` already does via a temp table; the outer join then probes BOTH index columns. **Measured: timeout/0 rows → 1,048 ms/96 rows; live call seeded 96 in 3.6s, second call 0 in 1.5s (idempotent).** This step had **never once succeeded** (0 of 3 retained runs carry `seeded_knot_occupants`). **Revert:** restore the prior body (inline subquery).

The two verification runs together drained the wmc backlog **82,277 → 80,107** (2,170 rows, 2,200 audited moves incl. sales); the rest is left to the nightly cron (~10 nights) rather than bulk-mutating 80k rows in one unobserved shot. ⚠ A `p_limit=2000` attempt appeared to "time out" first — that was the **MCP session's own short default `statement_timeout`, not the function's 300s**; the statement rolled back whole (verified 0 audit rows from it, no partial state). **Revert:** drop the `AND ( EXISTS … )` block from `_split`. **Data revert:** `audit_20260704_subedition_split_remap` holds every move.
- **ANSWERED the handoff's ⚠ frozen-selection-window check — it was right, but on the wrong metric.** `knots_resolved: 5` is **NOT** frozen: `topshot_collision_knot_resolutions` holds **66 rows / 66 distinct `x_nft_id`** (zero repeats), up from the handoff's 51 = exactly 3 nights × 5 — the identical 5 is the `p_limit=5` cap binding, i.e. real progress. But `wmc_realigned: 5` **IS** genuinely stuck: the same nfts (45867565, 50280489, 50296355, 50983490) were realigned **4 nights running**. Natural experiment in the data: rows on Trevor's constantly-walked `0xbd94cade097e50ac` get reverted (`last_seen_at` minutes old, `edition_key` back to the wrong `::16`), while the same nft on the cold `0xceee47cd6ce5e043` (`last_seen_at` 06-10) **stayed fixed**. So a wallet-walk wmc writer overwrites `edition_key` after the realign corrects it. Only **4 rows** in this direction, so it is an infinite loop of trivial scale — NOT fixed here (it needs a wmc write-path change, which is ingest-adjacent and deserves its own scoped pass). **QUEUED: WMC-REALIGN-VS-WALLET-WALK-EDITION-KEY-LOOP.**
- **Durable lesson (third instance of this class this month):** a trailing `LIMIT` is not a bound. It bounds work only when the result set is at least as large as the limit — on a rare-event search it degenerates to a full scan, and on an already-drained queue it samples ~99% no-ops. Both of today's fixes are the same repair: push the actionable-row predicate INTO the candidate CTE so the LIMIT binds on work.

### 2026-07-29 (Claude Code, interactive — deep-dive bug sweep) — fixed a HIGH-severity IDOR write (profile/teams) + a Rules-of-Hooks crash in the Sets analytics dashboard

Two confirmed defects from parallel deep-dive agents (auth/wallet + analytics), each verified before fixing. Route + component only — NO prod/DB/deploy change (Vercel rebuilds).

- **SECURITY (HIGH) — `app/api/profile/teams/route.ts` IDOR write.** The POST handler had **no session check**: it read `ownerKey` from the request body, resolved it to a `user_id` via the PUBLIC `profile_bio.username`, then did a service-role (RLS-bypassing) delete-then-insert replace-all of that user's `user_favorite_teams`. Filtering the Sets dashboard to a collection whose series overview is empty (e.g. the Pinnacle chip → `analytics_sets_series_overview` returns `[]`) while the component stayed mounted threw React's "rendered fewer hooks than during the previous render", blanking the section. Fixed by moving the `useMemo` above the early return (hooks now unconditional).

### 2026-07-29 (Claude Code, interactive — wallet-capability handoff items 17 + 18) — made FCL wallet discovery SINGLE-OWNER (two modules were racing it on `/dashboard`), defaulted sign-in to self-custody, and gated the one live transacting surface on `v_wallet_capability_tier` with absence treated as UNKNOWN

Drained [docs/handoff-2026-07-29-wallet-capability.md](../handoff-2026-07-29-wallet-capability.md) items 17 + 18. **Code + tests only — no migration, no prod-DB mutation, no edge/worker deploy.** The DB half (`v_wallet_capability_tier`) was already shipped by Cowork; re-verified live this turn: anon SELECT **false**, authenticated SELECT **false**, `security_invoker=on`, `check_public_security_invariants()` **0 rows**, 239 addresses (95 advanced / 99 child / 45 standalone).

- **Item 17 — one owner for `discovery.wallet`.** `lib/chains/flow/flow.ts` wrote Dapper-restricted discovery from an **auto-init import side effect** while `lib/chains/flow/fcl-config.ts` wrote self-custody discovery behind its own guard; neither guard could see the other, so both endpoints shipped to `/dashboard` and the winner was import-order dependent. All `discovery.*` keys now live ONLY in `fcl-config.ts`, behind a new `configureFcl({ intent })`: **`sign-in` and `transact` → self-custody** (`fcl-discovery.onflow.org/authn`), and Dapper-restricted is reachable only via the explicit `dapper-custodial` intent, which **has zero callers** — correct, since a Dapper child cannot sign a withdraw. Removed `initFclSelfCustody` / `FLOW_SELF_CUSTODY_DISCOVERY`; `configureFclAuth()` kept as a deprecated alias. Callers repointed: `SignInWithDapper`, `dashboard/page.tsx` (verify-link), `useFlowUser.logIn` (was Dapper-custodial — now self-custody, per Trevor's ruling), `GiftClient` (→ `transact`).
- **⚠ CORRECTION to the handoff — do NOT "delete the bare `initFcl()`" as written; it would have broken ~14 server routes.** The auto-init is **load-bearing**: `app/api/{wallet-search,sales-indexer,cache-refresh,wallet-backfill,owned-flow-ids,cost-basis-*,allday-sets,allday-wallet-search,backfill-edition-names,cron/ownership-onchain-walk}/route.ts` + `lib/chains/flow/wallet-backfill-helpers.ts` all `import fcl from "@/lib/chains/flow/flow"` and call `fcl.query()` **without ever calling `initFcl()`** — they depend on the import to set `accessNode.api` + the `0x…` contract placeholders. So the side effect was **kept** and the *discovery* keys were removed from it instead: flow.ts is now chain-config-only. That preserves every server route AND kills the collision, which deleting the call would not have done.
- **⚠ CORRECTION — FCL has no allowlist primitive, so handoff point 5 ("pin the wallet allowlist") is not implementable as written.** `discovery.authn.include` only opts IN wallets Discovery hides by default; it does not restrict the list to its members. Both keys are forwarded verbatim to the Discovery **API** and filtered server-side (verified in `@onflow/fcl-core`'s `getServices`), so **`discovery.authn.exclude` is the only lever** that can remove an offered wallet. Shipped as `discovery.authn.exclude`, **empty by default** and driven by `NEXT_PUBLIC_FCL_DISCOVERY_EXCLUDE` (comma-separated) — deliberately not pre-populated, because excluding a guessed address would silently hide a working wallet and the target service's address has to be read off the live Discovery list in a browser. **Open operator step:** if a deprecated wallet is still offered, read its address off the live list and set that env var. Note the `blocto` string Trevor may have seen is inside FCL's own vendor bundle, not RPC config.
- **Item 18 — capability gating, absence ≠ read_only.** New `lib/wallet-capability.ts` (`getWalletCapability`, service-role read of the view) + `app/api/wallet/capability/route.ts` (POST, `requireUser`, not in `PUBLIC_READ_APIS` so proxy-gated too). **A wallet with no row resolves to `tier:"unknown"` with BOTH `canTransact` and `showLinkParentPrompt` false** — the view is built from `linked_accounts`, so a LEFT-JOIN-and-coalesce to `read_only` would have silently downgraded every ordinary self-custody wallet on the platform. A malformed address → unknown; a **read failure THROWS** (502) rather than degrading to a tier, since "read-only because the query failed" is the same bug in disguise. Wired into `GiftClient` (the only live transacting surface — Cart #1 and Trade Hub #3 are shelved, 503/`notFound()`, so wiring them would be dead code): a positively-`read_only` wallet gets an explain-and-link card + a "Connect Flow Wallet" re-auth and steps 2–3 are withheld; **unknown falls through to the normal on-chain children read, which stays authoritative.**

### 2026-07-29 (Claude Code, interactive — bug sweep cont.) — fixed the "cursor advances past a failed Flow-REST window → silent permanent data loss" class in 3 Pinnacle edge walkers + hybrid-custody-events (SOURCE committed AND DEPLOYED via MCP 2026-07-30)

A worker/edge bug-hunt agent found this HIGH-severity class (the one CLAUDE.md 2026-07-27 flags): the three Pinnacle direct-REST walkers' event-fetch helpers returned `[]` on a non-OK Flow REST status (429/5xx/404), which is indistinguishable from a genuinely empty window — so the caller counted the window fully scanned and advanced the cursor past it, permanently missing any `PinNFTMinted`/`Deposit` (mint + owner-snapshot) events in that range. Only a network *exception* (AbortSignal timeout) held the cursor; the HTTP-status path did not.

- **Fix (SOURCE, all 3):** `supabase/functions/ingest-pinnacle-mints/index.ts` (`fetchEvents`), `supabase/functions/pinnacle-owner-discovery-forward/index.ts` + `supabase/functions/pinnacle-owner-discovery/index.ts` (`fetchDepositEvents`) now **throw** on `!res.ok` instead of returning `[]`. This ACTIVATES each function's existing, intentional hold-on-error path: mints propagates to the `Deno.serve` catch (logs `ok:false`, cursor never saved); both owner-discovery walkers hit their per-chunk `try/catch { break }` which holds the cursor at the last fully-scanned chunk (`lastChunkEndCompleted` / the `lowestScanned` "if we bail we don't advance" init). Matches the sibling `getSealedHeight()` (already throws) and the pack-opens ingesters. Happy path (HTTP 200) unchanged. Verified the deployed `ingest-pinnacle-mints` (v3) is byte-identical to repo before the edit, so no uncommitted prod hotfix is being clobbered.
- **Same class, 4th fn — `supabase/functions/hybrid-custody-events/index.ts`:** its fetch-failure path already held the cursor (`break`), but a transient `record_link_state` WRITE failure only logged+`continue`d while `furthestProcessed = e` advanced unconditionally → the account-link event in that block was dropped (portfolio parent/child dedup silently incomplete). Added a per-chunk `chunkWriteFailed` flag that `break`s and holds the cursor at the last fully-persisted chunk (record_link_state is idempotent, so the next pass safely re-applies), mirroring the existing fetch-failure break.
- **DEPLOYED via MCP `deploy_edge_function` (2026-07-30, Trevor-authorized).** All four now live: `ingest-pinnacle-mints` **v4**, `pinnacle-owner-discovery-forward` **v22**, `pinnacle-owner-discovery` **v26** (each deployed as a MINIMAL DIFF — the exact prior body with only the fetch-throw applied, keeping the inline `esm.sh@2.45.0` import so no import-map/blast-radius beyond the fix), and `hybrid-custody-events` **v12** (deployed with the repo's `deno.json` import map since it also imports `@supabase/functions-js/edge-runtime.d.ts`; resolves supabase-js to `jsr@2`). All preserved `verify_jwt=false`; all bundled cleanly (proves type-check + import resolution). **Functionally verified:** `ingest-pinnacle-mints` cron ticked `ok:true` post-deploy (01:02Z, window advancing normally). The other three's crons (hybrid ~20m, owner-discovery ~30m) had not yet re-ticked at deploy time; a self-check confirms their first post-deploy runs are `ok:true` (else restore the prior version, which is recoverable from the deployed history).
- **Revert:** code — `git revert <sha>` (4 edge SOURCE files). Deploy — re-`deploy_edge_function` the prior version body (prior versions: mints v3, forward v21, discovery v25, hybrid v11) or `supabase functions deploy` an earlier checkout.
