### 2026-07-29 (Claude Code, interactive — bug sweep) — fixed a silent-total-loss stall in the underpriced-#1s active-listings ingest: the GHA sweep was SIGKILLed at the 30-min job timeout on every run since 07-28 22:29Z; script now self-limits and logs a degraded run instead

Live-health sweep turned up a real firing incident: `detect_stalled_pipelines()` flagged `topshot-active-listings-ingest` silent ~22h (last ok:true `pipeline_runs` row 07-29 01:13:02Z). GHA run history showed every scheduled run since 07-28 22:29Z concluding **`cancelled`**, with the "Ingest active listings" step running *exactly* to `timeout-minutes: 30` — i.e. Atlas slowed/throttled, the per-target 4× retry backoff (up to ~15s/call) ballooned the ~486-target serial sweep past 30 min, and GitHub SIGKILLed the process mid-loop. Because `flush()` + the final POST never ran, **all buffered rows were lost AND no `pipeline_runs` row was written** (a silent stall), and the script's own `allBlocked` egress guard was unreachable in that state.

- **Fix (`scripts/ingest-topshot-active-listings.mjs`, GHA-run script — no Vercel bundle/route change):** added an internal wall-clock budget `DEADLINE_MS` (default 24 min, env-tunable, kept under the 30-min job timeout). When exceeded, the loop stops early, flushes the partial rows it DID collect, and POSTs a **degraded** final `{ final:true, deactivate:false, ok:false, error:"time_budget_exceeded" }` — reusing the exact route contract the existing `allBlocked` path already uses (`app/api/cron/topshot-active-listings-ingest/route.ts` logs it as an ok:false run). `deactivate:false` so an incomplete sweep can't wrongly drop still-live listings; the honest `pipeline_runs` row breaks the silence so the stall/alert path sees it. `node --check` clean.
- **Root-cause note:** the underlying trigger is an Atlas-side slowdown (~since 01:13Z 07-29; recovered ~23:34Z, a fresh ok:true 479-target run landed + stall detector back to `[]`) — may self-heal or may need operator IP attention (Atlas WAF is IP-sensitive). The code fix makes the pipeline resilient + observable regardless; it does not itself restore full Atlas throughput.
- **Follow-up hardening (same commit family):** added `curl --connect-timeout 10 --max-time 30` to the Atlas calls. Without a per-call timeout, a throttling Atlas that accepts the connection but never responds hangs curl indefinitely — the retry backoff only bounds FAILED calls and the `DEADLINE_MS` check runs BETWEEN loop iterations, so one hung call would have bypassed the budget and still ridden to the 30-min SIGKILL. Now every call is bounded, so the budget is reliably reachable. `node --check` clean.
- **Revert:** `git revert <sha>` (1 script file; no migration, prod-DB, or FMV/pricing-logic change).

### 2026-07-28 (Claude Code, interactive — handoff round 6) — closed a 4-hour window in which a stalled sales indexer was invisible to EVERY alert branch; the cursor-stall threshold is now expressed ONCE and guarded

Drained [docs/handoff-2026-07-28f-alert-gap.md](../handoff-2026-07-28f-alert-gap.md) item 16. **Two DB migrations + one route/test change.** (Migration names are `audit_20260729_*` — the Supabase clock is UTC and this shipped after 07:00Z-equivalent midnight UTC; the PT session date is 07-28. Search by the `20260729` names, not the heading date.) Guard **proven to bite** (see below). Smoke suites 38/38; `npx tsc --noEmit` clean outside the documented stale `.next/types/validator.ts` entries (7, pre-existing, absent in CI which typechecks without a prior build).

- **The defect: one concept, two literals.** `silent_indexer_failures` classified `cursor_stalled` at **2h**; `get_pipeline_alerts()` alerted on it at **6h**, reading `event_cursor` directly. The view's `CASE` is first-match-wins, so at 2h an indexer flipped to `cursor_stalled` and thereby **stopped matching** the `ok` / `resolving_editions` / `silent_failure` arms the alert fn consumes — and **nothing alerts on the `cursor_stalled` status itself**. Between 2h and 6h it emitted no alert of any kind. Confirmed live pre-fix: `ufc_sales`, cursor age 2.27h, `unmapped_written_24h` 210, status `cursor_stalled`, **absent from `get_pipeline_alerts()` entirely**. Harmless on UFC (dead Flow market since 2026-05-13); on `topshot_sales`/`allday_sales` it is four silent hours on a primary sales indexer.
- **SHIPPED — `audit_20260729_unify_cursor_stall_threshold` (DB-only).** New `public.cursor_stall_threshold()` (IMMUTABLE, returns `interval '6 hours'`) is now called by **both** objects, so the two cannot drift apart by construction. Took the handoff's **option 2** (raise the view to the alerting value) over option 1 (lower the alert arm to 2h): lowering would page on cursors legitimately idle 2–6h — several watchlist entries are max-governed well past 2h (`topshot-active-listings-ingest` at 900 min). Between 2h and 6h an indexer now keeps its prior honest classification and stays visible under it until the real 6h alert fires; **no new alert volume**. Live post-fix: `ufc_sales` reads `resolving_editions` and appears in `get_pipeline_alerts()` at `info`. Both objects rebuilt from `pg_get_viewdef`/`pg_get_functiondef` via **guarded `replace`** (occurrence-count assert → `RAISE`, so a whitespace miss aborts rather than silently no-ops); `security_invoker=true` re-asserted after `CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW` wiped reloptions. **Revert:** restore the view arm to `cursor_updated_at < (now() - '02:00:00'::interval)`, restore the alert arm to `WHERE updated_at < now() - interval '6 hours'`, then `DROP FUNCTION public.cursor_stall_threshold();`
- **SHIPPED — `audit_20260729_check_cursor_stall_threshold_drift` (DB-only) + the smoke probe.** The handoff was right that the *actual* defect is drift-ability, not either value. New SECDEF `check_cursor_stall_threshold_drift()` asserts the threshold fn exists, is a positive interval, and that **both** objects still reference it; returns `[]` when clean. Wired into `/api/smoke-test` as a **HARD** probe (non-soft ⇒ Sentry-alerts). **A repo-side CI test would not have caught this class at all** — these objects are changed via the Supabase MCP, which never touches git, so the guard has to live where the drift happens. **Revert:** `DROP FUNCTION public.check_cursor_stall_threshold_drift();` + `git revert <sha>`.
- **Guard proven to bite, not assumed.** Re-inlined the old 2h literal inside a transaction that `RAISE`s to roll back: guard returned **1 violation** (`inlined_threshold:public.silent_indexer_failures`); post-rollback re-verified `[]`, view still shared, `reloptions` intact, `ufc_sales` still `resolving_editions`. **The first attempt at this proof returned a false PASS** — `pg_get_viewdef` renders the call **unqualified** (`cursor_stall_threshold()`, no `public.`), so my replace string was a silent no-op. Re-ran against the actual rendered text. Same trap as the 07-27 SWC finding: *test the real input, not a paraphrase of it.*
- **ACL note:** Supabase `ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES` grants anon/authenticated EXECUTE on every new public function, so `REVOKE … FROM PUBLIC` left those explicit grants standing (`has_function_privilege('anon',…)` stayed **true**). Closed by `audit_20260729_cursor_stall_threshold_revoke_anon` — both fns now anon/authenticated `false`, `service_role` `true`. Neither is anon-reachable regardless (the view is service_role-only).
- **Sole consumer verified before touching anything:** `get_pipeline_alerts()` is the only DB object referencing the view (`pg_proc.prosrc` + `pg_get_viewdef` sweep) and there are **zero** repo references. Out-of-repo Cowork artifacts that display this view's `status` will now show `resolving_editions`/`ok` instead of `cursor_stalled` during 2–6h — a display change, not a break.
- **Not changed (recorded, no action):** `topshot_sales` reads `ok` with `runs_1h` 0 / `last_run_at` NULL because `ok` is driven by `sales_written_24h > 0` — a 24h window deciding an hourly process's health. Per the handoff, defensible; it means `ok` asserts "wrote sales sometime today", not "is running now".
- **Branch:** direct to `main` per CLAUDE.md; no PR.

### 2026-07-28 (Claude Code, interactive — flake fix on Batch-10 AchievementsCard test) — a leaked 2000ms setTimeout re-fetch could flake a later component-suite file; no-op'd it while the refresh chain settles

Test-only. The Batch-10 `component-AchievementsCard.test.tsx` "Refresh POSTs" case clicked Refresh, whose `handleRefresh` schedules a **real** `setTimeout(…, 2000)` that later calls `load()` → a relative-URL `fetch` (throws in node). ~2s later it fired mid-run inside whatever component file was executing, surfacing as **1 failed / 647 passed** on one full-suite run (passed on rerun — the leaked-timer signature). Fix: `vi.spyOn(window,"setTimeout")` no-op while the POST's `.finally` microtask settles, so nothing real is scheduled (spy restored by `restoreAllMocks`). Verified: two consecutive full component-suite runs now **115 files / 648 tests, 0 failures**. **Revert:** `git revert <sha>`.

Requested "health check + fix anything off." The one real latent bug was a blind monitoring metric.

- **SHIPPED (DB, no deploy) — `audit_20260728_fix_edition_integrity_flags_metric`.** The `edition_integrity_flags` arm of `v_rpc_trust_health` read `count(*) FROM v_edition_integrity_flags` — but that view is a per-collection `GROUP BY` (one row per collection ⇒ **always 5**), so the metric was pinned at ~5, could never approach `breach_at=50`, and the real defect columns it computes were never summed. Genuine editions drift was therefore UNMONITORED by it. Rewired to `SUM(canonical_bad_circulation + canonical_missing_tier + canonical_missing_thumbnail)` across collections (excludes the accepted ~6.5k TS UUID-dupe residue and the structurally-null candy/ufc on-chain-id columns), `breach_at` 50→**250** (above the continuous thumbnail-hydration baseline; Trevor's call to include thumbnails). ### 2026-07-28 (Cowork, interactive) — RECON RESOLVED: Golazos has NO DapperOffersV2 offers at all (neither EDITION- nor NFT-type) — cron deliberately NOT wired, and the handoff's supporting premise corrected

Drained the recon gate in [docs/handoff-2026-07-28-golazos-offers-indexer.md](../handoff-2026-07-28-golazos-offers-indexer.md). The route is sound; the collection has no offer book. **No cron wired — deliberately.**

- **The gated POST ran clean.** `ok:true, pages 60, offersSeen 0, offersCompleted 0, editionsWritten 0`, cursor `159,437,130 → 159,452,130`, 12.2s, no error. So the route itself works end-to-end (auth, Flow REST, cursor, `log_pipeline_run`); it simply found nothing.
- **NEITHER handoff branch applies — and the disambiguation mattered.** Branch 2 reads "`offersSeen == 0` while OfferAvailable volume exists ⇒ offers are NFT-type". Global OfferAvailable volume *does* exist, but **none of it is Golazos**, so a bare `offersSeen == 0` would have been misread as an NFT-type finding. This environment (unlike the build sandbox) **does** have Flow REST egress, so the baseline was measured directly rather than inferred: a fully-covered contiguous **400,000-block window (~4 days, 1,601 chunks, 0 failed)** carried **14,495** `OffersV2.OfferAvailable` events — TopShot 9,460 · MFLPlayer 3,986 · AllDay 775 · MFLClub 274 · **Golazos 0 · UFC 0**. Six spot samples at −0.5M/−1M/−2M/−4M/−8M/−16M blocks (2026-02-26 → 2026-07-23, 659 more offers) also returned **Golazos 0, UFC 0**. Public Flow REST's event floor sits between −16M and −32M blocks (404 below).
- **Positive control (same contract, same code path):** `allday-offers-indexer` 142 offers / 24h, `topshot-offers-indexer` 1,979 / 24h, `golazos-offers-indexer` 0. The scanner and the route agree on every collection that *does* have offers.
- **⚠ Handoff premise CORRECTED — `marketplace_offers` is not evidence of Golazos DapperOffersV2 offers.** The handoff cited "284 historical rows, `nft_type = A.87ca73a41bb50ad5.Golazos.NFT`". That table is **Flowty-extractor output** (`20260517220000_flowty_extractor_marketplace_offers_and_rpcs.sql`): its `offer_state` CHECK is `LISTED/CANCELLED/PURCHASED/EXPIRED` keyed on `listing_resource_id` — Flowty storefront vocabulary, **not** the OffersV2 `OfferAvailable`/`OfferCompleted` lifecycle — and `edition_id` is **NULL on all 100,771 rows across all four collections**, not just Golazos. It is frozen at Flowty's shutdown (last `event_timestamp` 2026-05-16). It says nothing about DapperOffersV2 either way.
- **The cause is demand, not plumbing.** Golazos secondary market: **123 sales / 30d, 6 in the last 4 days**, last sale 2026-07-25 — against TopShot's 90,612 / 30d. A collection trading ~4 moments/day has no standing offer book.
- **DECISION — cron NOT wired.** At the route's own cadence a 20-min cron costs ~60 Flow REST chunk-pairs/tick × 72 ticks ≈ **8,640 range-requests/day for a structurally guaranteed zero**, against the standing read-diet. Route + `golazos_open_offers` stay inert and harmless; they light up for free if Golazos offers ever start printing. `docs/operations/cron-schedule.md` deliberately **not** touched.
- **Explicitly NOT filed as "the NFT-type variant is needed."** That was the handoff's pre-scripted fail branch, but the measurement doesn't support it — there is no offer volume of *either* type to resolve. Filing it would have manufactured a build off a finding that isn't there.
- **Prod state touched (the only mutation):** one `pipeline_runs` row (`golazos-offers-indexer`, ok=true) and `event_cursor('golazos_offers')` `0 → 159452130`. Left advanced on purpose — ~35k blocks behind tip is ~3 catch-up ticks if it is ever wired, whereas resetting to 0 forces a fresh 50k-block backfill. No `pipeline_cadence_watchlist` row exists for this pipeline, so the single run raises no `cron_silent`; `detect_stalled_pipelines()` = `[]` after. **Revert:** `UPDATE public.event_cursor SET last_processed_block = 0 WHERE id = 'golazos_offers';`
- **Honesty constraint held.** `edition_offers` unchanged (TopShot 12,364 / AllDay 2,195 / Golazos 0); nothing written to `fmv_snapshots`.
- **Revert (docs/comment):** `git revert <sha>`.

### 2026-07-27 (Claude Code, interactive) — SHIPPED (k): the pack-opens backfill "zero-yield" finding was WRONG about the cause — a silent cursor RESET destroyed 31.4M blocks of walk progress on 07-25; fixed the reset bug in BOTH pack-opens fns + made `pulls_written` stop lying (~18× overstatement)

Drains the one open item from the 07-27 late sweep (`allday-pack-opens-backfill` burning Flow REST for ~zero rows). The sweep's cost number was right; its diagnosis ("genuinely finding already-ingested ground", needs only a counter) was incomplete — the pipeline is re-walking ground **because its cursor was reset**. **Edge-fn code only; no migration, no prod DB mutation, no cursor repositioned.**

- **ROOT CAUSE — `getCursor` conflates "read failed" with "cursor absent".** Both `ingest-allday-pack-opens` and `ingest-topshot-pack-opens-history` did `const { data } = await supabase.from("event_cursor")…maybeSingle(); return data ? … : null` — **`error` is dropped**. One transient PostgREST blip returns `data: null`, the caller reads that as "never initialized" and takes the init branch, which **re-seeds the cursor to TIP**. Measured on the AllDay backfill: it had walked down to **127,740,659** by 07-25, was reset to **159,183,789**, and has been re-walking since (now 149,508,789). Fix: `getCursor` returns a discriminated `{ok:true,value}｜{ok:false,error}`; a read failure logs `ok:false` + `cursor_read_failed` and **aborts the tick without touching the cursor**. Same guard applied to the TopShot twin (its `Math.min(seedStart,t)` seed made it look safer, but it re-seeds identically).
- **⚠ THE SWEEP'S "~14k calls/day for zero yield" WAS MEASURED FROM 3 RUNS AND IS WRONG IN BOTH DIRECTIONS.** Live 24h: **18,389** Flow REST calls (14,400 event queries + 3,989 tx fetches — the sweep missed the tx leg), and yield is **not** zero: `allday_pack_pull` grew **93 rows**. Same class as the 07-27 wallet-walk lesson — *a 3-run sample classifies, it cannot rate.*
- **`pulls_written` IS A LYING METRIC — ~18× overstatement.** 24h claimed **1,684** (backfill 1,627 + forward 57) against **93** actual rows. Decisive case: the 03:26 tick reported `pulls_written: 102` for a window whose **102 pull rows were all created 2026-06-30**, with table-wide growth that hour of **0**. So `.upsert(…, {ignoreDuplicates:true}).select()` returns **pre-existing** rows, not inserted ones — the in-code comment asserting "`.select()` returns only inserted rows" was false. Fixed by reading the existing `(pack_nft_id, moment_nft_id)` keys up front (paginated via `.range()` — a bare `.select()` clamps at 1,000 and would have re-inflated the very counter this fixes) and counting real inserts. New `extra` keys **`rips_already_present` / `pulls_already_present`** make a 0 self-explaining (nothing new HERE) instead of ambiguous — the catalogue #21 prescription, now on both fns' write path.
- **~~NOT DONE — DELIBERATELY~~ → DONE same-day by Cowork (`audit_20260727_allday_pack_opens_backfill_cursor_restore`), and MY COST/BENEFIT FRAMING WAS BACKWARDS — do not reuse it.** I left the cursor un-repositioned and wrote that restoring it to the low-water mark 127,740,659 would save ~110k Flow REST calls but "forfeit the ~93 rows/day the re-walk is still recovering (~560 rows over 6 days)". That treated the re-walk's yield as the thing at risk. It was the opposite: **93 rows/day was the re-walk's ENTIRE output**, while the restored position immediately produced **494 pulls on the first tick and 548 on the next** — and, decisively, at **`pulls_already_present: 0`** versus the re-walk zone's 0-written / 104–164-already-present. So the restore was not a coverage sacrifice for a cost saving; it was strictly better on **both** axes, ~6 ticks/hour of virgin ground instead of none. **Durable lesson: I sized a decision by the yield of the ground already being walked, when the whole question was the yield of the ground NOT being walked — the two regimes are not comparable and the new `*_already_present` counter is exactly what distinguishes them (0% vs 100%).** Restore SQL, for the record: `UPDATE event_cursor SET last_processed_block = 127740659 WHERE id = 'allday_pack_opens_backfill';`
- **DEPLOY STATUS — AllDay is LIVE (v8 → v9), TopShot is repo-only.** AllDay verified on prod after deploy: `probe` decodes an open cleanly; a `forward` tick wrote 2 rips / 2 pulls with `already_present` 0/0; and a `backfill` tick over the re-walk zone reported **`rows_found 60 · rips_written 0 · pulls_written 0 · rips_already_present 60 · pulls_already_present 164`** — the zero is now self-explaining, and 164 is exactly what the old counter would have falsely claimed as writes. The 22:36:01Z row is the *scheduled* tick, so cron is on v9. **`ingest-topshot-pack-opens-history` is committed but deliberately NOT deployed:** its cursor is currently healthy (105,265,659) so the bug there is latent, and that fn is mid-incident from today's cold-spork revert (`audit_20260727_ts_pack_opens_history_cursor_revert_cold_spork` + QUEUED `TS-PACK-OPENS-COLD-SPORK-WARMUP`) — redeploying it while that is unresolved risks confounding the diagnosis. Repo-ahead-of-prod is the benign drift direction; the next repo-based deploy picks it up.
- **Revert:** `git revert <sha>` restores both prior fn bodies, then redeploy the AllDay edge fn from the reverted repo (deployed AllDay was **v8**, byte-identical to the repo base before this change — verified via `get_edge_function`, so there was no repo↔prod drift to reconcile). TopShot needs no redeploy (never deployed).

### 2026-07-27 (Claude Code, interactive) — SHIPPED (g): `resolve-topshot-stubs` claimed ~7,000 resolutions/week against 514 stubs that never moved — no cursor, plus "success" defined as "a row matched"; and a live data-corruption path disarmed one step before it fired

Fourth instance of the same class in one day, found by the **standing "does green mean it saw the work?" check** (frozen-`extra` arm: 47 runs/24h, 1 distinct payload). Three stacked defects, all shipped fixed. Migration `audit_20260727_topshot_stub_resolver_rotate_and_honest_change` (DB) + edge fn `topshot-stub-resolver` **v13 → v14** + route + tests.

- **(1) The counters in the Vercel route were hardcoded literals.** `app/api/cron/resolve-topshot-stubs/route.ts` passed `p_rows_found/written/skipped: 0` as constants, so `rows_written = 0` across 140 runs was a **literal zero, not a measurement** — which is exactly why the "parts that don't sum" sweep had never surfaced this pipeline. Now forwards the edge fn's real counters via `countersFrom(bodyJson)`, or `null` (honest 0/0/0) when the body carries none.
- **(2) The queue had no cursor, so it re-walked the same 50 rows forever.** `get_topshot_stub_targets` was `ORDER BY created_at ASC LIMIT 50` over a predicate the resolver could not clear. Measured: **47 of the head-50 touched in the last 24h vs 6 of the 464 rows behind them — 458 rows the pipeline exists to drain had never once been attempted.** Fixed to `ORDER BY updated_at ASC NULLS FIRST, created_at ASC`: the upsert stays unconditional so `trg_editions_updated` always advances `updated_at`, making that column a real attempt cursor with **no new schema**. Verified post-ship: the head immediately rotated to a different, never-attempted set.
- **(3) "Resolved" meant "a row matched", not "a field was filled".** `upsert_topshot_edition_metadata` COALESCEs every column then returned `ROW_COUNT > 0`. For a team moment — **~88% of this queue, and they have no player on chain at all** — `player_name = COALESCE(NULLIF(player_name,''), NULL)` is a no-op, yet the UPDATE still matched, so the RPC returned true and the caller counted a resolution. Now returns whether a tracked column actually took a **new** value (before/after tuple `IS DISTINCT FROM`, compared post-trigger so a normalizer counts). Edge fn splits `rows_resolved` from a new **`rows_no_change`** counter. Sole caller — verified 0 other DB callers and 0 other repo callers.
- **⚠ (4) THE LATENT ONE, and the reason (2) could not ship alone.** `pickPlayerName` guarded the on-chain `"<invalid Value>"` sentinel on `FullName` **but not on the `FirstName`/`LastName` fallback it composes from** — so those rows would have written the literal string **`"<invalid Value> <invalid Value>"`** into `editions.player_name`, which feeds player pages, slugs, search and the pooled serial-FMV set/player effects. **Live on 4 of 42 sampled targets** (set 141, "The Champion's Path 2024"). **Bug 1 — every jersey row would have rendered as "Low".** The Serials formatter was `first_mint ? "#1 First" : last_mint ? "Last" : "Low"` — a fallthrough. Now matched explicitly, with its own chip style.

**Bug 2 — TWO stacked silent caps, both below the new maximum.** The board is 125 editions × 4 kinds = **625 theoretical max**. The fetch was `limit = 600` and the client `cap={550}`, and `DataTable` truncates with a bare `r.slice(0, cap)` — no "showing N of M". So the first daily walk after launch would have silently dropped rows at *both* layers. Raised to 800 each. The 07-27 readiness audit had specifically praised this board for having "no LIMIT — not a silent cap"; that was true at 500 rows and stopped being true the moment a fourth kind existed.

**Bug 3, found by a test warning and live in production right now — duplicate React keys on all 500 rows.** Writing the fixtures produced *"Encountered two children with the same key, `mike-trout`"*. That is not a test artifact: `DataTable`'s row key is `pda_address || external_id || wallet_address || player_name || i`, first-truthy-wins, which on the Serials tab resolves to `external_id` — and **every edition contributes up to four rows**. React's documented behaviour with duplicate keys is to duplicate or omit children, and **this table re-sorts on every header click**, which is exactly when it bites. Replaced with a composite key including `serial_number` and `kind`. **Proven to bite**: reverting the key fails the new test, restoring it passes.

Copy updated — the Serials note now describes the jersey kind and states the precedence rule ("a serial that is both a low serial and the jersey number keeps its low-serial label, so each serial appears once") rather than leaving a user to wonder why #2 isn't tagged twice. 4 new tests. `tsc` clean; full suite **7,162 tests, 0 failures**.

### 2026-07-27 (Cowork, interactive) — ROOT CAUSE FOUND for the jammed copy: it IS the SWC JSX transform. My earlier acquittal of it was wrong, and wrong for an instructive reason

Supersedes the "root cause not established" verdict in the entry below. **It is the transform**, reproduced offline against Next 16.2.9's own SWC binding, with a matching negative control.

**Why I wrongly cleared it the first time.** I tested the hypothesis by hand-writing a *paraphrase* of the JSX shape, ran it through SWC, saw the space preserved, and concluded the transform was innocent. It was the paraphrase that was innocent. Feeding the **verbatim committed source** through `@next/swc-linux-x64-gnu` reproduces production exactly:

```
CandyBoardClient.tsx (verbatim, pre-fix)  -> "editions have traded — and most of..."   ← space GONE
PaniniSqueezeClient.tsx:155 (verbatim)    -> " editions of this set. Panini publish..." ← space KEPT
```

Those two match what the deployed pages actually render — Candy jammed, Panini fine — so the transform reproduces both the positive and the negative case. `PackDropsBoardClient.tsx` reproduces the drop verbatim too. **Lesson worth keeping: when testing whether a tool mangles your input, test the input, not a retyping of it.** A paraphrase is a different input, and here the difference was the whole phenomenon.

**Two more live instances found and fixed**, both in *fresh* (`x-vercel-cache: PRERENDER`) builds, which independently retires the stale-cache theory:
- `/insights/pack-drops` — `<strong>39</strong>distinct editions against on-chain FMV`, rendered **6 times** on the page (once per drop card).
- `/insights/deals` — `<em>seller's</em>proceeds — so we show what you'd keep`.

All four sites now emit `<element>, " ", "text…"` — the explicit space as its own child — **verified through the same binding rather than assumed**.

**What I still cannot state precisely is the minimal trigger.** Every confirmed case is a text run that begins with a space and wraps to the next source line, but Panini and `CandyBoardClient.tsx:654` do exactly that without breaking, so wrapping alone is not sufficient. The confirmed cases all sit after the *second* of two consecutive inline elements (`<b>{a}</b> of <b>{b}</b> text…`) or after an element that itself follows a line-ending `{" "}`; a controlled A/B on the pack-drops shape showed the preceding `{" "}` flipping the outcome on its own. That is suggestive, not proven, and I am not going to write a rule I have not isolated.

**UPDATE (end of session) — the detector is now in the repo at `scripts/detect-jsx-space-drop.js`, working but deliberately NOT wired to CI.** The bug that made the first cut untrustworthy is fixed: it scanned emitted string literals with a regex, which silently skipped most strings in a file already known to be broken. Replaced with a proper quote/escape tokenizer, and it now finds **32 candidates in 22 files**. **It still OVER-REPORTS** — spot-checking 5 against deployed HTML found **1 real, 4 false** — and the header documents exactly why: it never inspects the *preceding sibling* in the emitted children array, so a boundary where the space is already supplied (an existing `{" "}`, or a previous string with a trailing space) reads as a defect. In the HTML the false ones look like `</strong> <!-- -->meets or approaches` (fine) versus the real `<em>not</em>a guaranteed flip` (jammed). **To finish: walk the arguments of each `jsx`/`jsxs` call rather than the flat set of literals, and flag a text child only when its immediate predecessor is an element with no `" "` between.** Then it becomes a true defect list and can gate CI. The one real defect that sweep did surface — *"A big discount is not a guaranteed flip"* rendering as **"nota guaranteed flip"** on `/insights/deals` — is fixed. Original note follows.

**QUEUED — `JSX-SPACE-DROP-DETECTOR` (worth building, I did not finish it).** The right guard is not a style heuristic — it is to run each `.tsx` through the Next SWC binding and diff emitted text against the source's intended spacing. A first cut is written and works file-by-file (it confirms all four fixes and correctly clears Panini), but my whole-repo version's source-side matcher has a bug: it silently missed `PackDropsBoardClient.tsx`, a file I *knew* was broken, and returned mostly `aria-*` false positives. **Do not trust that scan's "6 files" output** — it is not sound yet. Finishing it would turn this from a class found by eye into one that cannot ship again; until then, the existing style rule in the Candy component test is the only automated cover, and it is deliberately scoped to one file.

### 2026-07-27 (Cowork, interactive) — TS-PACK-OPENS-HISTORY-CURSOR-FASTFORWARD: shipped, then REVERTED after three ticks characterised the blocker. The lasting finding is bigger than the cursor: NBA Top Shot has **zero** recorded pack opens before 2023-09-29 while NFL All Day has 1.4 million, and the job that could settle it is now wedged on an unreachable spork

Closes the item queued 07-26 (see the CLOSED note further down this ledger). **I got the reasoning wrong on the first pass and corrected it before shipping the writeup — recording both, because the wrong version is the more tempting one.**

**What I first concluded (WRONG).** Bucketing every Top Shot `pack_rips` row by 25,000-block windows over 61,925,000 → 106,949,999 gives 1,801 windows, 331,844 rips and **23 empty windows, 22 of which sit below block 63,125,000**. I read that bottom cluster as the signature of an incomplete historical import and moved the cursor to sit on top of it. **That reading does not survive contact with the data.** Pulling counts *and* `sealed_at` ranges for the cluster shows those windows are interleaved with windows holding 1, 2, 3, 4 and 6 rips, and the timestamps chain continuously from 2023-09-29 to 2023-10-18 with no discontinuity. At 2–6 opens per window, a zero window is Poisson noise. An incomplete import truncates; it does not leave 1-rip windows scattered through the zeros. **The cluster is a genuine quiet period at the dawn of Top Shot pack-opening, not a gap.** Same test applied to the isolated empty at 86,025,000–86,049,999 dissolves it too: neighbours hold 2 and 2, and their timestamps bracket a real ~19-hour lull on 2024-09-05. **No targeted rescan needed — that owed follow-up is closed, not deferred.**

**What the data actually says, via a control.** Top Shot's earliest recorded rip is block **61,930,346 / 2023-09-29**, and there are **0** Top Shot rips before that date. The sibling collection on the identical scan mechanism, NFL All Day, has **1,396,033 rips before that same date**, reaching back to block 21,373,356 / **2021-12-10**. So the `PackNFT.Opened` scan path was producing millions of rows for nearly two years before Top Shot's first one. Either (a) Top Shot migrated to the PackNFT standard long after All Day did, and there is genuinely nothing below 61.93M, or (b) **~1.5 years of Top Shot pack-open history is missing.** These are opposite conclusions and internal data cannot separate them. This is precisely the failure mode the 07-26 note said the repo cares about most, and it is a much larger question than the cursor.

**So the cursor move was right, for the opposite reason I gave — though it did not survive contact with the infrastructure (see below).** Migration `audit_20260727_ts_pack_opens_history_cursor_to_gap_cluster` moved `event_cursor.topshot_pack_opens_history_backfill` from `105865659` → **`63125000`**. The justification is NOT that it lands on missing history; it is that the 1,753 windows it skips are **provably re-derivation** — exactly one of them is empty, and the last 40 logged scans found *precisely* what was already stored (**5,284 opens → 5,284 rips present, 0 written, zero discrepancy in either direction**) — whereas everything below 61,930,346 has **never been scanned by any logged pipeline** and holds the (a)-vs-(b) answer. **Do not raise `floor` (27,341,470).** That instinct was right even though my first reasoning for it was not. **Revert:** `UPDATE public.event_cursor SET last_processed_block = 105865659, updated_at = now() WHERE id = 'topshot_pack_opens_history_backfill';`

**The move immediately surfaced a latent wedge — and this is the finding worth keeping.** The first tick under the new cursor (15:41Z) read `cursor_before=63125000`, correctly scanned window 63,100,000–63,124,999 — and **failed on query 1 of 100**: `events 63100000-63100249 status 500`, `transient: true`, cursor held. Block 63.1M routes to the **55,114,467–65,264,618** spork; every successful run this pipeline has ever logged sat in the **88,226,267–130,290,658** spork, and *no* logged pipeline in either collection has queried below 105,865,659 (Top Shot) or 127,740,659 (All Day). **There is no evidence the configured spork proxy serves any spork below 88,226,267.** If it does not, then:

1. **The job wedges silently and forever.** `after = anyTransient ? cur : start` — a transient error holds the cursor and retries the same window. A 500 from a spork the proxy does not serve is *permanent in effect but transient in classification*, so the walk retries block 63,100,000 every 15 minutes indefinitely.
2. **Monitoring DOES see it — I checked before claiming otherwise.** My first draft of this entry asserted the wedge would be invisible, reasoning that the `pipeline_cadence_watchlist` arm is `max_silent_minutes: 90` (a **silence** alarm, which a job failing on schedule never trips). That is true of the cadence arm but false of the system: `app/api/sentinel/route.ts:293-296` says so in as many words ("the daytime monitor only scans `pipeline_runs` for ok=false"), and `pipeline_alert_state` confirms it in practice — the sibling **`allday-pack-opens-backfill` alerted on 2026-07-04 at `last_failure_count: 3` with `events 137378483-137378732 status 404`, the same failure class at a spork boundary**. So this wedge pages after ~3 ticks (~45 min), and the two arms are complementary by design, not a hole. Recorded because "the monitoring can't see it" is a claim that sounds authoritative and costs nothing to check.

**Three ticks then characterised it exactly, and it is neither unreachable nor flaky — it is a COLD-CACHE 500:**

```
15:41Z  ok=false  queries=1  events 63100000-63100249 status 500
15:56Z  ok=false  queries=2  events 63100250-63100499 status 500
16:11Z  ok=false  queries=3  events 63100500-63100749 status 500
```

Every tick succeeds on every 250-block sub-range it has requested **before** and 500s on the first one it has **never** requested. The proxy appears to materialise a range on demand, 500 while it warms, then serve it fine. `j()` retries 3× at 400ms/800ms — far too short to outlast the warm-up — and `scanOpens` aborts the entire window on the first failed sub-range, discarding the 99 it would have read. **Net: the walk advances exactly one 250-block sub-range per 15-minute tick — ~25 hours per 25,000-block window, ~50 days just to cross 63.125M → 61.93M.**

**REVERTED** (`audit_20260727_ts_pack_opens_history_cursor_revert_cold_spork`, cursor back to `105865659`, verified). Not because the move was wrong, but because the fix needs a measurement I cannot take from this sandbox — probe mode against a cold range, timing how long until it serves — which needs the function's `GATE` key. Leaving it wedged would have paged every 45 minutes overnight for a question that is not urgent. The job is now back to exactly its pre-today behaviour: knowingly re-deriving covered ground, silent and harmless.

**QUEUED — `TS-PACK-OPENS-COLD-SPORK-WARMUP` (owner, needs the GATE key).** The experiment first, then the fix: (1) `?mode=probe&start=<cold block>&blocks=250` and time repeat calls until one returns 200 — that number decides everything. (2) If warm-up is seconds, lengthen the spork retry schedule in `j()` (exponential, ~30s ceiling) and the window completes in one tick. (3) If it is minutes, a single tick cannot warm 100 ranges and the shape must change instead: fire all 100 requests to warm them and re-scan on the next tick, or drop `?blocks=` so a window is a size a tick can actually finish. **What NOT to do: reclassify the 500 as permanent and advance** — that silently drops windows, the one outcome this repo refuses. If windows must be abandoned, they go in a durable gap ledger as *explicitly unscanned*, the dead-letter pattern already established in `candy-sales-indexer` this session.

**One alert did fire before the revert** — `pipeline_alert_state` shows `topshot-pack-opens-history-backfill` alerted at **16:16:06Z** on `last_failure_count: 3` with `events 63100500-63100749 status 500`. So if Trevor saw a page for this pipeline this afternoon, that was me: it is fully explained by this entry, it self-resolved when the cursor was reverted (16:26Z tick: `ok=true`, 100 queries, cursor advancing normally), and no further alerts should follow. It also, incidentally, is the direct proof that the failure arm works — which is the claim I nearly got wrong above.

**Two things this bought even though the cursor came back.** The pre-2023 Top Shot history question above is now on the record with a control behind it. And the wedge is a property of the pipeline, not of my change — **`allday-pack-opens-backfill` is walking toward the same boundary** (cursor ~127.7M, descending 25k/tick at 6 ticks/hour, so it reaches 88,226,267 in roughly 11 days) and will hit the identical cold-spork behaviour then, with nobody watching for it. Fixing it before that is cheaper than diagnosing it live.

### 2026-07-27 (Claude Code, interactive) — SHIPPED (e): the ipfs-media proxy was streaming videos the edge cache SILENTLY REFUSES — every view an unamortised 16–23 MB (the Fast Data Transfer alert); + the 502 soft-fail was unreachable dead code

Route + component, one commit. **No migration, no DB.** Drains items 2 and 3 of [docs/handoff-2026-07-27-alert-triage.md](docs/handoff-2026-07-27-alert-triage.md); both handoff claims **re-verified live before coding**.

- **The leak.** `app/api/public/ipfs-media/[cid]/route.ts` set `s-maxage=31536000, immutable` and its header reasoned "the first request warms the Vercel edge and every subsequent load is a cached same-origin hit". True for images, **false for video** — the objects exceed Vercel's max cacheable response size and the route had **no size ceiling**, streaming `upstream.body` at any length. Measured on prod, same URL 3×: **4.03 MB image/png → MISS, HIT, HIT** vs **16.75 MB mp4 → MISS, MISS, MISS** and **23.27 MB mp4 → MISS, MISS, MISS**, with `s-maxage` **stripped** on the oversize responses. So every video view cost a full 16–23 MB of Fast Data Transfer forever, with zero amortisation. Blast radius **10,786 editions** carry an IPFS video URL (`nba_top_shot` 10,270 + `ufc_strike` 516; AllDay/Golazos/Candy 0). Fix: read `content-length` and **302 to the upstream gateway above 8 MB** (between the largest size proven to cache and the smallest proven not to), cancelling our own body so the bytes never transit the function. CSP-safe — `proxy.ts` already allows `https://ipfs.io` in **both** `img-src` and `media-src` (verified). SSRF-safe — `CID_RE` validates before the redirect target is built. A missing/chunked `content-length` falls through to the old streaming path rather than guessing.
- **The amplifier.** `components/MomentHeroMedia.tsx` was the **only** autoplaying `<video>` in the app without `preload="none"` — every sibling clip surface (`TrophySlab`, `EditionsGridPaginated`, `MomentMedia`, the profile trophy tiles) is hover-mounted and/or `preload="none"` (all four audited). So every `/moment/[id]` render pulled the entire clip whether or not anyone watched. Added `preload="none"`; the `poster` (which DOES cache) still paints immediately, so a real viewer sees no change.
- **The 504s (item 3).** `AbortSignal.timeout(25_000)` sat at **exactly** the platform's own initial-response cutoff, so the platform always won (`504 [error/serverless-middleware] … did not return an initial response within 25s`) and the `catch`'s 502 never ran — making the `<img onError>` candidate-advance chain **unreachable dead code for precisely the slow-gateway case it was written for**. Lowered to 8s so the abort fires first. (The 504 burst had already self-resolved — 205 in 12:25–13:05Z → 2 in 13:50–14:40Z — ipfs.io recovering, not a code change; fixed because the soft-fail path is proven not to work.)
- **Tests:** `__tests__/api-public-ipfs-media-cid.test.ts` 4 → 8, pinning the oversize 302 + body-cancel, the under-ceiling stream keeping `s-maxage`, the chunked-no-content-length fallback, and that the timeout is under the platform cutoff. **2 of the 4 new tests proven to fail** against the pre-fix route by stashing it. `tsc` clean on all real source.
- **Revert:** `git revert <sha>` (route + component only; no schema, config, or env).

### 2026-07-27 (Cowork, interactive) — Candy pre-launch, part 3: the Deals board was advertising discounts the sales history contradicts. Median-sale publish guard shipped

The most serious thing found in the whole readiness pass, because Deals is the surface that tells a stranger *buy this, it is 45% under fair value*.

**The defect, measured at the top of the board:**

| edition | ask | FMV | advertised | sales | MEDIAN sale | truth |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `bobby-witt-jr` | $4.58 | $8.31 | **44.9% off** | 4 (4.33 / 4.44 / … / 20.04) | **$4.44** | ask is ABOVE the median — **no discount at all** |
| `jordan-walker` | $5.00 | $10.49 | **52.3% off** | 3 (5.97 / 7.01 / 18.49) | **$7.01** | ~29% off |
| `junior-caminero-blue` | $135.68 | $255.50 | 46.9% off | **1** ($300.59) | $300.59 | rests entirely on one print |

On a 1–11 sale market a single high sale lifts the fitted FMV above every other trade, and the board converts that estimator noise into a headline "% off" aimed at someone's wallet. That is the fabricated-signal class this codebase refuses to ship, and it was pointed at the most actionable tab.

- **Shipped a PUBLISH guard, not a pricing change** (precedent: the troll-ask floor guard, the fabricated-EV publish guards): a listing is published as a deal only if it is below FMV **and** below the edition's median sale, when a median exists. `median_sale_usd`, `sales_count` and `discount_vs_median_pct` are exposed so the board shows its work. Live effect **47 → 40 rows**; `bobby-witt-jr` drops out; `jordan-walker` still appears but now also reads "28.7% below the median trade". FMV computation is untouched — this only changes what we are willing to CALL a deal. Prior definition captured in `audit_20260727_candy_deals_board_prior`; `security_invoker` and the anon revoke both verified after. Gotcha for the next person: `CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW` cannot insert a column mid-list (42P16) — append.
- **Client:** the Discount column is now **"vs FMV"** beside a new **"vs median sale"** column (hover shows the median and the sale count), the table sorts by the median-based figure by default, and the blurb explains the guard. It also loses another stale claim — *"FMV comes off just 1–2 sales"* and *"Empty until secondary listings open"* were both false.
- ⚠ **A rendered-DOM check on the Deals tab is OWED** (this sandbox cannot render). The change is one additive column plus a formatter in an existing DataTable, and `tsc` + the full suite are green, but the 390px mobile pass already owed for this board should cover this tab first.
- Also verified while here and NOT changed: the K=10 troll ceiling is healthy — median floor/FMV **1.20×**, 32 asks excluded across 28 editions. The one surviving 12.1× floor is NOT a leak: the ceiling is `10 × GREATEST(edition FMV, tier median FMV)`, and the tier-median arm deliberately protects thinly-priced editions from an absurdly low ceiling. The queued `K = 5` decision stands as Trevor's, with this measurement attached.

**METHOD (reusable):** `pipeline_runs` grouped over 3 days, `HAVING sum(rows_written)=0 AND sum(rows_found)>0` — pipelines that FOUND work and wrote nothing. 29 pipelines write 0 rows, but most are dispatchers/heartbeats/drained backfills; the `found > 0, written = 0` filter cuts it to 11, and the shape `found=N, written=0, skipped=0` (parts that don't sum) cuts it to 3.

Ground truth: `allday_pack_pull` grew **+61,179 rows in 3 days** (373,490 total). A second, opposite lie sat next to it: `pullsWritten += chunk.length` counted ATTEMPTED rows, so an all-duplicate chunk of 500 reported 500 writes. ### 2026-07-27 (Cowork, interactive) — the ratio guard was ALSO not enough: Candy listing deactivation is now EVIDENCE-BASED, and the 419 falsely-killed asks are restored

Third and final iteration on the same incident, and the one that removes the class instead of narrowing it.

**Why the ratio guard failed.** It compares the sweep against "the book we already hold" — but after one bad tick, that number IS the damaged one. Verified live: the 03:35Z tick saw 22 listings against the (already-wrecked) 24-row book, sailed past a 50% ratio test, and reported a clean sweep. Meanwhile Magic Eden's `/listings` answers for this one collection over six hours were **420 → 7 → 22**, while its collection PAGE said 409 listed and the chain said the book barely moved. **That endpoint is not a census and must never be treated as one.**

- **Shipped: deactivation on POSITIVE EVIDENCE only.** The listings sweep now also walks the ACTIVITIES feed (2 × 500 rows — the reliable half of ME's API; `candy-sales-indexer` has walked it every 3h without a gap) and collects the mints with a listing-ENDING event: `delist`, `buyNow`, `buyNowFill`, `acceptBid`. Only those mints' asks are deactivated, plus anything past its own `expiry`. The "any row this sweep did not see is dead" rule is **deleted**, for cards and packs alike. A failed activities walk means no evidence, therefore no deactivation — never the other way round. A short listings answer is now merely fewer price refreshes, so it is reported as a metric (`feed_looks_truncated`, `activities_seen`, `listing_ending_mints`) rather than a failure. **Revert:** `git revert <sha>`.
- **Shipped: the repair.** `audit_20260727_candy_listings_restore_false_deactivation` restored **407** of the 419 asks — every row the 21:38Z sweep last confirmed alive, minus the 7 whose token has since sold and 0 expired. Live after: active asks **428**, `candy_listing_floor` **7 → 112 editions**, `candy_deals_board` **3 → 53**, `candy_offer_spread_board` **11 → 109**. The restored PDAs are preserved in `public.audit_20260727_candy_listings_restored` (RLS on, anon revoked) and the revert is a one-line UPDATE against it.
- **THE DURABLE LESSON, in three versions because I needed all three:** (1) don't guard a destructive sweep on the degenerate value (empty) — partial is likelier than empty; (2) don't guard it on a ratio to your own state either — one bad tick poisons that baseline; (3) **only delete on positive evidence of deletion.** If the upstream cannot prove a thing is gone, it is not gone.
- **Checked the same class on the Flow side and deliberately did NOT change it.** `topshot/golazos/allday/ufc-listing-cache` all purge `cached_listings` rows older than the run start, guarded only by `upserted > 0` — the same degenerate-zero guard that just failed here. Measured before prescribing: over 3 days / 474 runs those routes wrote min **50**, avg **101**, max 122 rows with **zero** tiny or empty runs, i.e. Flowty's API is stable where ME's is not, and they feed ASK-side FMV. Queued as **CANDY-CLASS-PURGE-GUARD-FLOW-CACHES**, not shipped — a speculative edit to an FMV-feeding path is exactly the kind of change the standing rule says to hand off.
- +3 tests (delist/fill evidence deactivates; an unseen ask survives an empty feed; a failed activities walk deactivates nothing), each proven to fail against the pre-fix route; the 2 ratio-guard tests they replace were deleted. `tsc` clean; full suite **902 files / 7,122 tests, 0 failures**.

### 2026-07-27 (Cowork, interactive) — LIVE INCIDENT + FIX: a degraded Magic Eden response wiped 419 of 426 Candy asks in one tick; the zero-only guard was not enough, ratio guard shipped to BOTH sweeps

**Caught in the act while verifying the same day's work.** The `candy-listings-indexer` tick at **00:35Z** received **7 listings** from Magic Eden against a **426-ask** book and, because 7 is not 0, my hours-old empty-feed guard did not fire: it treated the sweep as complete and **deactivated 419 standing asks**. `candy_listing_floor` collapsed 114 editions → **7 rows**, `candy_deals_board` → **3**, `candy_offer_spread_board` → **11**.

**Proven upstream, not real, from the blockchain — not from Magic Eden's own feed.** An 80-transaction on-chain sweep of the collection over the same window (23:47Z → 02:04Z) shows the whole collection did **6 `CoreCancelSell` (delists) and 8 sales**. A 419-ask book collapse would need ~400 delists. The book did not move; the feed did. (Independent corroboration: the ME collection PAGE read 409 listed at ~23:40Z, and a sandbox fetch of `/listings?limit=100` returned 15 rows — this endpoint demonstrably serves truncated answers.)

- **Fix (both sweeps, symmetric):** guard on the RATIO, not on zero. A sweep that returns `< 50%` of the book already held (once that book is ≥ 20 rows) is treated as INCOMPLETE: deactivation is suppressed, rows that WERE returned still upsert, expiry-based deactivation still runs, and the run reports **ok=false** with the two counts in the message. Deliberately not self-clearing — a genuine >50% collapse keeps tripping it and stays visible, which is the right way round, because suppressing a deactivation is reversible and issuing a wrong one is not. Ported to `candy-offers-indexer` too (same shape is reachable there: every per-bidder fetch can "succeed" with a short answer). New metrics `active_before`, `active_offers_before`, `degraded_sweep`.
- **NO data repair issued, deliberately.** A healthy sweep re-upserts every live ask with `is_active=true`, so the book self-heals on the next good tick (03:35Z) — reactivating 419 rows by hand would also resurrect the handful that genuinely did die, and the surface is gated so nothing user-facing was affected. Verify at 03:35Z; repair by hand only if the feed is still degraded.
- **THE DURABLE LESSON:** I shipped the zero-case guard the same evening after reasoning that an empty response was the destructive case. The destructive case is a *partial* response, and partial is far more likely than empty. **When guarding a destructive sweep against a flaky upstream, never guard on the degenerate value — guard on the ratio to the state you already hold.**
- +3 tests (2 listings, 1 offers), each proven to fail against the pre-fix routes; one pre-existing offers fixture re-sequenced for the added count read. `tsc` clean; full suite **902 files / 7,123 tests, 0 failures**. **Revert:** `git revert <sha>`.

### 2026-07-27 (Cowork, interactive) — ON-CHAIN VERIFICATION of the Candy sales feed (27 mints, 0 misses) + pack-bid instrumentation

Two follow-ons to the pack layer, both about knowing rather than assuming.

- **The Candy secondary-sales capture is now VERIFIED COMPLETE against the blockchain, not against Magic Eden's own feed.** Using the public Solana RPC (reachable from the Cowork sandbox even though Helius/DAS is not), walked `getSignaturesForAddress` + `getTransaction` for **27 mints** and counted true ME sale instructions in the logs (`CoreExecuteSaleV2` / `SolMplCoreFulfillBuy`), then diffed against `public.sales`:
  - 12 mints that HAVE sales in our DB: **22 on-chain sales, 22 captured, 0 missed.**
  - 15 RANDOMLY-sampled circulating mints (the unbiased direction — the one that can expose a systematic miss): **1 on-chain sale, 1 captured, 0 missed, 0 phantom.**
  - Non-ME activity on those mints is only `CreateV2` (mint) and `Transfer` (plain wallet move) — **no Tensor, no AMM, no other marketplace**, matching the earlier 8-mint venue census.
  - **Decoded the ME instruction vocabulary for mpl-core** (worth keeping): `CoreSell`=list · `CoreCancelSell`=delist · `BuyV2`=place bid · `CancelBuy`=cancel bid · **`CoreExecuteSaleV2`=sale** · **`SolMplCoreFulfillBuy`=sale into a bid/pool**. Both sale forms appear in the sampled history and both were captured, so `SALE_TYPES` {buyNow, buyNowFill, acceptBid} does cover pool/bid fills.
  - **Method gotcha:** the first pass reported `onchain=0` for every mint because the regex anchored on `Instruction: ExecuteSale` — the real instruction is `CoreExecuteSaleV2`, so it never matched. A completeness check that returns a clean zero is a red flag, not a pass; the fix was `Instruction: \w*(ExecuteSale|FulfillBuy|FulfillSell)\w*`.
- **Pack bids: instrumented, not built.** The offers sweep drops a bid on a sealed pack for the same reason listings did (its wmc gate only knows card mints). Rather than guess whether pack bids are worth a `candy_pack_offers` table, the sweep now re-checks a card-gate miss against `candy_packs` and reports **`pack_offers_seen`**. Build the table if that number is non-zero after a few ticks; skip it if not. One indexed lookup per distinct mint, no extra ME call. +1 test (fails against the pre-fix route). **Revert:** `git revert <sha>`.

### 2026-07-27 (Cowork, interactive) — the Candy PACK layer: pack supply, pack sales and pack asks were all being discarded; 3 tables + `candy_pack_market` + capture in all three indexers. Plus an on-chain venue census that CLOSES the "other marketplaces" question

Follow-on from the dead-letter ship. Every Candy pipeline was throwing the sealed-pack side of the market away, on a product whose packs trade at **3-4x retail**. No pricing/FMV logic touched; pack prices are structurally walled off from `fmv_snapshots`.

- **What was being dropped.** (a) `candy-editions-ingest` DAS-walks all 27,876 assets daily and discarded the **2,501 packs** (`packs_skipped`) — it was already paying for the fetch; (b) `candy-sales-indexer` saw pack sales and could not resolve them (they were the first 3 rows the dead letter caught — 0.39-0.45 SOL, i.e. **~$30-34 against a $10 pack**); (c) `candy-listings-indexer` dropped pack asks entirely because its wmc gate only knows card mints. Net: RPC had no pack supply, no pack holders, no sealed-vs-opened split, no pack floor and no pack sale history.
- **Shipped (DB):** `candy_packs` (mint PK; `is_burnt` = an OPENED pack), `candy_pack_sales` (PK `transaction_hash,token_mint`), `candy_pack_listings` (PK = ME listing PDA), and one-row view **`candy_pack_market`** — supply/sealed/opened/holders, ask floor, 24h+7d sales and volume, median, and the three honest ratios: **vs retail, vs `typical_pull_ev_usd`, vs `actual_ev_usd`**. Every EV figure is PASSED THROUGH from `candy_pack_ev_model`, never recomputed, so there is still exactly one pack-EV implementation. All four objects RLS-on / anon+authenticated REVOKED (verified `has_table_privilege` false). Migrations `audit_20260727_candy_pack_layer_tables` + `audit_20260727_candy_pack_market_view`. **Revert:** `DROP VIEW IF EXISTS public.candy_pack_market; DROP TABLE IF EXISTS public.candy_pack_listings, public.candy_pack_sales, public.candy_packs;`
- **Shipped (code):** editions ingest now checks `isPack` BEFORE the burnt filter (a burnt pack is an OPENED pack and must be recorded, unlike a burnt card) and upserts `normalizePack()` rows; sales indexer writes the `candy_pack_sales` row before classifying the sale `pack_asset`; listings indexer re-checks a wmc miss against `candy_packs` (indexed lookup, **no extra ME call**) and upserts pack asks, with the same complete-sweep-only deactivation rule. New metrics `pack_rows_touched`/`packs_distinct`/`pack_asks_upserted`/`pack_asks_deactivated`. **Revert:** `git revert <sha>`.
- **The number that makes this worth surfacing:** live `candy_pack_ev_model` reads `typical_pull_ev_usd` ~$33.70 and `actual_ev_usd` ~$62.82 on a $10 pack. The observed pack sales (~$30-34) sit ~1.0x TYPICAL PULL and ~0.5x ACTUAL EV — the market is pricing the median pack, not the mean. That is the same lottery-pricing structure the Top Shot pack surfaces exist to expose, and RPC now measures it on chain two.
- **VENUE CENSUS — closes the open "are sales happening off Magic Eden?" question with on-chain evidence.** The public Solana RPC IS reachable from the Cowork sandbox (`api.mainnet-beta.solana.com`, `getHealth` ok) even though Helius/DAS is not. Sampled 8 Candy mints (2 that sold on ME, 4 randomly-held cards, 2 packs), walked `getSignaturesForAddress` + `getTransaction` over **43 transactions**, and matched every account key against the marketplace program IDs: **magic_eden_v2 22 hits, mpl_core 43, and ZERO Tensor / Tensor-AMM / cNFT / Hadeswap / ME-MMM-pool.** Magic Eden is the whole market for Candy MLB today, so ME-feed volume is not materially undercounting. Also re-censused the ME activity vocabulary over a 89-row window: `list` 54 / `delist` 16 / `bid` 8 / `buyNow` 8 / `cancelBid` 2 / `poolUpdate` 1 — our `SALE_TYPES` {buyNow, buyNowFill, acceptBid} covers every sale-shaped type present.
- **NOT built, deliberately:** the `/insights/candy-mlb` pack-market UI block. The view is correct but EMPTY until the pipelines fill it (packs land on the 08:40Z daily walk), and this sandbox cannot render a page — shipping a surface I cannot verify by rendered DOM breaks the standing rule. Next session: add the block once `candy_pack_market` has rows.
- +6 tests (all six proven to fail against the pre-fix routes by stashing each route). `tsc` clean; full suite **900 files / 7,099 tests, 0 failures**.

### 2026-07-27 (Claude Code, interactive) — proactive date-boundary flake audit (follow-on to the db-tests CI fix): swept the whole test suite for the same class, hardened the one real vitest risk

Test-only, no product change. After fixing the `get_edition_fmv_history.sql` midnight flake, swept every test for the same class (relative-date-from-real-clock feeding a day-bucket/date-string assertion). **SQL side: clean** — no other `supabase/tests/*.sql` uses a sub-day `now() - interval 'N hours/minutes'` in a DATE() bucket (the only remaining hit is the explanatory comment in the fixed file). **Vitest side:** of 30 real-clock tests, one had a genuine (microsecond-window) midnight race — `api-edition-floor-persist.test.ts` asserted a persisted timestamp's day == `new Date()`'s day, which can differ if the test straddles midnight UTC between the route's internal `new Date()` and the assertion's. Hardened by capturing the UTC day on BOTH sides of the route call and accepting either (the route ran between them) — zero timer-mocking risk. ### 2026-07-27 (Claude Code, interactive) — CI FIX: `main` was RED (db-tests) on a midnight-boundary flake in a DB-invariant SQL test

Test-only, no product/DB change. Found via a proactive CI check: the `db-tests` job (only that one; typecheck/unit/component/cadence/ledger all green) was failing on every run since ~00:xx UTC — `get_edition_fmv_history.sql` asserted a default-30d window returns **2** daily points but got **3**. **Root cause:** the fixture used `now() - interval '2 hours'` for a "today" snapshot; CI ran at **00:58 UTC**, so `now() - 2h` = 22:58 the PREVIOUS day → a separate `DATE()` bucket → 3 buckets instead of 2. A pure date-boundary flake (the function is correct), latent since the test was added and tripped whenever CI runs in the first ~2h of a UTC day. **Fix:** anchor both "today" snapshots to `date_trunc('day', now()) + interval '1h'/'2h'` so they are guaranteed the SAME calendar day regardless of run time (the 10d/100d points already use full-day offsets, no boundary risk). Verified locally against a throwaway `postgres:16`: the full suite is **22/22 PASS** (was 1 FAIL), and `db-invariants-drift-guard` is 22/22 (only fixture lines changed — the verbatim function DDL is untouched). **Revert:** `git revert <sha>`.

### 2026-07-27 (Claude Code, interactive) — bug fix: the 23505 batch-insert data-loss bug in 3 backfill scripts + guarded the superseded classify-acquisitions writer (resolves the 07-26 documented drift items)

Fixes the real drift items the 07-26 scripts audit had DOCUMENTED-but-not-edited (all three scripts confirmed dead one-offs — referenced by no `package.json`/workflow/scheduler). Code-only, no prod DB mutation, no migration; the scripts aren't imported by any test so verification is `node --check` + project `tsc` (both clean) + matching the canonical, tested row-by-row pattern from `app/api/sales-indexer/route.ts`.
- **23505 co-batch data loss fixed in 3 `sales` writers.** A batch `.insert()` is all-or-nothing: one duplicate `transaction_hash` (23505) fails the whole statement and writes NONE of it, so counting the batch as skipped silently drops every co-batched NEW sale (permanently, since the cursor still advances). `scripts/flow-backfill.ts` (its comment even claimed a `ignoreDuplicates` it never used) and `scripts/cryptoslam-scrape.ts` never retried; `scripts/sales-backfill.mjs` was **inverted** — it retried row-by-row on NON-23505 errors and counted the whole batch `duped` on 23505, exactly backwards. All three now retry row-by-row on any batch error so real dups skip individually while new rows land.
- **`scripts/classify-acquisitions.mjs` — superseded-WRITE guard.** It's superseded by `/api/bulk-classify` and has two cost-basis-corrupting defects (reads getMintedMoment `price` = current/listing price instead of `lastPurchasePrice` = price paid; upserts synthetic `classifier_<id>` rows instead of resolving the existing `unknown` row). Rather than a half-fix I can't verify, it now REFUSES a real write unless `--run-superseded` is passed; `--dry-run` inspection (writes nothing) stays available. Points the operator to `/api/bulk-classify`.
**Revert:** `git revert <sha>` (restores the swallow + the unguarded writer).

### 2026-07-26 (Cowork, interactive) — Candy / Magic Eden ingest hardening: dead-letter for stranded sales, bidder cap 40->250 (offer deactivation had been frozen ~42h), an empty-feed guard that could otherwise have wiped the whole ask book, honest editions metrics

Prompted by a review of "are we tracking Candy secondary effectively" (project doc `claude/candy-ingest-review-2026-07-26.md`). All four Candy pipelines were green; every defect below was silent under `ok=true`. Code + 2 DB objects; no pricing/FMV logic touched, no public surface touched (`CANDY_MLB_PUBLIC` still false).

- **Stranded sales -> dead letter.** `candy-sales-indexer` stops at the first ME activity <= `max(sold_at)`, so a sale it SEES but cannot write (DAS throw, unresolvable serial, edition not yet ingested, no SOL rate, asset-budget exhausted) is only re-offered while it is still the newest thing — the next successful write steps the cursor over it and it is gone. Measured over the first 25 runs: **359 found vs 322 written = 37 skipped**, with no dead-letter and no signal. Now parked in new `public.candy_sales_unresolved` via SECDEF `candy_park_unresolved_sale()` (attempts++ on re-park) and drained oldest-first each tick (`DRAIN_LIMIT` 60, `MAX_PARK_ATTEMPTS` 25) with whatever asset budget the live walk left. A drained row keeps its original `sold_at`, so recovery can never move the cursor. A 23505 on drain closes the row `duplicate_tx_hash` (`sales` dedups on `transaction_hash` alone, so a second item under one ME signature can never land). New extras: `parked`, `drain_attempted`, `drain_resolved`, `unresolved_open`, `activities_seen`, `me_key_present`. **Revert:** `git revert <sha>` + `DROP FUNCTION IF EXISTS public.candy_park_unresolved_sale(text,text,timestamptz,numeric,text,text,text); DROP TABLE IF EXISTS public.candy_sales_unresolved;` (migrations `audit_20260726_candy_sales_unresolved_deadletter` + `audit_20260726_candy_park_unresolved_sale_fn`; table RLS on, anon/authenticated revoked, fn revoked from PUBLIC too — verified `has_*_privilege` false).
- **Offer sweep un-truncated: `MAX_BIDDERS` 40 -> 250.** `bidders_discovered` crossed 40 on 2026-07-25 06:50Z and reached 60, so every tick since logged `bidders_truncated: true` — and because step 5 correctly refuses to deactivate on a partial sweep, **the deactivation pass had not run for ~42h**: 6 of 17 `is_active` offers were last seen 07-25 00:50Z, i.e. `candy_best_offers` / `candy_offer_spread_board` could quote a cancelled bid. The failure mode was stale-LIVE, never false-dead. A truncated tick now also logs **ok=false** so the freeze cannot hide behind a healthy `offers_upserted`. **Revert:** `git revert <sha>`.
- **Empty-feed guard on the listings sweep (latent mass-deactivation).** An empty first page set `sweep_complete=true`, so a single degraded ME response would have marked the **entire standing book** dead in one tick (420 asks) and emptied `candy_listing_floor` / `candy_deals_board` / `candy_offer_spread_board` until ME recovered. Reachable: ME's public arms for this symbol serve degraded answers (its `/stats` arm echoes `listedCount: 0` for ANY symbol). Now: 0 raw rows while active asks exist => sweep treated as incomplete, deactivation suppressed, `ok=false`. Expiry-based deactivation still runs. New extras `raw_listings_seen`, `active_before`, `me_key_present`. **Revert:** `git revert <sha>`.
- **`candy-sales-indexer` empty activities feed => ok=false.** Previously `found=0, written=0, ok=true` — the silent-degradation shape, on the pipeline that feeds the only Candy price signal. **Revert:** `git revert <sha>`.
- **Editions metrics renamed to what they measure.** `editions_written: 3108` was upsert ROWS TOUCHED across DAS page-chunks against a **125-edition** catalog. Now `edition_rows_touched` / `serial_rows_touched` plus true `editions_distinct` / `serials_distinct`. **Revert:** `git revert <sha>`.
- **Tests:** +10 (4 sales, 2 listings, 2 offers, 2 editions assertions rewritten); **8 of them proven to fail against the pre-fix routes** by stashing each route and re-running. `__tests__/helpers/route-harness.ts` fixture type widened to carry `count` (needed by any `{ count: "exact", head: true }` read). `tsc --noEmit` clean; full suite **891 files / 7,007 tests, 0 failures**.
- **Measured but NOT changed (needs a decision):** ME reports 4,982 collection supply against our 7,251 circulating serials (treasury `BhA2Bfd8...` holds 18,124 of 25,375; no second treasury wallet exists, so our count is sound). Until that is reconciled, ME collection-feed volume cannot be claimed as the whole Candy secondary market. Pipeline severities left at `info`/`medium` per the go-live doc — raising `candy-sales-indexer` to `high` rides the launch flip, not this.

### 2026-07-26 (Claude Code, interactive) — SHIPPED (DB index, live): killed the cold-scan behind the `get_team_detail` connection-pool-timeout (Sentry JAVASCRIPT-NEXTJS-1Y)

**Additive index, no code / no function change, no deploy.** Chasing the 3 unresolved Sentry errors (`GET /[collection]/team/[slug]` + `/player/[slug]` "Timed out acquiring connection from connection pool", 4/4/1 events / 5–6 days). Profiled both RPCs: they're fast warm (LeBron 23 ms, Knicks 110 ms) and already well-indexed, so this is NOT a `get_team_activity`-style 28 s algorithmic stall — the pool-acquire timeout is a saturation symptom, worsened by one cold cost center in `get_team_detail`.

- **Root cause:** the team-variant lookup (`SELECT array_agg(DISTINCT team_name) … WHERE regexp_replace(lower(trim(team_name)),'[^a-z0-9]+','-','g') = $slug`) had no matching index — the slug is a functional expression — so it index-only-scanned the WHOLE collection's editions. New York Knicks: 18,121 rows examined (17,471 removed by the regexp filter), **8,186 heap fetches / 6,703 buffers**. Cold, that page-read amplification balloons to seconds and holds the pooled connection the whole time. `players` already had the exact mirror index (`idx_players_collection_name_slug`) — which is why `get_player_detail`'s own slug lookup was already a seek (its twin error is pure saturation collateral); `editions` was just missing the twin.
- **Fix:** `idx_editions_collection_team_slug` on `editions (collection_id, (regexp_replace(lower(trim(team_name)),'[^a-z0-9]+','-','g'))) WHERE team_name IS NOT NULL` — functional btree on the same immutable expression, partial to match the sibling `idx_editions_collection_team`. Built **CONCURRENTLY** via `execute_sql` (valid+ready verified), parity migration `20260726170000_audit_20260726_editions_collection_team_slug_index.sql` (plain `CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS` for history).
- **Measured (Knicks):** variant lookup **60.4 ms → 3.5 ms** (buffers **6,703 → 501**); full `get_team_detail` **110 ms → 63 ms** warm, output **byte-identical** (edition_count 650 / player_count 64 / fmv_total 42668.28 / sales_30d 3827 unchanged across Knicks·Lakers·Thunder). Function body untouched → results cannot change (an index is never chosen when slower); end-to-end strictly ≥ as good. Deliberately did NOT touch the remaining cold costs (per-edition FMV lateral — already indexed + FMV-adjacent; sales-30d join — already on its tuned partition index).
- **REVERT:** `DROP INDEX IF EXISTS public.idx_editions_collection_team_slug;` (+ `git revert <sha>` for the parity file).

### 2026-07-26 (Claude Code, interactive) — the wallet-lookup wedge moved to the surfaces that actually get traffic, and made measurable for the first time

The top-of-funnel wedge ("paste a wallet, see what you own") was reachable only from the LEAST-visited surface, and two thirds of the boxes that did exist emitted no event at all. Both halves are fixed. Evidence-driven throughout; the placement decision was changed mid-pass by the data.

**What the measurement actually said (funnel_events, 30d, read at the start of the pass).** The brief's premise — home 20/7d vs collection_view 131/7d vs insights_view 40/7d — held. But the obvious fix (put the box on the collection landing page) was a trap. Broken down by tab, `/<c>/overview` is only **8.8%** of `collection_view`: `edition/*` **51.4%**, `pack/*` **15.5%**, `/collection` **14.2%**, overview 8.8%, rest ~10%. The same shape holds on insights — the `/insights` hub is only ~18% of `insights_view` (first-mint 44, squeeze 14, pack-sniper 10, … across ~30 boards). **A page-level block on either landing page would have reached under 10% of the traffic it was meant to catch.** So the entry point went in the two LAYOUTS, mounted once each, covering 100% of both subtrees.

**The second, larger finding: the wedge was already on the high-traffic surfaces — it just wasn't instrumented.** `wallet_paste` reading 24 lifetime / 2 in 7d was NOT purely a placement problem. There were **four** hand-rolled copies of the same input (`HomePageMarketing`'s private `WalletSearch`, `InsightsWalletSearch`, `AccountValueSearch`, and a block on `/<c>/overview`) and **only the home one called `trackFunnelEvent`**. Every lookup on `/insights` and `/insights/account-value` — the #2 surface by traffic — has been invisible for its entire life. The `/overview` copy was worse than invisible: it pushed anon visitors at the **auth-gated `/dashboard`**, so the #1 CTA on a public landing page bounced to `/login`. All four are now one component.

- **NEW `components/WalletSearch.tsx`** — the canonical input, factored out of `HomePageMarketing`'s private copy. Same behaviour, same styling: `variant="hero"` and `variant="inline"` reproduce the two looks that already shipped 1:1, so this is a placement+instrumentation change, not a restyle. `destination` is constrained to the two ANON-SAFE public routes (`/share/<wallet>`, `/insights/tc-report?wallet=`) — never an auth-gated one.
- **NEW `components/WalletSearchBand.tsx`** — the compact layout-level placement. One row: a line of copy + the 52px input (stacks at ≤640px; ~112px on a 390px viewport). The old `/overview` hero's 32px decorative glyph and 32px padding are deliberately NOT reproduced. **§3 compliance:** it carries no logo, nav, breadcrumb, collection switcher, tab bar or ticker — it is the first CONTENT block inside the existing `<main>`, sharing that `<main>`'s max-width and padding, so it is not a second header. Renders in the SSR pass (crawlable + verifiable in delivered HTML) and removes itself one tick after hydration if a wallet is already known, so a returning collector is never nagged. Self-suppresses on `/insights`, `/insights/account-value`, `/insights/tc-report`, `/insights/squeeze-check` — the routes that already ARE the lookup.
- **Mounted in 3 layouts:** `app/(collections)/[collection]/layout.tsx`, `app/(collections)/disney-pinnacle/layout.tsx` (the bespoke Pinnacle layout serves its collection+sniper tabs from their own page dirs and would otherwise silently lose the wedge), and `app/insights/layout.tsx` (wrapped in a 1180px column matching `.rpc-ins-hero`).
- **`/<c>/overview`'s forked block DELETED, not patched** — the layout band supersedes it and a second box would be a duplicate. Its now-dead `WALLET_HINTS` / `ctaSubtitle` / `hasWallet` locals went with it.

**Instrumentation.** No new `event_type` and **no migration required**. `wallet_paste` was already emitted on SUBMIT, not on paste — read the emitter, the semantics already match "lookup submitted", so reusing it keeps the historical series comparable instead of splitting it. What changed is that every placement now emits it, under a **distinct `surface`** so the next read can attribute WHICH placement worked rather than just "more pastes": `home` (unchanged) · **`collection_layout`** · **`insights_layout`** · **`insights_hub`** · **`insights_account_value`**. This follows the existing convention — explicit strings for interaction events, pathname for the `perPath` view events.

**Attribution (`lib/track-funnel.ts`).** 990 of 1,086 `funnel_events` rows had a null/empty `referrer` and **zero** carried a `utm_*`, so nothing promoted anywhere would have been attributable. Attribution is now resolved **once per session** (the first event of a session IS the landing hit) and stamped on every later event, because `document.referrer` degrades to our own origin the moment a visitor navigates internally — which is the actual reason `/insights` arrivals all looked referrer-less. Folded into the EXISTING `referrer` column in a bounded documented format (`utm_source=…&utm_medium=…&utm_campaign=…&ref=https://host/path`, capped at the column's own 512 limit), so **no schema change ships**. `components/FunnelTracker.tsx` no longer passes the live `document.referrer`, which was overwriting the landing attribution with our own origin. **Privacy:** our own campaign params + the referring page only; utm values stripped to `[A-Za-z0-9._~-]` and capped at 64; the referrer reduced to **origin+pathname** so a referring URL's query string (which we do not control and which can carry personal data) is never stored; same-origin referrers dropped. No PII, nothing user-identifying, no user data placed in a URL.

**Verification.** `npx tsc --noEmit` **0 errors on pristine `origin/main` before editing and 0 after**. ESLint on every touched file: **0 errors** (one pre-existing `COLLECTION_TICKER` unused warning on the overview page, present at `origin/main` too, left alone). `next build` compiled + typechecked clean. Tests: **29 new/updated across 3 files**, and the full component+funnel suite **49 files / 248 tests PASS**. New `__tests__/component-WalletSearchBand.test.tsx` (13) pins the things that break the MEASUREMENT silently rather than the render — a distinct surface per placement, the two surfaces not colliding, `wallet_paste` firing at all, the band being in the FIRST render pass, the `/dashboard` regression guard, ≥44px touch target (§9), and no literal hex / font strings (§0). New `__tests__/component-WalletSearch-bindings.test.tsx` (6) pins each binding's surface + public destination and that the paste is emitted BEFORE navigation. `__tests__/track-funnel.test.ts` +5 on the attribution (utm capture, survival across internal navigation, same-origin drop, hostile-utm sanitising, explicit-referrer override).

**Revert paths (three, cheapest first).**
1. **Kill switch, no code change:** set `NEXT_PUBLIC_WALLET_BAND=off` in Vercel production and redeploy — both layout placements return `null`. Nothing else is affected (the home hero, `/insights` hub box and account-value box keep working, still instrumented).
2. **Placement only:** delete the four `<WalletSearchBand …/>` lines (one in each of the three layouts, plus the insights wrapper `<div>`). The unfork + instrumentation + attribution all survive.
3. **Everything:** `git revert <code-sha>`. To restore just the old `/overview` block: `git checkout <code-sha>^ -- 'app/(collections)/[collection]/overview/page.tsx'`.

**Migration left for review — NOT applied, and NOT needed for this to work.** The attribution above deliberately reuses `referrer`. If a future pass wants first-class UTM columns for cheap `GROUP BY`, this is the exact DDL; the shipped code needs no change to keep working without it, and would need a small emitter edit to populate the new columns:
```sql

  add column if not exists utm_source   text,
  add column if not exists utm_medium   text,
  add column if not exists utm_campaign text,
  add column if not exists referrer_host text;
```

**Target metric.** `wallet_paste` per week, split by `surface`. Baseline to beat: **2 in the trailing 7 days, 24 lifetime, all from `surface='home'`**. The read that matters is whether `collection_layout` + `insights_layout` + `insights_hub` together exceed `home` — that is the whole thesis, and it is now answerable. Note the 20-registered-users / 0-WAU demand problem is untouched by this; this makes the wedge reachable and measurable, it does not create traffic.
