### 2026-07-25 (Claude Code, interactive, ~15:50 PT) — three defensive-correctness fixes: NULL-FMV fabrication (3 feeds + the board), a confidence chip that survived the 2026-07-11 removal, and real 404s on the five entity SEO routes

Audit-sourced, all three independent of any pending product decision — plus a fourth (FIX 4) found while verifying the first, which FIX 1 turns out to depend on. **All verified against the live site after Vercel reported READY**, not just from the diff: five entity routes curl'd good-slug-200 / bogus-slug-404, a 20-URL real-sitemap regression sweep across all five collections, an A/B of both sniper feeds against the immediately-preceding production deployment, and the shipped client chunk grepped for the deleted chip. `tsc --noEmit` **0 errors before and after** (pristine `main` was already clean this pass — the ~11 `__tests__` errors named in the brief had been cleared by cont. 36). ESLint delta on every touched file: **zero** new errors. New/updated tests all green.

**FIX 1 — a NULL FMV was being rendered as a fabricated number in four places, not the three the audit named.** Standing policy is that an em-dash is always correct where data is absent and a substituted number never is. Each site verified against current code first.
- `app/api/sniper-feed/route.ts` (Top Shot live leg, ~L1372): the ask-proxy fallback guards on `baseFmv < 1`, and **`null < 1` is `true` in JavaScript** — so an edition whose `fmv_usd` is NULL fell into the branch and got priced at `floor_price_usd * 0.90`. A *fabricated fair value for an edition that has none*. Now the row is dropped before the guard; a genuine near-zero FMV still takes the documented ask-proxy path (pinned both ways). `FmvRow.fmv` is typed `number | null` so the compiler enforces the null check at future call sites.
- `app/api/sniper-feed/route.ts` (All Day live leg, ~L1031): `fmvEntry?.fmv || askPrice` **substituted the ask for the FMV**, producing a fake 0% discount — and, when an `fmv_snapshots` row existed with a NULL `fmv_usd` (folded to 0 by `Number(x) || 0` upstream), it shipped that row labelled `confidenceSource: "fmv_snapshots"`. Missing FMV now excludes the listing. Note `||` vs `??`: a legitimate 0 is also not a usable fair value (nothing is "40% off" $0), so both are excluded.
- **Two siblings the audit did not name**, same class, found by grep: the All Day **RPC-fallback** path (~L950) and the Top Shot **RPC** path (~L1231) both emitted `baseFmv: Number(r.fmv_usd) || 0` → a literal **$0.00** fair value on the board. Both now filter on a shared `hasUsableFmv` predicate.
- `app/api/golazos-sniper-feed/route.ts` (~L94): emitted `baseFmv: 0` as the stand-in for unknown. Now emits **null**.
- **Consumer end** (`app/(collections)/[collection]/sniper/page.tsx`, the real path — the audit cited a non-existent `app/insights/sniper/page.tsx`): `(deal.aspUsd - deal.baseFmv) / deal.baseFmv` with `baseFmv` 0 returned **Infinity**, whose `Math.abs(diff) >= 0.1` is always true → a permanent spurious ↑ trend arrow. Replaced with `safeRatioDiff` (returns null for a zero/absent denominator) and all three FMV cells now go through `fmvDisplay`, which renders an em-dash rather than `$0.00`/`NaN`/`∞`. Both helpers live in `lib/sniper/helpers.ts` and are unit-tested.
- **Product impact — MEASURED, and smaller than I first wrote.** I initially recorded "the All Day board will show fewer rows". Then I A/B'd the live production deploy against the immediately-preceding one (`0a63da72`, still serving on its deployment URL) and the counts are **identical: PRE 200 / NEW 200, zero rows lost**, with 0 fabricated rows on either side. Reason: the live AD path is currently the **RPC fallback**, and `get_allday_sniper_deals(0,100000,'all','all','listed_desc',200)` returns 200 rows of which **200 have a positive `fmv_usd`** (checked in SQL), so the new filter drops nothing. My first request did return 0 — but so did the PRE deployment on the same minute; that was a transient upstream blip, not my change. The exclusion only bites on the **GQL live-pool** path, where **1,075 of 6,190 AD editions (17.4%)** have a NULL newest `fmv_usd` — those are exactly the rows that used to render `baseFmv == askPrice` while labelled `confidenceSource: "fmv_snapshots"`. Re-measure if the GQL pool comes back. `[sniper-feed] AD DONE: … fmv_hits=` logs the reach.

Deleting the five layouts alone restores the soft-404 without touching anything else.

**FIX 4 (not in the brief — found while measuring FIX 1, and it is what makes FIX 1 safe) — the All Day FMV map was silently truncated by the PostgREST 1000-row cap.** The map was built from a raw, **unbounded** `fmv_snapshots.eq(collection_id).order(computed_at DESC)` read, justified by a comment asserting the AD snapshot table was tiny (~341 rows). Live it is **306,895 snapshot rows over 6,190 editions**, so the cap meant the map only ever held the newest ~1,000 *snapshots* — a few hundred distinct editions. **The "~341" in the comment was the truncation artifact being mistaken for the table size.**
- Why it is load-bearing here: while a missing FMV merely *mislabelled* a row (ask borrowed, 0% discount), a truncated map was cosmetic. Now that a missing FMV **excludes** the row, the same truncation would have dropped most of the AD board on the GQL live-pool path. FIX 1 and FIX 4 had to ship together; shipping FIX 1 alone would have turned an honesty fix into an availability bug.
- Now reads **`fmv_current`** (DISTINCT ON (edition_id) latest, ≤1 row/edition — verified to agree exactly with the JS dedupe it replaces: 6,190 / 5,115 positive / 1,075 null), paged with **`.range()`** (6,190 > 1,000), with `.gt("fmv_usd", 0)` filtering unusable FMVs server-side so a map MISS and an unusable FMV are one condition for `buildDeal`.
- **This is the class `__tests__/invariants-postgrest-cap.test.ts` exists to prevent** (documented there as having bitten prod at least six times). It slipped through because that guard's allowlist is **per-file**, and `app/api/sniper-feed/route.ts` was already listed for its *other*, genuinely `.in()`-bounded Top Shot read. Added an explicit regression pin to that guard (`fmv_current` + `.range()` present, stale premise absent) — the per-file allowlist granularity is the underlying weakness and is worth a follow-up.
- **Tests:** +2 in `api-sniper-feed-allday-compute.test.ts` — a 1,500-row fixture whose priced edition sits at **index 1,200** (invisible under the old single read) asserting it prices off page 2 and that the requested windows are `[0,999]`/`[1000,1999]`, plus a page-read error degrading without throwing. The mock is now range-aware so the paging loop is really driven, and it deliberately does **not** implement `.gt`, so the NULL/0 cases keep exercising `buildDeal`'s own guard as a second layer.
- **Revert:** `git checkout <this-sha>^ -- app/api/sniper-feed/route.ts` (reverts FIX 1's sniper-feed half too — they are one change).

**STOPPED — needs a product/editorial decision (not shipped):** the Below FMV board still renders a **CONFIDENCE filter group** labelled "High + Med" / "High only" (`DealsBoardClient` L311-325), and the lede + Methodology prose still name the tiers ("scored **HIGH or MEDIUM** confidence"). ### 2026-07-25 (Claude Code, interactive) — live-audit QA: the `/moment` soft-404 root-caused to the Suspense shell, the guessable Pinnacle moment URL, meta-description trim; `% LISTED` + `TOP OWNERS` investigated (correct as-is)

Five items off a live rippackscity.com audit: three shipped, two closed as investigate-only after the reported symptom turned out to be honest behaviour. Full suite green (841 files / 6208 tests); `tsc --noEmit` 11 errors, all pre-existing in `__tests__/`, 0 in touched files.

- **FIX 1 (P2) — soft-404 on `/moment/<id>`, root-caused to `loading.tsx`, not to the page.** The audit reported `/disney-pinnacle/moment/GEN-DPIN-SIMB-S0` landing on a **200 with "Moment Not Found"**. Live re-check found the described redirect only happens for a signed-in user — anonymously that URL **307'd to `/login`**, so a crawler never even reached the soft-404. Three distinct defects, fixed separately:
  - **The soft-404 is mechanical and class-wide.** `app/moment/[id]/` ships a `loading.tsx`, so Next wraps the page in an implicit `<Suspense>`, flushes the document shell + fallback immediately, and streams the page after. By the time the page's own `notFound()` fires the status line is already out as 200; the 404 arrives as a streamed `NEXT_HTTP_ERROR_FALLBACK;404` row. Verified against **Next 16.2.9** with a four-variant probe app, unresolvable id in each: `loading.tsx` + `notFound()` in the page → **200**; + `notFound()` in `generateMetadata` → **200** (metadata streams too, so the common "throw in generateMetadata" advice does NOT work here); + `notFound()` in a segment **`layout.tsx`** → **404**; no `loading.tsx` → **404**. A layout is part of the shell so Next must await it before the first flush. Shipped the layout variant — it keeps the navigation skeleton. New [app/moment/[id]/layout.tsx](../../app/moment/%5Bid%5D/layout.tsx) gates on `resolve_moment_id`, deliberately **not** `get_moment_detail`: it is the same resolver `get_moment_detail` calls internally, so a 404 here is a strict subset of what the page already 404'd on and cannot invent a false 404, and it returns 0/1 rows instead of a large jsonb. It **fails OPEN** on RPC error so a transient blip can't deindex a real moment. Also wrapped `fetchDetail` in React `cache()` — `generateMetadata` and the page were each firing `get_moment_detail`, so the request went from 2 heavy calls to 1 cheap + 1 heavy (net faster than before the gate).
  - **The guessable URL now resolves.** `GEN-DPIN-SIMB-S0` is a `pinnacle_catalog.render_id` (1 row) and **not** a `pinnacle_editions.id` (0 rows), which is exactly why only `/pinnacle/moment/*` — the surface that reads `pinnacle_catalog` — can render it. Added a `/disney-pinnacle/moment/:id` → `/pinnacle/moment/:id` 308 in [next.config.ts](../../next.config.ts). Direction is deliberate: `/pinnacle/moment/*` is the canonical surface (~2,412 sitemap URLs, `lib/sitemap-data.ts` segment 4, and the page self-canonicals there), so redirecting the other way would churn every indexed URL and contradict its own canonical tag — **those 2,412 stay untouched 200s**. No loop: `moment` is absent from both `/pinnacle/:page` allowlists. `next.config` redirects also run **before** the `proxy.ts` auth gate (verified live: `/pinnacle/overview` 308s cleanly rather than bouncing to `/login`), so anonymous crawlers get one hop to the rendered page.
  - **The `/login` bounce.** `moment` was the one entity segment missing from the public-entity allowlist in [proxy.ts](../../proxy.ts), so every `/<collection>/moment/<id>` 307'd anonymous traffic to `/login`. Added it. The route is a pure resolver that renders nothing and only forwards to `/moment/<id>` or `/<collection>/overview`, both already public — no new data exposure, just no bounce.
  - **NOT shipped, follow-up:** the identical soft-404 affects **5 more routes** — `edition`, `set`, `player`, `team`, `series` under `app/(collections)/[collection]/` — each of which ships part of the ~20.5K sitemap URLs and returns **200 on an unknown slug** (confirmed live: `/nba-top-shot/edition/bogus-xyz`, `/nba-top-shot/set/bogus-xyz`, `/nba-top-shot/player/bogus-xyz` all 200). The correlation is exact: every route with a `loading.tsx` soft-404s, every route without hard-404s (`/pinnacle/moment/BOGUS` and `/insights/not-a-real-board` both correctly 404). Left alone because the two fixes are a **trade-off call, not a bug fix**: deleting the 5 `loading.tsx` files is trivial and guaranteed, but drops the loading skeleton on the five highest-traffic SEO surfaces; the layout variant keeps it but needs a cheap existence resolver per entity type (5 new RPCs). Mechanism and probe results above are the hard part and are now settled.
  - **Reverts:** `git rm app/moment/[id]/layout.tsx`; drop the `/disney-pinnacle/moment/:id` block from `next.config.ts`; drop `|moment` from the entity regex in `proxy.ts`; unwrap the `cache(...)` around `fetchDetail` in `app/moment/[id]/page.tsx`.

**HYGIENE CLOSEOUTS (this pass).**

**1. The wmc lock-freshness "crisis" was the METRIC, not the pipeline — false alarm retired.**

- **Carried as:** `MAX_AGE_DAYS=7` promise ~70x oversubscribed, ~1.61M of 2,038,344 `wallet_moments_cache` rows (79%) stale. **Refuted at the column level.** wmc has **two independent** freshness dimensions and the alarm collapsed them into one.
- **Ownership freshness is genuinely healthy.** `wallet-backfill` enumerates each wallet's **complete** on-chain id set every run; cached ids in that set are **confirmed still owned** and the `skip_cached` path then writes nothing. Measured live: **2,390,895 such confirmations in 24h** vs **~291,192/day** needed to honour a 7-day promise across 2,048,775 rows — an **~8.2x surplus** — and **250 distinct wallets walked in 72h against 246 distinct Top Shot wmc wallets**, i.e. every wallet every <=3 days. `last_seen_at` nonetheless showed **1,188,087** Top Shot rows older than 30 days, because `upsert_wmc_batch`'s 2026-06-10 change-detect deliberately skips rows whose `edition_key`/`serial` are unchanged. **`last_seen_at` is a content-change watermark, not a verification watermark.**
- **Lock freshness IS oversubscribed and was left alone, honestly labelled.** 1,385,681 of 1,623,424 TS rows never lock-checked; `lock-check-batch` stamped 46,383 rows in 7d (~6,626/day) vs ~232,000/day for a 7-day promise. That constant is already documented as a background target at the callsite and displayed-lock trust comes from the on-view refresh, so **no behaviour was changed** — an old `lock_checked_at` is a real but expected signal.
- **Fixed the metric, not the data — deliberately.** A blanket `last_seen_at` bump on cache-skip would be **~2.39M UPDATEs/day on a 2.05M-row / ~800MB table on the hot write path** — more than a full table rewrite per day in heap churn + WAL, to move a number already true at the grain that matters. **And the correct grain already existed and was already being written every run:** `wallet_backfill_state.last_scanned_at`, per wallet+collection, via `record_wallet_backfill_scan`. Ownership verification is a per-**wallet** event (the whole id set is enumerated atomically), so per-wallet is the right grain. **Zero new writes.**
- **Shipped:** `audit_20260725_wmc_freshness_metric_truth` — column comments on `last_seen_at` (explicitly "do NOT raise a staleness alarm off this column") and `lock_checked_at`, plus `check_wmc_ownership_freshness(p_max_age_days integer DEFAULT 7)`, set-returning, **0 rows = clean**. **Live proof: the truthful metric returns 4 rows — ONE wallet (`0x01be49cb0c...`) across 4 collections at 9.25 days — against the 1.61M-row alarm it replaces.** Code comment added at the `skip_cached` callsite in `app/api/wallet-backfill/route.ts` so the next reader cannot re-file it.
- **Revert:** `DROP FUNCTION IF EXISTS public.check_wmc_ownership_freshness(integer); COMMENT ON COLUMN public.wallet_moments_cache.last_seen_at IS NULL; COMMENT ON COLUMN public.wallet_moments_cache.lock_checked_at IS NULL;` + `git revert <sha>` for the code comment.

**2. `evm-transfers-ingest` muted — it will flag forever otherwise.**

- Runs ~24x/day returning `{"message":"no_active_contracts"}` because the **Beezie/Base plane was retired 2026-07-13**. Its own watchlist notes already said "No product consumer — monitoring only", so `cron_silent` on it can never be actionable. `pipeline_cadence_watchlist.is_active` -> **false** (`audit_20260725_mute_evm_transfers_ingest_watchlist`). Verified: 23 runs/24h, 0 failures, still ticking.
- **OPERATOR STEP REQUIRED:** the schedule is a **cron-job.org** entry — **not** in `cron.job`, `vercel.json`, or `.github/workflows/`. Muting the watchlist row stops the false flag; only an operator can delete the cron-job.org entry to stop the ticks.
- **Dune checked and deliberately NOT touched.** `sales-ingest-dune` and `sales-seller-recovery-dune` have **no `pipeline_cadence_watchlist` rows at all**, so they generate **zero** `cron_silent` noise — there is nothing to mute. Their failures (24h: 12/12 and 23/23, the known HTTP 402 datapoint cap) surface through the separate failure-count arm. Crons and routes left intact: a concurrent session repositioned `sales-ingest-dune` onto the 2020-21 gap today.

**3. `special_serial_holders` retired as a dead path — and it WAS wired to a live surface.**

- **25 rows against ~56,202 target tuples (0.04%)**, last written **2026-07-05**, and the table comment still advertised a "daily delta sweep". The only scheduled special-serial job in `cron.job` is `rpc-refresh-special-serial-owners-mv` (the working MV, **7,393 rows**); the `special-serial-{sweep,delta}` edge functions that write the table are **unscheduled**.
- **Grepped consumers first, as instructed. The three named readers** (`get_recently_traded_special_serials`, `get_special_serial_targets`, `resolve_special_serials_from_ownership`) **are consumed only by those two unscheduled edge functions** — dormant, not provably unused, so **nothing was dropped**; all three are labelled DORMANT in their DB comments with a pointer to the live path.
- **But one USER-FACING reader existed:** `app/moment/[id]/page.tsx` (`fetchSpecialSerialsForSerial`) read the empty table directly for the hero badge pills. Consequence: **the "Jersey Match" hero pill could never render**, and an empty pill row was indistinguishable from "this serial is not special". `#1` and `Perfect Serial` survived only because `derivedSerialBadges` recomputes those two deterministically.
- **Repointed at the working wmc-backed `get_edition_special_serials`** — the same RPC **this page already calls** for its edition-wide "Special serials" section, so the repoint **removes a DB round-trip rather than adding one**. Tags are mapped back into the legacy `badge_type` vocabulary, so `specialSerialLabel`, `SpecialSerialGlyph` (which accepts both vocabularies by design) and the `derivedSerialBadges` dedup all keep working untouched.

**4. Badge coverage — one gap closed, one proven NOT portable.**

- **All Day: 584 of 6,190 editions have no `badge_editions` row — confirmed exactly (90.57% coverage).** **Top Shot's mechanism is NOT portable, and that is the finding.** Top Shot self-heals via a GHA catalog sweep (`badge-sync?mode=catalog`), but All Day badges come from the Dapper Atlas `EditionService`, which **WAF-blocks Vercel egress AND datacenter runners** — that is exactly why the All Day writer runs on a residential runner (`scripts/ingest-allday-badges.mjs`). A GHA cron would be blocked at the source. **Also: the gap is not growing.** All 584 were created in a single batch on **2026-04-12** and none since; 352 are ULTIMATE tier; only 225 have any sale and 211 any owner. **Deliberately did NOT backfill** — writing `badge_editions` rows with no real Atlas badge data would be exactly the fabricated-data class killed in the pack-EV P0 above. **No change shipped; recorded as a residential-runner coverage limit.**
- **Golazos badge feed: the reported blocker was re-checked and was WRONG, so it is now WIRED.** The report said edition resolution was blocked (610/610 `cached_listings_v2` rows NULL `edition_id`) and hoped today's ownership fix would unblock it. **It did not:** all **9,494** Golazos wmc rows have **NULL `edition_key`**, so `flow_id -> wmc -> editions.external_id` resolves **0 of 610** (272 of 610 flow_ids *are* now in wmc — the missing bridge is `edition_key`, not ownership). **But a different bridge works and always did:** `sales.nft_id -> sales.edition_id` resolves **426 of 610, 0 ambiguous**, 184 unresolvable (never-traded NFTs have no sales row by definition). **So the blocker was resolution LOGIC, not data.**
- **Shipped the Golazos equivalent of `allday-badge-low-ask-refresh`:** `resolve_golazos_listing_edition_ids()` (NULL-only, **ambiguity-safe** — writes only when exactly one distinct `edition_id` exists, so a mis-keyed NFT stays NULL rather than being guessed), the `golazos_edition_floor_ask` view (exact mirror of `allday_edition_floor_ask`, `security_invoker=on`, **no anon grant**), `refresh_golazos_badge_low_ask()` (port of the All Day function **plus** a self-heal call to the resolver each tick, which the All Day path gets for free), and `cron.job rpc-golazos-badge-low-ask-refresh` at `10,40 * * * *` (offset off All Day's `*/30`).
- **Live proof:** `edition_id` **0 -> 426**; the floor-ask view **0 -> 135 editions**; first tick logged `updated: 34, cleared: 70`; `badge_editions` newest row moved **2026-07-21 -> 2026-07-25 20:33 UTC** (feed no longer frozen). **Note the honest direction of `low_ask`: 116/218 -> 67/218.** That is a *correction*, not a regression — **70 of the old 116 were stale asks for editions with no live listing**, held over from the frozen 07-21 snapshot. All 67 now correspond to a live ask. **`highest_offer` remains 0/218** — no Golazos offer writer exists; out of scope here.
- **Deliberately did NOT invent badge rows:** 68 of the 135 floor-ask editions have no `badge_editions` row, because **no Golazos badge-classification writer exists at all**. That is the remaining Golazos gap and is left open rather than papered over.
- **Revert:** `SELECT cron.unschedule('rpc-golazos-badge-low-ask-refresh'); DROP FUNCTION IF EXISTS public.refresh_golazos_badge_low_ask(); DROP VIEW IF EXISTS public.golazos_edition_floor_ask; DROP FUNCTION IF EXISTS public.resolve_golazos_listing_edition_ids(); UPDATE public.badge_editions SET low_ask = NULL WHERE collection_id = '06248cc4-b85f-47cd-af67-1855d14acd75';` (to undo the 426 `edition_id` writes: `UPDATE public.cached_listings_v2 SET edition_id = NULL WHERE collection_id = '06248cc4-b85f-47cd-af67-1855d14acd75';` — safe, that column was 100% NULL for Golazos before today).
- Migrations: `audit_20260725_golazos_listing_edition_resolver`, `..._fix_uuid_agg`, `audit_20260725_refresh_golazos_badge_low_ask`, `audit_20260725_cron_golazos_badge_low_ask_refresh`.
- **Trap worth keeping:** the resolver's first version used `min(sa.edition_id)` on a **uuid** column — there is no `min(uuid)` in Postgres, so it raised `42883` and resolved 0 rows. **This is the second time today** (`audit_20260725_resolve_sales_ingest_unresolved_fix_uuid_agg` was the first). Use `(array_agg(DISTINCT col))[1]` + `count(DISTINCT col)` in one LATERAL — it gives the candidate *and* the ambiguity count in a single pass.

### 2026-07-25 (Claude Code, interactive) — test-coverage pass (cont. 26): sniper-feed 50%→83% — and a TEST-HARNESS BUG that was silently voiding an existing test

Test-only, behavior-preserving. Biggest single-route jump of the whole program.

- **BUG FOUND IN THE HARNESS (the important part).** `makeSupabaseFixture` captures its fixtures object **by reference**. Any test that does `fx.tables = { ... }` (plain reassignment, the obvious idiom) **detaches** it — the fixture keeps serving the original object, so every table reads empty. The pre-existing `api-sniper-feed-compute` "runs the compute body end-to-end over a populated pool" case was therefore asserting on **zero deals** while appearing to pass: its only assertions were `Array.isArray(body.deals)` and `count === deals.length`, both trivially true on an empty feed. Diagnosed from the route's own `[sniper-feed] ts_listings: 0 rows` log. **Fix:** the mock now hands the fixture a live `Proxy` view of `fx.tables`, so both reassignment and in-place mutation are seen. **Any other test using this fixture with reassignment has the same latent defect — worth a sweep.**
- **`/api/sniper-feed` 50.3%st/34.9br → 82.8%/62.7.** With the fixture actually connected, added the data contract that makes the enrichment fan-out execute instead of early-returning on empties: `get_editions_for_sniper` (edition resolution parses `"Player — Set"` out of `edition.name` — the key nothing else supplies), `editions` → `fmv_snapshots` joined by uuid, `badge_editions` by player, `players` by jersey, and a `serial_fmv_estimate` RPC for the `#1`-serial path. Now covers `fetchTopShotPool` → `resolveEditionKeys` → `fetchFmvBatch` → `fetchBadgesByPlayers` → `fetchJerseyNumbers` → `attachSerialFmvEstimates` → build/sort/filter, plus the newest-snapshot-wins dedupe (stale duplicate ignored), `editions.thumbnail_url` preferred over the constructed asset URL, degradation on a `badge_editions` **and** a `players` read error, the editions-miss and no-FMV unpriced feeds, and `?limit=`.

### 2026-07-25 (Claude Code, interactive) — Dune has NOT reset (still 402 as of 16:11Z today) + the AllDay resolution lever is UNSAFE for TopShot (287 ambiguous nft_ids). Measurement only, nothing shipped.

Follow-up to the historical-sales measurement below, after Trevor said Dune may have reset and to keep going. Both findings are measured. Detail: handoff §5 "UPDATE".

- **Dune did NOT reset.** Last `ok` run **2026-07-24 06:11Z**; every tick since — 9 of them on 07-25, through **16:11:36Z** — fails `HTTP 402 … exceed your configured datapoint limit per billing cycle`, cursor frozen at `2025-06-19..2025-06-21`. Our telemetry can only prove Dune is still refusing us; **the account's billing-cycle date + datapoint balance need checking directly.**
- **DO NOT run `backfill_nft_edition_map_from_sales` for TopShot.** It is collection-parameterised so it looks like a drop-in, but (1) it resolves ambiguity by **latest-sale-wins** (`DISTINCT ON (nft_id) … ORDER BY sold_at DESC`), which was safe on AllDay only because AllDay had **0 ambiguous** nft_ids — **TopShot has 287 in the 2021 partition alone**, and sampled cases are cross-set **misattribution**, not the benign `::` re-key (`nft_id 102839 → 134:5038` AND `5:12` same day; `107831 → 29:584` AND `5:50`). Latest-wins would bake those into `nft_edition_map` → propagates into sale resolution → FMV. Needs an **ambiguity-safe variant** (`count(DISTINCT edition_id)=1` only, quarantine the rest). And (2) it only drains nft_ids already in `unmapped_sales`, which the Dune path never populates — so **"park unresolved rows" is a hard prerequisite**, not an optimisation.
- **Why the miss rate is ~85–90%, quantified:** of **106,559** distinct TopShot nft_ids in 2021 sales, only **702 are in `moments` (0.66%)** and 33 in `nft_edition_map` — and the Dune ingest resolves *only* via `moments`. `sales` (3.01M resolved TS rows) is the far richer source, which is why park-then-resolve is right and why it must be ambiguity-safe first.

### 2026-07-25 (Claude Code, interactive) — SHIPPED (DB-only): closed the 2 hard smoke-test security violations the sentinel flagged (2 AllDay audit tables had RLS off AND were anon-readable)

Sentinel reported `hard 37/38` — `check_public_security_invariants()`: `rls_off_base_table` on `audit_20260725_allday_v1_unsplittable_retag` (19,589 rows) and `audit_20260725_allday_unmapped_dedupe_tx_nft`. Both created by today's AllDay unmapped-residue work **without RLS**, and both measured **anon-readable** (`has_table_privilege('anon',…,'SELECT')` = true) — i.e. queryable at `/rest/v1/<table>` with the public anon key. Contents are internal ingest bookkeeping (`unmapped_id` / `nft_id` / `transaction_hash` / resolution hints) — no PII, but internal state, and it broke the platform invariant "0 public tables with `rowsecurity=false`". This is the **route-gating ≠ data-gating** trap again (CLAUDE.md security posture).

- **Migration `audit_20260725_secure_allday_residue_audit_tables`:** `ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY` + `REVOKE ALL … FROM anon, authenticated` on both, in the SAME migration (no create-then-normalize-later window), + table comments. **Pattern was not invented — it was measured:** of 64 `audit_*` tables, 62 already had RLS on and only these 2 were anon-readable; the canonical shape (verified on 3 secured siblings) is **RLS on with ZERO policies** (deny-all to non-bypassrls roles) with `service_role`/`postgres` retaining access, which is how every consumer reads them.
- **Verified functionally, not from `information_schema`:** both now `rls_on=true, policies=0, anon_sel=false, auth_sel=false, svc_sel=true`; `check_public_security_invariants()` → **0 violations**; `rls_off` public base tables → **0**; anon-readable `audit_*` tables → **0**.
- **Timing note:** the 17:00:37Z smoke run still showed the failure because it called the endpoint seconds before the migration landed at **17:00:24Z**; a fresh run was dispatched to confirm. Sandbox egress to prod is proxy-blocked (403 CONNECT), so the endpoint could not be curled directly from here.
- **Revert:** `ALTER TABLE public.audit_20260725_allday_v1_unsplittable_retag DISABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY; ALTER TABLE public.audit_20260725_allday_unmapped_dedupe_tx_nft DISABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY; GRANT SELECT ON public.audit_20260725_allday_v1_unsplittable_retag, public.audit_20260725_allday_unmapped_dedupe_tx_nft TO anon, authenticated;` (restoring the anon grant is NOT recommended — it was the defect).

### 2026-07-25 (Claude Code, interactive) — MEASURED the historical-sales gap (Trevor: "we should have all historical sales"). Blocked on Dune billing + an 85–90% edition-resolution miss. NOTHING SHIPPED — decision required.

Measurement only, no code/DB change. Trevor rejected "accept the loss", so I measured. **The 23505 bug is a rounding error next to a missing ERA.** Full write-up: [docs/handoff-2026-07-25-sales-indexer-23505-batch-loss.md](../handoff-2026-07-25-sales-indexer-23505-batch-loss.md) §5.

- **The gap, self-evident from our own data:** `sales` = 4.56M rows. By partition 2020 79k / **2021 166k** / 2022 748k / 2023 **1.21M** / 2024 804k / 2025 738k / 2026 815k. **Top Shot alone: 166,141 in 2021 (mania year) vs 679,691 in 2023 (quiet year) — 4.1×.** (TS-to-TS; the raw 2023 partition of 1,209,696 includes other collections.) Intra-2021 TopShot is inverted vs reality (Jan 74,969 → Feb **27,552** → Mar 7,133). The 2020–21 V1 `Market.MomentPurchased` era is essentially absent.
- **Blocker 1 — `DUNE-DATAPOINT-CAP-402` (hard stop).** `sales-ingest-dune` fires every 2h, **4 ok / 37 runs**; every tick since 07-24 06:23Z dies on `HTTP 402 … exceed your configured datapoint limit per billing cycle`. Cursor parked at **2025-06-21** against a 2019-01-01 floor (~6 months done of ~7 years), `inserted: 0`. The 07-19 `window_days` 7→2 hedge did NOT clear it — the cap is per *billing cycle*, not per request.
- **Blocker 2 — edition resolution, the deeper one.** Even on the 4 successful runs, ~**85–90%** of each batch was dropped `skipped_unresolved` (e.g. 152,195 found → 139,266 unresolved → **1,074 inserted**). Cause: `nft_id → edition` resolves via `moments`, which holds only **565,345** rows (`nft_edition_map` 130,946) against a TopShot mint universe in the millions. **And `apply_sales_ingest_external` does NOT park the unresolved rows** (verified against the live function definition — no `unmapped_sales` reference); they are counted and discarded, so every Dune datapoint spent on them is spent again on any re-run.
- **⇒ Key conclusion: lifting the Dune cap TODAY would burn ~85–90% of the spend on rows we immediately throw away.** Recommended order: (1) free — park unresolved rows in `unmapped_sales`; (2) free — extend the AllDay-proven `backfill_nft_edition_map_from_sales` immutable-edition trick (pg_cron jobid 215) to TopShot, then re-measure the miss rate; (3) only then size the Dune spend, and evaluate the free Flow-REST lane that already beat Dune once here (`sales_counterparty_recovered` 26,127 → 208,834).
- **Not shipped deliberately:** (1)+(2) are `sales` ingest/resolution logic (off-limits for autonomous shipping) and (3) is a billing decision. All three are Trevor's call.

### 2026-07-25 (Claude Code, interactive — bug hunt cont.) — offers-sweep :: subedition map truncated at 1,000 rows → ~72% of Top Shot parallel editions missing their offer/ask cache

Follow-up to the same bug hunt: `fetchSubeditionMap` in `app/api/cron/offers-sweep/route.ts` read the `::` parallel editions with a bare `.limit(10000)`, which PostgREST silently clamps to 1,000. ### 2026-07-25 (Claude Code, interactive — "implement a TODO" + bug hunt) — candy-sales-indexer no longer silently drops NEW sales co-batched with a duplicate (23505)

Task: implement a straightforward TODO + look for general bugs. Every live-code TODO is gated/shelved/resolved (Trade Hub needs the undeployed contract; Candy/Panini go-live are operator/editorial gates; the rest are `RESOLVED`-annotated comments), so the deliverable is a real bug fix.

- **BUG FIXED (code) — `app/api/candy-sales-indexer/route.ts` batch-insert data loss.** A `sales` batch insert is all-or-nothing: a single duplicate `transaction_hash` (23505) fails the whole ≤100-row statement and writes NONE of it. The old 23505 branch swallowed the entire batch (`// dupes — already recorded`), silently dropping every co-batched NEW sale; because nothing lands the DB high-water cursor never advances past them, so the same dupe re-drops the batch on every tick = permanent loss. Reachable via ME offset-pagination overlap and multi-item txns sharing a signature. Candy is now printing ~53 sales/24h, so the path is live. Fix: on 23505 (like every other error) fall through to the EXISTING row-by-row retry — genuine dupes skip individually while new rows land. ### 2026-07-25 (Claude Code, interactive ~01:55 PT) — pack "What's Inside" infinite spinner BOUNDED (server was healthy all along — the client never swapped the streamed segment in) + entity hero montages stopped painting 4 MB IPFS masters into 72px tiles (~1,460× per tile)

Two user-facing defects from the 07-25 audit, both verified live before and after. Code-only: **no migration, no `vercel.json`, no pricing/FMV/EV logic touched.** `tsc --noEmit` 0 errors; full suite **804 files / 5,519 tests, 0 failures** (+47 new). Both fixes proven to bite by reverting them (11 of 16 new assertions fail on the old code).

- **P1 — pack `What's Inside` spun on "Loading pack contents…" forever. FIXED, but NOT the way my first commit `7c0a0d5f` claimed — that approach was proven non-functional against prod and replaced in the same session; this bullet supersedes it.** The section is an async server component behind `<Suspense>`, so it ships in the tail of the initial response — there is no client fetch to observe, which is why the audit's "zero API requests fired" was a red herring rather than a clue. **The data path was never at fault:** `get_pack_contents` returns **24 rows in 67 ms** for TS dist 1599 (`≤731 ms` across the 40 largest pools), and a full `curl` of the production page returns the completely rendered `<h2>What's Inside</h2>` section, its hidden `<div id="S:1">` payload, a complete RSC flight payload (every `$L` ref has a matching row, incl. `56`) and the trailing `$RC("B:1","S:1")` script as the final bytes — **all in ~1.1 s**. Yet a real Chrome tab on the same URL sat on the fallback indefinitely with `document.readyState` `complete`, `$RC` defined, and `#S:1` **present but unconsumed**; no console error, no Sentry event. So the server produces and delivers the content and the client never performs the swap. **THE DECISIVE FINDING (measured live, and it invalidated my first fix): React does not hydrate the fallback of a dehydrated Suspense boundary** — the visible fallback `<section>` carried **zero `__reactFiber$` keys** while a sibling section carried them. A watchdog/timer placed inside a Suspense fallback therefore **never mounts and can never fire**, which is exactly why my first attempt (a self-bounding `PackContentsFallback` client component, shipped in `7c0a0d5f`) did nothing: post-deploy the page still spun after 20 s. That component has been **deleted**. **The working fix: the grid no longer depends on client stream completion at all.** `fetchPackContents` + `fetchExhaustedCount` moved into the SHELL and render via a new server `PackContentsSection`, so the content is visible in the initial HTML; the remaining streamed group (sales history · top pulls) now uses **`fallback={null}`** — the same choice `PackStreamedTop` already makes for supplementary content in this file — so nothing can spin forever again. **This does NOT re-create the pre-P3 pool fan-out: the two reads were MOVED off the streamed group, not added** (shell 1→2 reads, streamed group 4→3; total DB work per request unchanged, and both reads are ≤731 ms). **Also fixed a second, independent silent failure in the same block:** `fetchPackContents` swallowed RPC errors into `[]` and the panel was gated on `length > 0`, so a failed read **deleted the whole panel with nothing on screen to say so** — it now returns `null` for a load failure vs `[]` for a genuinely empty pool, and renders honest, different copy for each. Guard: `__tests__/pack-dist-contents-not-streamed.test.ts` (5 structural assertions — contents read in the shell, section emitted outside the boundary, no text fallback, null-vs-empty distinction; proven to redden when the grid is put back behind a skeleton fallback). **Revert:** `git revert <sha>` (reverts to the still-broken streamed arrangement — not recommended).
- **P1 — entity hero montages were downloading full-resolution IPFS masters into 72px tiles.** Root cause is a data shape, not a component bug: since Top Shot pinned all media to IPFS, `editions.thumbnail_url` is an `ipfs.dapperlabs.com/ipfs/<cid>` URL for **10,289 of the 12,920 TS editions that have art (79.6%)** and `ipfs.io/ipfs/<cid>` for **518/518 UFC** — and those CIDs are the **2880×2880 archival masters, measured live at 3,870,931 / 3,961,256 / 4,181,732 / 4,655,501 bytes**. `HeroMontage` rendered five of them at `fetchPriority="high"` into 72px boxes ⇒ ~20 MB of blocking image bytes on every Set / Team / Series page, which is exactly why montage tiles showed as broken-image alt text or blank in the sweep. **The IPFS gateways cannot resize** (verified: `?width=` is ignored — byte-identical 3,961,256 both ways — and `/cdn-cgi/image/…` 403s), **but Top Shot's own CDN can**: `assets.nbatopshot.com/media/<nft_id>/image?width=N` returns a real per-moment derivative at **2,716 bytes for width=144 vs ~4,000,000 for the master ≈ 1,460×** (also measured 1,503 B @48 · 31,507 B @400 · 453,616 B unsized). The entity RPCs **already** return a representative `rep_nft_id` per edition — confirmed populated on `get_set_editions` and `get_team_top_editions`, and it is what the *grid* tiles on these same pages already use off the *same array*; `HeroMontage`'s narrow `MontageItem` interface was simply discarding it. So the montage now prefers the sized derivative at 2× its 72px slot, keeps the IPFS proxy as an **error fallback** (a 404 on the sized URL demotes that one tile instead of pruning it), and drops `fetchPriority="high"` from what is an `aria-hidden` decorative strip. Extracted `tsSizedMomentImage()` into `lib/entity-editions-grid-format.ts` and made `buildEditionImageCandidates(e, slug, width)` width-parameterised (default unchanged at 400, so **every existing grid caller is byte-identical**). **COST: zero added spend — deliberately.** `next/image` is used in exactly 1 file repo-wide (60 files use raw `<img>`), and Vercel bills image optimization per source image transformed, so with ~19.5k TS editions routing it through `/_next/image` would create a real metered bill; adding `sharp` resizing to `/api/public/ipfs-media/[cid]` was also rejected (that route is `runtime = "edge"`, where sharp cannot run, and `sharp` is only a transitive dep, not in `package.json`). Pushing the resize onto Top Shot's CDN costs nothing. Intrinsic `width`/`height`, `loading` and `decoding="async"` were already correct — layout was already reserved — so bytes were the whole defect. Tests: `__tests__/component-HeroMontage.test.tsx` (9 cases) + 8 in `entity-editions-grid-format.test.ts`. **Revert:** `git revert <sha>`.
- **P1 (same class, second instance — FIXED as far as is free) — team-page PLAYER tiles were also painting IPFS masters, and with no layout reservation at all.** Found while verifying the montage fix: `/nba-top-shot/team/memphis-grizzlies` still pulled **53** `/api/public/ipfs-media/<cid>` images after it — a *different* component (`PlayersGridPaginated`), which falls back to `portrait_thumbnail` whenever a player has no `headshot_url`. Measured live at **397 KB–3.44 MB** each into a ~200px tile, and the tags carried **no `width`/`height`, no `loading`, no `decoding`** — so 53 multi-megabyte fetches all fired at once with unreserved boxes, which is the bulk of that page's ~27 MB and the visible blank-tile flash. **Unlike the edition tiles there is no resizable upstream to prefer:** `PlayerTile` carries no `rep_nft_id` (so `tsSizedMomentImage` has nothing to build from) and the IPFS gateways ignore `?width=`. Shipped the free half only — intrinsic `width`/`height` (reserves the box) plus `loading="lazy"` + `decoding="async"` (keeps the offscreen ones out of the initial burst). **Byte size per portrait is unchanged and is honestly still wrong**; closing that needs one of the two options in the carried item below. Guard: `__tests__/component-PlayersGridPaginated-image-weight.test.tsx` (5 cases, incl. that the mitigations apply to the headshot path and to every tile, not just the first). **Revert:** `git revert <sha>`.
- **CARRIED, needs a Trevor decision — the same IPFS-master weight still hits UFC (518/518 editions), the ~2,631 TS editions with no `rep_nft_id`, and every player portrait that falls back to `portrait_thumbnail` (53 on one team page alone).** They have no resizable upstream: UFC art is `ipfs.io` only and Dapper's gateway won't transform. Fixing those requires resizing inside `/api/public/ipfs-media/[cid]`, which means switching that route `edge → nodejs` and adding `sharp` as a real dependency. That is **not metered image-optimization billing** — it is lambda CPU on cache MISS only, and since CIDs are content-addressed and the route already sets `s-maxage=31536000, immutable`, each `(cid,width)` transforms exactly once ever and then serves from the edge forever. Estimated cost is therefore near-zero but non-zero (a one-time ~4 MB PNG decode per unique tile size, plus added cold-start weight on a hot public route). **Not shipped: it is a dependency + runtime change on a public media path, which is Trevor's call, not an autonomous one.**

### 2026-07-24 (Claude Code, interactive, Trevor-directed) — RTR lock-ROI playoff-points estimate v2: fold tier + serial scarcity into the estimate (implements the standing TODO(lock-roi-calibration)); the board's ranking is no longer integer-floor rounding noise

Code-only to `main` (`app/api/rtr/lock-roi/route.ts` + its test). Authed RTR pro route; auto-deploys. Couldn't run vitest/tsc locally (sandbox `@noble/hashes@2.2.0` lockfile artifact, do-not-fix) — relies on CI `typecheck` + `unit-tests`; model math + the 3 new assertions were pre-verified with a dependency-free script.

- **What.** v1 was `estimatedPlayoffPoints = floor(fmv / 10)`, which made points-per-dollar a flat `1/10` for every moment — so the board was effectively sorted by the integer FLOOR (rounding noise), and any moment under $10 rounded to 0 points and sank to the bottom regardless of quality. v2 scales the FMV base by the two signals the TODO called out: an ordinal/relative **tier** weight (`COMMON 1.0 · FANDOM 1.1 · RARE 1.6 · LEGENDARY 3.0 · ULTIMATE 6.0`) and a bounded **serial-scarcity** factor (`1 + 0.25·e^(−serial/250)`, range [1.0, 1.25], lower serial ⇒ higher). points-per-dollar (= tierWeight·scarcity/10) now varies with moment quality, and is computed from the UNROUNDED estimate so a cheap moment keeps a real non-zero ratio instead of being dumped. Weights are documented **interim heuristics** — the absolute Run 2 curve still needs empirical calibration once real scoring data is collected; this is an honest ordering, not a precision claim.
- **Tests.** +3 regression tests in `__tests__/api-rtr-lock-roi.test.ts`: rarer tier outranks common at equal FMV, lower serial outranks higher at equal FMV+tier, and a sub-$10 moment is no longer zeroed out.
- **Revert:** `git revert <this code commit sha>` (reverts the route + test together; no DB/data state touched).

### 2026-07-20 (Cowork, interactive) — prewarm reports REAL per-collection results instead of hardcoded "deferred"; welcome email stops telling new signups their live collections are "Coming soon"

Triggered by the day's signup (chase.standen, 320 moments). The funnel watch came back clean, but reading the row exposed a user-facing lie in the welcome email.

- **ROOT CAUSE (a stale hardcode, not a missing scanner).** `lib/allow-list/prewarm.ts` hardcoded the four non-TopShot collections to `"deferred"` with the comment *"seeders not yet shipped"*. That comment predates `dispatchBackfillAndSeedWallet`, which fires `/api/wallet-backfill-multicollection` — a route whose `SYNC_COLLECTIONS` + `FIRE_AND_FORGET_COLLECTIONS` cover **all five collections**. So prewarm was already scanning everything and then reporting four-fifths of it as not-yet-supported. The welcome email renders `deferred` as the badge **"Coming soon"**, so chase was told NFL All Day wasn't available while holding **67 All Day moments that were indexed 93 seconds later** (dispatch 20:44:07Z → last wmc row 20:45:40Z). The hourly reconciler then silently corrected the row at 22:12Z — after the email had already gone out. **Correction to my own earlier read of that signup: the data was NOT ~90 min late; only the reporting was.**
- **SHIPPED (code) — `lib/allow-list/prewarm.ts` + `app/api/admin/allow-list/prewarm-drain/route.ts`.** Prewarm now captures a pre-dispatch baseline of `wallet_backfill_state`, dispatches the backfill, then polls that table (the authoritative per-collection completion signal the pipeline already writes) for a bounded window and records real per-collection status + `last_found_count`. Freshness is decided by **`last_scanned_at` CHANGING from the baseline**, never by row existence — those rows persist across scans, so a returning wallet's stale row must not read as this run's result; comparing against a baseline instead of an app-server timestamp also makes it immune to lambda↔Postgres clock skew. Collections that finish in-window → `complete` with a real count (a finished walk that found 0 is `complete`, found:0 — strictly more honest than `deferred`, and it stops the reconciler re-examining a settled collection). Stragglers → **`in_progress` ("Loading…"), never `deferred` ("Coming soon")**, and still land in `complete_partial` so the hourly reconciler finishes them exactly as before.
- **Budget sized off the real case, not a guess.** Default 120s; a 60s budget would have timed out chase's own 93s walk and shown "Loading…" on a fully-indexed wallet. `prewarm-drain` (maxDuration 300, claims ≤5) divides its remaining wall clock across rows still to process (cap 150s, 60s/row reserve), recomputed per row off the live clock so the sum can never exceed the deadline and a fast row hands its unspent budget to the next. Single-row claims — the common case at current signup rate — get the full cap; a 5-row burst degrades to a short poll plus the reconciler.
- **Cost:** the welcome email is now delayed by the poll (≈95s for a chase-sized wallet) in exchange for being accurate. No new pipeline, no new cron, no schema change, no DB migration.
- **Tests:** 3 new cases in `__tests__/allow-list-prewarm.test.ts` — real counts read from `wallet_backfill_state` (the `found:67` assertion is unreachable under the old hardcode, so the guard is real), stale-baseline row → `in_progress` not a false `complete`, and no-wallet → still `deferred`. 21/21 green across the prewarm + drain suites; `tsc` clean on all changed files.
- **Revert:** `git revert <code sha>`.

### 2026-07-20 (Claude Code, interactive) — DECLINED monitor 1805Z Item 1 (ALLDAY-LOCK-REFRESH proconfig fix) as PROVEN INERT; durable finding: fn `proconfig statement_timeout` does NOT extend the outer RPC call's ceiling on the PostgREST/service_role path either (not just pg_cron)

- **NO PROD CHANGE this turn** (a diagnostic probe fn was created and dropped, net-zero). Recording because it **declines a queued monitor item with proof** and **flags a prior ship for re-examination** — the night pass must not apply the inert fix.
- **Monitor 1805Z Item 1 proposed** `ALTER FUNCTION get_allday_lock_refresh_wallets(integer) SET statement_timeout='120s'`, mirroring the 07-20 `get_lock_check_batch` ship, and explicitly asked for *measured* confirmation (not assumption) given last night's proconfig lesson. **Measured — it is inert.** Controlled probe: a fn with `proconfig statement_timeout='60s'` whose body runs `pg_sleep(12)`, called with the session default at 5s, **died at 5s**; the identical fn called with the session at 20s **survived** (returned 1). So the *caller's* session/role default binds the outer `SELECT fn()` — the fn's proconfig cannot extend it (the timer is armed at outer-statement start, before the fn's SET fires). This is the **same mechanism the 07-20 night pass proved on pg_cron**, now shown to hold on the **Vercel-cron → PostgREST → `supabaseAdmin.rpc()`** path too.
- **Ground truth:** `allday-lock-refresh-batch` calls the RPC via `supabaseAdmin` = **`service_role`, whose role default is `statement_timeout=30s`** (`pg_roles.rolconfig`; anon 3s / authenticated 8s / authenticator 8s). `get_allday_lock_refresh_wallets` is a full per-wallet aggregate over ~334k AllDay wmc rows (`GROUP BY wallet_address … ORDER BY min(lock_checked_at)`), which crosses 30s under daytime contention → the 6/24 `stage: wallet_fetch` timeouts. A 120s proconfig cannot help; the real ceiling stays 30s.
- **FLAG (for night pass / owner): `get_lock_check_batch`'s 07-20 `statement_timeout=120s` proconfig (`audit_20260720_get_lock_check_batch_statement_timeout_120s`) is inert by the same proof** — it too is called via `supabaseAdmin.rpc()` (service_role 30s). Its reported "doubled throughput" was NOT the timeout (contention variance or the concurrent scope-to-2-collections change). Not touched this turn (an inert proconfig is harmless; removing it is zero-gain churn) — recorded so the belief doesn't propagate again.
- **QUEUED (real fix, NOT auto-shipped) — ALLDAY-LOCK-REFRESH-SELECTION-COST (LOW/MED).** The only genuine remedies are to make the selection complete under 30s or move it off the hot path: a covering index `wallet_moments_cache (collection_id, wallet_address, lock_checked_at)` would turn the seq-scan+hashagg into an index-driven group-min, but that is a **new index on the 1.6M-row hottest, actively-written table** — exactly the write-amplification the 07-16 IOPS-diet program weighs deliberately, so it wants an owner/night-pass call with measurement, not an autonomous add. Reducing `p_limit` does NOT help (the GROUP BY+ORDER-BY-min must scan all AllDay rows before LIMIT). Monitor's own read: pipeline is *converging* (AllDay `lock_checked_at` 85.2%, lock_flips decaying to single digits), so this is throughput drag on a near-finished first pass, not a break. **Target metric:** `allday-lock-refresh` `wallet_fetch` fails → 0/24h once the selection is index-driven.

### 2026-07-20 (Claude Code, interactive) — both watchlist routes: same PostgREST 1000-row-clamp bug (fmv_snapshots DESC → fmv_current); large watchlists silently lost FMV/floor + below_target alerts on overflow editions

- **SHIPPED (code, correctness fix — same class as the concierge fix above).** Both `app/api/profile/watchlist/route.ts` (GET) and `app/api/watchlist/route.ts` (GET) read every watched edition's FMV from **raw `fmv_snapshots` ordered `computed_at DESC` with no `.limit()`**, deduping latest-per-edition in JS (one even commented "DISTINCT ON latest"). Neither route caps watchlist size, so a collector watching **~29+ TS editions** (daily history ~34 rows/edition) crosses PostgREST's **1000-row clamp**, and because the order is global-DESC, the overflow editions **silently lose their FMV/floor** — and on `/api/profile/watchlist`, a null floor makes `below_target` read false, so a watched moment that IS below its alert price **stops flagging**. Fix = read from **`fmv_current`** (`DISTINCT ON (edition_id) … computed_at DESC`, verified via `pg_get_viewdef`) which returns ≤1 row/edition (well under the cap). Both routes use the `service_role` client (verified readable). Both regression suites updated to the `fmv_current` fixture key (mocks key by table name).
  - **Honest tradeoff (measured, deemed favorable):** `fmv_current` is the *absolute* latest row, whereas the old loop skipped null-fmv rows to find the latest *non-null*. Of 26,588 editions, **4,923 have a null-fmv latest row, but only 715 (~2.7%) have an older non-null value** that would now render as null instead of a stale (often months-old) price — arguably an honesty improvement (the edition is currently NO_DATA), and negligible beside the clamp loss that hit *every* edition on a large watchlist arbitrarily by recency. The other 4,208 null-latest editions never had a value (no change).
  - **Not run locally** (no node_modules here); relying on CI `unit-tests` + `typecheck` (both `Supabase = any`-typed / mock-keyed-by-table, so type-clean). **Revert:** `git revert <sha>`. **Target metric:** watchlist FMV/floor/below_target correct for watchlists of any size, not just ≤~28 editions.

### 2026-07-20 (Cowork, interactive) — RETRACTION: "CREATE INDEX is blocked by the tooling" was wrong. Non-concurrent works fine at this scale and fails BETTER. Serial-premiums board **418,933 -> 2,113 buffers (198x)**

I queued `SALES-SERIAL-1-PARTIAL-INDEX` as blocked on tooling an hour ago. That was a bad call and I want the reasoning corrected in place, because the queue entry would have sent someone hunting for a psql session they never needed.

- **What I got wrong: I generalised from ONE failed attempt.** Earlier tonight `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY` on `pack_rips` (1.7 GB, 3.58M rows) timed out mid-build and left an invalid index I had to clean up. From that I concluded index creation as a class was unreachable here. **Only CONCURRENTLY is unreachable** (bare statement times out; cannot be combined with `SET statement_timeout` because MCP multi-statement calls are transaction-wrapped).
- **A NON-concurrent build is not just possible, its failure mode is strictly better.** Plain `CREATE INDEX` is transactional: a timeout rolls the whole thing back and leaves **nothing** behind. CONCURRENTLY is the one that strands an invalid index. I had the risk exactly backwards.
- **Scale made it a non-event:** `sales_2026` is 216 MB / 773,488 rows and the partial predicate matches only 2,168 rows. The resulting index is **144 kB**. The SHARE lock blocks writes for one 216 MB scan against ~183 writes/hour (~3/min). Partial indexes on this partition were already established practice (`sales_2026_collection_id_idx` is `WHERE serial_number = 0`).
- **SHIPPED — `audit_20260720_sales_serial1_partial_index`.** `(collection, edition_id, sold_at DESC) WHERE serial_number = 1` on `sales_2026`, plus the same on the empty `sales_2027` as forward insurance (instant), matching the `idx_sales_2027_null_serial` precedent. Column order mirrors the consumer exactly: filter `collection`, then `DISTINCT ON (edition_id) ORDER BY edition_id, sold_at DESC`.
- **MEASURED: the Parallel Seq Scan is gone**, replaced by `Index Scan using idx_sales_2026_serial1`. **Buffers 28,867 -> 2,113 (13.7x further), and 418,933 -> 2,113 (198x) against where this board started tonight.** Wall time 461 -> 389 ms; the residual 368 ms is cold-read I/O on first touch of a brand-new index (454 read buffers) and will drop warm — **the buffer count is the durable win, and it was always the point: this was an IOPS problem, not a latency one.**
- **Verified unchanged:** board returns **376** rows, same leaders (Jokić 1,125x, LeBron 875x, Wembanyama 433x). Invalid indexes **0**. Health: secdef `[]` · RLS-off `[]` · stalled `[]` · pg_cron none. Writes flowing throughout (newest sale 04:58Z, 176 pipeline runs/30 min) — the SHARE lock caused no visible disruption.
- **Durable rule: distinguish CONCURRENTLY from plain CREATE INDEX before declaring index work impossible here.** Plain builds are available and safe for small/partial indexes on partitions; reserve the "needs an external session" verdict for genuinely large non-partial builds where a multi-minute SHARE lock is the real blocker.

Two findings, one shipped, one deliberately NOT shipped.

- **Triage method worth reusing: `min_exec_time` separates "still slow" from "already fixed".** The five remaining queue entries all have a FAST floor — `topshot_market_index_daily` 1.58s · `v_topshot_pack_ev_calibrated` 2.28s · `get_insights_hub_stats()` 2.54s · `get_market_pulse_windows()` 3.05s · `topshot_serial_premiums_board` 5.90s — against means of 15-19s. **None is the "can never succeed" class the pack boards were** (those had min ≈ mean ≈ 26s/58s). Their 26-30s maxima are CONTENTION, not structure. `get_insights_hub_stats` in particular confirms the 07-18 rewrite worked; its 18.3s mean is historical. **Re-measure with min, not mean, before treating a queue entry as broken.**
- **And tonight's work should itself lower their maxima**, since the four MVs removed ~106s of repeated heavy scanning per page view from a shared, IOPS-constrained instance. Re-measure after 24h of the new steady state before doing anything else here.
- **SHIPPED — `audit_20260720_topshot_pack_market_ev_from_mv`.** After materializing the sales aggregate, `pack_ev_latest` became the dominant remaining cost on that board: 435 ms of 475 ms and **244,541 shared buffer hits per read** (index scan over `pack_ev_history` with a correlated SubPlan at 33,414 loops), doubled by the two-page read. Repointed the `ev` CTE to **`mv_pack_ev_latest`, which already existed**, is refreshed every 10 min, has identical columns and row count (1,824), and already carries the `(dist_id, collection_id)` index — `pack_table_rows` already read it; this just extends that choice. **474.7 -> 251.4 ms, and buffers 249,293 -> 2,184 (114x).** Cumulative on this board: **9,908 -> 251 ms (39x), 448,464 -> 2,184 buffers (205x).** Verified byte-identical output: 1,233 rows, 319 with a ratio, same top-3 discounts (Extra Spice 0.08x/$194, 8430 0.20x/$69, Elite 0.24x/$125).
- **DELIBERATELY NOT REPOINTED — `v_topshot_pack_realized_ev`, and the reason is the interesting part.** Comparing the view against the MV column by column: **`pack_price` differs on 0 of 1,824 rows, but `gross_ev` differs on 289.** That drift is NOT staleness — only **2** rows differ in `snapshotted_at`. `pack_ev_latest` carries a LIVE correlated filter against `pack_ask_state` (`NOT EXISTS (... gross_ev > 3 * lowest_ask)`), so as asks move a **different history row wins the DISTINCT ON without the timestamp changing**. The MV can therefore hold a genuinely different row, not merely an older one. `v_topshot_pack_market` consumes only `pack_price` (0 diffs) so it is unaffected; `v_topshot_pack_realized_ev` consumes `gross_ev`/`pack_ev`/`value_ratio`/`price_source`, so repointing it would have **silently changed the modeled EV that the published model-vs-reality board compares against**. It sits at 2.8s (9% of budget) and needs no fix.
- **Generalisable lesson: "the MV has the same columns and row count" is NOT sufficient to swap.** Equivalence has to be checked per-column against the columns the caller actually consumes. Had I swapped both views on the row-count match, one public board would have kept working and the other would have quietly started publishing different numbers.
- **Health after:** secdef `[]` · RLS-off `[]` · stalled `[]` · pg_cron failures none · invalid indexes 0.

### 2026-07-20 (Cowork, interactive) — SWEEP: the 30s-timeout class is SYSTEMIC across `/insights`, not two boards. Seven read paths sit at 95-100% of budget. Ranked list + the method that found them

Rather than guess board-by-board, pulled real production timings from `pg_stat_statements` and split them **by `userid`** — the discriminator that makes this legible. Cron work runs as `postgres`/`cron_heavy` with a **600s** budget, so its 100-600s entries are fine and expected; only reads executed as **`service_role` carry the 30s budget**. Filtering to that role isolates page reads from maintenance.

**Read paths at risk (role=service_role, 30s budget):**

| Backing read | mean | max | % of budget at max | Surface |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `v_allday_pack_market` | 22.7s | **29.3s** | **98%** | /insights/allday-pack-market |
| `v_topshot_pack_market` | 19.8s | **29.9s** | **99.7%** | /insights/topshot-pack-market |
| `v_topshot_pack_ev_calibrated` | 19.1s | 26.5s | 88% | pack-reality downstream |
| `get_insights_hub_stats()` | 18.3s | **29.8s** | **99%** | the /insights HUB itself |
| `get_market_pulse_windows()` | 15.3s | **29.7s** | **99%** | /insights/market-pulse |
| `topshot_serial_premiums_board` | 15.1s | 28.4s | 95% | /insights/serial-premiums |
| `topshot_market_index_daily` | 14.9s | 29.5s | 98% | /insights/market (The RPC Index) |

- **Read this as coin-flips, not outages.** Every one of these has *completed* — they are one contention spike from the same silent empty state that hid on the two pack-reality boards. The two I fixed tonight were simply the ones already past the line (26.3s intermittent, 58.2s certain).
- **CAVEAT, stated because it changes how to act on the table: `pg_stat_statements` means are CUMULATIVE since the last reset**, so they include pre-optimisation executions. `get_insights_hub_stats()` in particular was rewritten 19.7s -> 5.7s on 07-18, so its 18.3s mean is likely dominated by old calls. **Re-measure any row with a fresh EXPLAIN before acting on it** — do not treat this table as current truth, treat it as a ranked candidate list.
- **SELF-FLAG: my own clamp fix put `v_topshot_pack_market` at MORE risk, and I should say so.** At 1,233 qualifying rows `fetchAllPaged` issues **two** reads of that view. Quiet-window EXPLAIN says 837 ms (so two pages ≈ 1.7s, and the board verifiably rendered 1,233 live), but the production mean of 19.8s says the quiet measurement is not the whole story — under contention two reads could total ~40s against a 30s budget. **It works today and is verified; it is thinner than I would like.** Correct fix is the same MV treatment, not reverting the truncation fix.
- **QUEUED — INSIGHTS-READ-PATH-TIMEOUT-HARDENING (MED).** Materialize or push filters down on the rows above, worst-first. `v_allday_pack_market` and `v_topshot_pack_market` first (both public boards, both ~99% at max, and the latter now double-read). Deliberately NOT attempted tonight: that is 6+ view rewrites at the end of a long session, and I already shipped one regression today by moving on an insufficiently-measured assumption.
- **The reusable method, worth keeping:** `pg_stat_statements JOIN pg_roles ON rolname = userid`, filter `rolname IN ('service_role','authenticator','authenticated','anon')`, `mean_exec_time > 8000`. That one query separates "page read approaching its cliff" from "cron job legitimately taking minutes" — the distinction that made this class invisible until now.

The function call and the verification subqueries were in ONE statement, so every subquery read the same pre-write snapshot. Re-reading in a separate statement showed it had worked. That is a real behaviour trade-off and an owner decision, not a doc fix.
- **Also recorded at the callsite:** the CRON-30S ordering trap (cron-job.org's hard 30s cap vs runs already at 17-27s; raise the batch first and the entry can be auto-disabled, silently stopping lock checks) and the fact that **on-view refresh**, not this batch, is what makes displayed locks trustworthy today.

### 2026-07-20 (Cowork, interactive) — BOTH Dune pipelines hit the account DATAPOINT cap (HTTP 402); window_days 7 -> 2 as a hedge; free Flow-REST worker is the sustainable path

- **THE FAILURE.** `sync-sales-ingest-dune` last succeeded 3:11pm PT (9 windows, 865 inserted / 34,064 filled), then 402 at 5:11 / 7:11 / 9:11pm. `sync-sales-seller-recovery-dune` has 402'd every tick since 6:47pm, parked at `2026-01-15..2026-01-22`. Error body: *"This api request would exceed your configured datapoint limit per billing cycle."*
- **THE LESSON — the binding Dune constraint is DATAPOINTS, not CREDITS.** Budget was being tracked as credits (~900/2,500, comfortable) while the cap that actually bit is a **separate per-billing-cycle datapoint limit**. These full-history queries return 100k+ rows per 7-day window, so datapoints burn far faster than credits. **Track datapoints, not credits, when costing any Dune-backed backfill.**
- **Only visible because of `8928041e`.** That commit made the route log Dune's response body instead of a bare status. Without it this was three identical `execute HTTP 402` lines with no cause — the same swallow-the-error shape that cost hours earlier in this thread.
- **Failing SAFELY.** Every failed tick reports `windows_done: 0`, nothing partial written, cursors parked (`sales_ingest_state` 2025-09-03, `sales_seller_recovery_state` 2026-01-22). Both resume from exactly where they stopped whenever the cap lifts; no cleanup and no dedup risk.
- **SHIPPED (DB-only, reversible) — `window_days` 7 -> 2 on both state tables.** A hedge, not a fix: total datapoints for a full drain are fixed by row count, so this does NOT reduce the overall bill. It only lets a smaller request fit if any cycle headroom remains. If ticks keep 402'ing, the cycle is genuinely exhausted and the honest state is "paused until reset". **Revert:** set `window_days = 7` on both.
- **Trevor's call: NOT upgrading the Dune plan.** So the Dune lane is capped by design and the **free Flow-REST counterparty worker is the sustainable path** — it has no Dune dependency, runs on Cloudflare's free tier, and is unaffected (`sales_counterparty_recovered` 203,336 and climbing; ~34.5k rows/day at 120/tick every 5 min). It will keep draining the null-seller backlog regardless.
- **Watch item:** the 402 ticks log `ok=false`, so both pipelines will appear in failure sweeps until the cycle resets. That is honest reporting, but if it masks a real failure, consider suppressing via `pipeline_alert_suppression` rather than disabling the crons (disabled crons are the documented silent-kill class).

### 2026-07-20 (Cowork, interactive) — POST-SHIP CATCH: my own clamp fix REGRESSED `/insights/allday-pack-reality` (paging doubled a 26s view). Fixed forward by pushing the filter into SQL; Top Shot board verified GOOD at 1,233

Post-ship verification of `1f71a9b` found the fix worked on three boards and broke the fourth. Recording the miss in full because the lesson is general.

- **VERIFIED GOOD — `/insights/topshot-pack-market` now reads "1233 qualifying dists"** live, exactly the DB count, up from the silently-clamped 1,000. The discount/premium/most-traded rankings are now computed over the complete qualifying set. This was the headline defect and it is fixed.
- **REGRESSION I INTRODUCED — `/insights/allday-pack-reality` rendered "0 qualifying dists".** Cause: `v_allday_pack_realized_ev` costs **26.3s** per read (measured: it GroupAggregates **2.8M `pack_rips` rows**; 902,747 shared hits + 109,549 reads). At 1,559 qualifying rows my `fetchAllPaged` issued **TWO** such reads instead of one — ~52s — and the build-time prerender took the error path and rendered the empty state.
- **The comparison that isolates it:** `v_topshot_pack_market` costs **837ms**, so its two pages (1,233 rows) total ~1.7s and rendered fine. Same code change, 30x different view cost, opposite outcome. **Paging is not free — it multiplies the cost of the underlying query by the page count. Measure the view before paginating it.**
- **FIXED FORWARD, not reverted** — pushed the page's own `priced` predicate into SQL (`.gt("pack_price", 0)` + `.not("modeled_gross_ev","is",null)`). That cuts **1,559 -> 302 rows**, which fits in ONE page, halving the work back to the pre-change cost while still eliminating truncation. The JS `priced` filter is byte-identical, so the rendered buckets and `qualifying` count are unchanged by construction — this is strictly better than both the old truncating `.limit(1000)` and my two-page version. Applied to the page AND `/api/public/insights/allday-pack-reality` so they cannot disagree.
- **Durable rule to carry: before converting a `.limit()` to paging, EXPLAIN the source.** If it is an expensive aggregate view, either push filters down so it stays one page, or leave the limit and disclose the truncation — do not silently double a 26s query. A cheap-view assumption is what made this a regression rather than a clean fix.

(2) Filter accepts EITHER identifier and TRIMs the event value: `new Set([dbSlug, collection])` membership on `(e.collection_slug ?? '').trim()` — mirrors the proven sibling `WalletPacksView` (`=== dbSlug || === collection`), defends stray whitespace/form drift. **Kept the filter, per the report — both accepted values are THIS collection's own identifiers, so no other collection's sales can leak onto the board.** The `!dbSlug` → show-all fallback (documented) is preserved for a genuinely unresolvable collection. ### 2026-07-19 (Cowork, interactive) — LIVE public boards were serving TRUNCATED data: two `/insights` surfaces silently dropped 233 and 559 rows before ranking. Fixed at 8 call sites behind one shared helper (`lib/supabase-paginate.ts`), +7 tests

Swept the PostgREST 1,000-row clamp class that produced the Panini `.limit(3000)` bug earlier today. It was not a one-off — it is live and wrong on public surfaces right now.

- **`/insights/topshot-pack-market` — ACTIVELY WRONG. 1,233 rows qualify (`n_sales >= 5`); `.limit(1000)` served 1,000.** ~233 dropped.
- **`/insights/allday-pack-reality` — ACTIVELY WRONG, worst of the set. 1,559 qualify; ~559 dropped.**
- **The severity is the ranking, not the row count.** Neither query carried an `.order()`, so PostgREST returned an ARBITRARY 1,000 — and both pages then compute "biggest discount / biggest premium / most traded" (and over/under/on-model) top-15 lists **in JS over that truncated set**. So a genuine top-15 discount pack could be absent from a public deal-finding board, nondeterministically. That is a credibility defect, not a cosmetic one.
- **`/insights/allday-pack-market` — 796 qualify, ~20% headroom.** Not truncating yet, same unordered shape, fixed alongside.
- **`/insights/market` (The RPC Index) — `.limit(2000)`, silently 1,000.** 686 rows today against a ~847 ceiling (121 days x <=7 tiers) so it is NOT truncating — but it sorts `d ASCENDING`, so the first overflow would drop **the NEWEST days off a market-index chart** while keeping stale history. Worst-possible failure mode for that surface; fixed pre-emptively.
- **The JSON APIs had the identical bug** — `/api/public/insights/{topshot-pack-market,allday-pack-market,allday-pack-reality,market}` all repeated it, so page and API would have disagreed after a page-only fix. **8 call sites fixed total** (4 server pages + 4 routes).
- **SHIPPED — `lib/supabase-paginate.ts` / `fetchAllPaged()`.** This class has now caused live wrong numbers **five separate times** (lock-roi, market, sets-db, market-pulse's 4x undercount, Panini squeeze), so the workaround now lives in one reviewed place instead of being re-derived per call site. Pages `.range()`, caps `pageSize` at 1,000 (a larger request would be clamped and then read as a false short-page = silent truncation *inside* the fix), terminates only on a short page, and returns an explicit **`truncated`** flag for maxPages/page-error so a partial set can never be mistaken for a complete one. Two rules documented in the header: the query MUST carry a deterministic `.order()` (Postgres gives no stable order without one, so paging an unordered query can duplicate rows on one page and drop them from another), and callers must check `truncated`.
- **Added `.order("dist_id")` to the three pack boards** — previously absent, which is what made the truncation nondeterministic *and* would have made naive pagination unsafe.
- **VERIFIED:** `tsc --noEmit` clean (it caught a real defect mid-change — `fetchAllPaged` narrows `error` to `string`, but four call sites still did `error.message`); **23/23 green** across the five public-insights route suites plus **6 new tests** for the helper (over-cap paging, short-page stop, exact-multiple probe page, pageSize clamp, page-error keeps partial rows + flags truncated, maxPages flags truncated). Fixture builders gained `.order()`/`.range()`.
- **Deliberately NOT changed:** `/api/public/insights/pack-reality`'s `.limit(1000)` — measured 184 rows, genuinely under the cap; and the many `.limit(100..200)` "top N" limits on other insights pages, which are intentional.
- **KNOWN REMAINING (not fixed, flagged): ingest/admin routes carry clamped limits too** — `offers-sweep .limit(10000)` (x2), `badge-sync .limit(10000)`, `pinnacle-metadata-backfill .limit(5000/8000/10000)`, `flowty-analytics .limit(100000)`. These are **throughput** bugs, not correctness ones (each tick processes 1,000 instead of the intended N, so sweeps drain ~10x slower than designed) and they touch ingest paths, so they want a deliberate owner session rather than a blind sweep. QUEUED: CLAMPED-LIMITS-INGEST-THROUGHPUT.
- **REVERT:** `git revert <code sha>` — restores the prior `.limit()` calls; `lib/supabase-paginate.ts` and its test are additive and can stay.

### 2026-07-19 (Claude Code, interactive) — LOCK FRESHNESS, Trevor's call = "fix on-demand refresh": the TS on-view refresh now converges the VIEWED wallet (stalest-first + stamps lock_checked_at); the `<500` guard that hid overstated whales is gone

Trevor picked the on-demand-refresh path over batch throughput / display-caveat / stop (the batch is ~24× short of a 7-day promise, so trustworthiness has to come from the wallet a user actually views, not from grinding 1.6M rows). Two real bugs found and fixed in the existing `cache-refresh?refreshLocked=1` path.

- **BUG 1 (the one that perpetuated the overstatement) — the trigger's `<500` guard was backwards.** `collection/page.tsx` fired the on-view lock refresh only `if (lockedCount < 500)` — i.e. it SKIPPED exactly the wallets already showing many (stale) locks. So an overstated whale (the ref wallet's ~13k months-old `is_locked=true`) never self-corrected on view. **Fixed:** fire on every Top Shot collection view; the server early-outs cheaply when nothing is stale (below), so this is safe.
- **BUG 2 (why it couldn't converge) — the backfill re-checked the same first-500 forever and never stamped freshness.** The old body took `allCachedIds.slice(0,500)` in on-chain order (so a whale's moments 501+ were never refreshed) and wrote **only `is_locked`, never `lock_checked_at`**. **Fixed (`app/api/cache-refresh/route.ts` step 7):** one query pulls the **stalest** held moments (`lock_checked_at` ASC NULLS FIRST, 7-day cutoff, cap 500) + the exact stale count; refreshes those via GQL `isLocked`; **stamps `lock_checked_at=now()` alongside `is_locked`** so it's a real freshness check and the batch stops re-selecting it. Each view advances the wallet's freshness frontier ⇒ a normal wallet is fully fresh in one view, a whale converges over a few. A fresh wallet costs **one indexed count query, no GQL** (early-out when `staleTotal=0`). GQL miss → row left stale + unstamped so a later view retries (never stamps an unverified value). Service-role client, so the `lock_checked_at` write is permitted.
- **Net effect:** the lock count on the wallet a user is looking at becomes trustworthy without any caveat and without the impossible 7-day batch chase; the batch (now reliable after the 120s-timeout fix in the entry two above) stays background best-effort for un-viewed wallets. Tests: `__tests__/api-cache-refresh-deep.test.ts` updated — stalest-first refresh now asserts BOTH `is_locked` + a `lock_checked_at` stamp, plus a new fresh-wallet early-out case (no GQL, no write); **7/7 green**, `tsc` clean on the changed files (only pre-existing `.next/types` phantom errors for already-deleted routes). **Revert:** `git revert <code sha>`.
- **SCOPE CAVEAT (verified live) — on-demand refresh fires for SIGNED-IN viewers only.** Deploy `d01e9343` READY on prod (www alias). Driving `/api/cache-refresh?wallet=<ref>&refreshLocked=1` **unauthenticated** returns the login shell — the route is `proxy.ts`-gated (it's a wmc WRITE path), so the client trigger only reaches it when the browser carries an auth cookie. This is a PRE-EXISTING posture (the feature was always signed-in-only; my change didn't alter it) and it's the right audience — a signed-in owner viewing their own portfolio is exactly the complaint's context (the ref wallet: 14,948 TS rows, all stale >7d, oldest 2026-04-13). **Anon viewers do NOT trigger it and rely on the batch.** Extending it to anon would mean adding a write route to the anon allowlist in `proxy.ts` (off-limits auth/lockdown file) — deliberately NOT done; flagged for Trevor if anon-viewer lock freshness is wanted. End-to-end authed prod drive not run here (no secret in-session); logic proven by the 7/7 tests + the READY deploy, DB timeout fix separately verified live (00:38Z tick ok=true).
- **STILL open (Trevor, not this fix):** the batch's 7-day promise remains structurally unmeetable — `MAX_AGE_DAYS=7` stays a background target, not a guarantee. On-demand now covers the display-trust need, so a "locks as of <date>" caveat is unnecessary for viewed wallets. Steps 2 (BATCH_LIMIT raise — unsafe until the selection read is made cheap) and 3 (denser cron string — actively harmful now, would add :08/:38-style collisions → more 60s selection-read timeouts) remain **not recommended** and were NOT shipped.

Actioned the LOCK FRESHNESS runbook. **Advances the 2026-07-19 Cowork "ceiling is cron-job.org's 30s cap" entry below** with a server-side measurement it didn't have. Step 1 (202-wrap, `76b6c2e0`) and the 2-collection scope (`9f3b1ea5`) are already shipped and live.

So the Cowork entry's fix order ("202-wrap THEN raise BATCH_LIMIT to ~800") is **still unsafe at step 2**: the read is O(limit × 480 hot wallets) and measured **5.8s warm @200 → 24.5s warm @800** (single call, quiet window). Under the contention that already kills it at 200/60s, an 800-limit read fails nearly every tick. The "17–25s inside 270s headroom" is the **Cadence leg** (7× headroom, 13–22 wallets/tick) — the *read* is the bottleneck and it is NOT governed by the soft deadline. **Do not raise BATCH_LIMIT until the read is reliable + cheap.**

Stops the 60s premature kill so the after()-context read (270s soft deadline / 300s maxDuration) completes and delivers its 200 rows instead of discarding 60s of IOPS. Fn is non-inlined (has `SET search_path`), so proconfig applies (precedent: `raise_edition_offers_from_chain` 600s). **~2× delivered throughput at the current limit, ZERO increase in peak per-tick load** — the disciplined "one lever, then watch a day" move under the IOPS caution, and the true completion of Step 1 (raising throughput first would have deepened the silent failure). **Revert:** `ALTER FUNCTION public.get_lock_check_batch(text,integer,integer) RESET statement_timeout;` **Target metric:** lock-check-batch ok=false rate ~50% → ~0 over the next day; rows_written>0 on ≥90% of ticks.
